title: Stepped run silently collapses to ONE atomic dispatch when every break phase is trimmed — per-group settings and group sequencing are discarded
impact: A saved run profile such as "charge to 100%, then bedrooms on quiet, then kitchen on max" runs as a single batch. On Roborock the per-phase `global_pre_calls` (fan / mop-intensity select, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:132-153,366) then fire ONCE max-wins over the merged room set, so the bedrooms are physically vacuumed at max suction instead of quiet — and a mixed vacuum/mop profile falls into the `mixed_mode_water_policy: safest` branch and under-mops instead of running the two groups at their own water levels. Where the same room appears in two groups ("vacuum the kitchen, then mop the kitchen" — the case _build_steps_phases exists to support) the room is dispatched ONCE with the last group's settings, so the vacuum pass never happens. No error is shown; preflight reports the run as ready.

title: _match_profile_from_fields is structurally brand-blind and rewrites every Roborock room's profile_name to "custom" on every start
impact: A Roborock room the user set to "Vacuum Only Quick" is reported as a Custom profile everywhere the start plan feeds: `queue_state["queue_rooms"][].profile_name` (queue_engine.py:127), `resolved_rooms[].selected_profile_name` (queue_engine.py:319), the frozen active-job record, and the card's profile label (`_settings_profile_display` flips `is_custom` True, run_plan.py:125). Dispatched settings are unaffected (the room's own stored fields still win in the resolver), so this is a wrong user-visible label and a wrong job/learning record with no error shown — and the seam is structurally unable to be fixed without a signature change, since the function has no way to reach the brand catalog.

title: A run profile whose first step is a zone is permanently unstartable and reports "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid"
impact: A saved run profile that begins with a saved-zone step (e.g. "spot-clean under the table, then clean the downstairs") can never be started. The user gets "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." — a message about a corrupt payload, pointing at nothing they can fix. The feature is dead for that authoring order with no diagnostic naming the zone step.

title: normalize_room_profile re-injects the Eufy literal "Quick" for clean_intensity, defeating Roborock's deliberate omission of the axis
impact: Applying a room profile to a Roborock room stamps `clean_intensity="Quick"` — a value from a brand whose intensity option list (`clean_intensity_options`) is deliberately absent (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:241). The card's intensity chip row has no matching option to select, so the room shows a value the user cannot change or clear, and the "one source, no second vocabulary" contract that rooms/room_defaults.py was written to establish is broken on the second write path. Wire-inert today (Roborock's GenericRoomIdsEngine discards the Eufy-shaped payload, dispatch_engines.py:188-197), so no wrong physical action.

title: A map rebuild silently auto-enables AND auto-approves rooms that never existed before, adding them to the clean queue unseen
impact: After a Rebuild Map, any segment that appeared since the last rebuild — a room the user renamed into existence in the vendor app, or on Eufy a phantom segment the CV segmenter split off — is cleaned on the next Start without ever appearing in the setup flow or the drift report. The user pressed Start expecting their configured room set and the robot cleans an extra room. With `preserve_existing_settings=False` the same two defaults apply to EVERY room, so the user's enable/disable selections are wholesale replaced by "everything on".

title: apply_capability_gate and _protected_room_config hardcode Eufy display literals for the framework's 'no water' / 'default path' concepts
impact: No wrong physical action on either shipped brand. Structural: the framework's "no water" concept is expressed as the string `"Off"` in the one function every brand's payload must pass through, so a brand whose no-water value is not case-insensitively "off" (an integer 0, "none", "dry") receives an unmappable value it must special-case in its own value_map — and the `resolved_rooms` record persisted to learning/history carries Eufy casing for every brand.

title: build_room_clean_payload treats an empty queue_room_ids as "no filter" rather than "no rooms", so a cleared queue yields a payload containing every enabled room
impact: No physical wrong action today: the DISPATCHED payload comes from `_build_effective_start_plan` -> `_build_dispatch_phases`, whose `queue_room_ids` is derived fresh from `effective_rooms` in the same call (run_plan.py:1320-1324, 1376), and the stored `data["payloads"]` written by `build_room_payload` is read only by `get_room_payload` (core/manager.py:2540). The user-visible effect is a preview/inspection payload listing rooms that are not queued. It is a live footgun for any future caller that passes a genuinely empty selection meaning "clean nothing".

title: Applying a built-in room profile to a Roborock room writes EUFY vocabulary onto the room; the fresh room_defaults fix covers creation only
impact: On a Roborock, choosing any built-in room profile (e.g. "Vacuum Only Deep") for a room stores an unusable capitalized suction value. The room then cleans at whatever fan speed the device happened to be left on — the user's profile choice has zero effect on suction, with no error, no warning, and no log line. The card's chip row (strict `===` against the lowercase option values) also renders no selection, so the room looks unconfigured.

title: A mop room on a granite or concrete floor resolves water_level to the empty string and that empty string is written verbatim to the wire
impact: A room the user configured to mop, on a granite or concrete floor, is dispatched to the Eufy with an empty water-level string — the robot either rejects the room_clean payload (the whole run silently fails to start) or mops with an undefined water setting. On Roborock the same empty value reaches `_run_global_pre_calls`, where `""` is not in the rank list; if it is the only room the loop hits `if best_index < 0: continue` (dispatch/manager.py:413) and the device-global mop intensity is LEFT AS-IS — potentially a HIGH level left over from a previous run, wet-mopping a room the user did not ask to be wet-mopped.

title: Zone-clean repeat cap defaults to 3 for Eufy while the framework's own room-clean cap for Eufy is 2, and the service schema has no upper bound
impact: An Eufy zone clean called with clean_times=3 (or 10) dispatches that raw value to a device the framework itself documents as capping at 2 passes. The user draws a box, presses clean, and either gets a silently rejected command (nothing happens, no error surfaced) or an out-of-range pass count. The stated per-brand ceiling enforcement is a comment, not code, on the Eufy path.

title: _write_room_field's value_map is fail-open: an unmapped canonical value is emitted raw, and the framework itself injects Eufy literals no adapter can declare a mapping for
impact: Any brand whose wire vocabulary differs from the canonical one gets un-translatable framework literals on the wire for capability-gated fields — a malformed payload the device rejects, or a wrong setting applied — and the framework prints nothing. Not reachable on Eufy (declares `value_map: None` everywhere, so the identity path is taken) or Roborock (declares no `room_fields` and discards the Eufy-shaped payload), but it is a structural seam defect: the adapter config has no way to express a mapping for a value the framework invents after the adapter's vocabulary has been consulted.

title: _protected_room_config stamps the Eufy literal "Off" into every non-mop room's water_level regardless of brand, on the path into the payload builder
impact: On a mop-settable Roborock the room editor's water chip row (strict `===` against the lowercase option values) renders nothing as selected for any vacuum-mode room, so the room reads as unconfigured. The value survives only because `_run_global_pre_calls` happens to lowercase before ranking (dispatch/manager.py:409) — a coincidence, not a contract. Any consumer that compares strictly against the brand's declared vocabulary sees an unrecognised value.

title: clean_passes_field: null omits passes in two engines but produces a None dict key in build_room_clean_payload
impact: A brand whose room-clean command carries no per-room pass count cannot express that on the `eufy_room_clean` template: instead of omitting the field it gets a `{None: 1}` entry, which fails JSON serialisation or reaches the device as a garbage key. The adapter author follows a documented contract and gets a broken payload with no validation error.

title: Strict-order per-room phases invert the live-id safety rule: an unresolvable slug dispatches the STALE stored segment id instead of being skipped
impact: On a Roborock strict-order run (user toggles 'clean in order', or ANY stepped run — run_plan.py:1363-1370 hardcodes strict_order=True for a profile containing a charge_wait/wait/zone step), if a target room's name changed or the map was re-segmented since the ids were stored, the robot is commanded to clean a segment id that now belongs to a different room. It physically cleans the WRONG ROOM. The phase watchdog then makes it worse rather than better: `_await_phase_started` (phase_runner.py:929-965) confirms only on native current_room == the phase target, which never matches, so it re-dispatches the same stale id up to `phase_timing.max_attempts` (3, adapter.py:325) — up to three wrong-room cleans — then gives up leaving `_phase_dispatch_pending` set and the run stalled.

title: _SinglePhaseMixin silently swallows strict_order and the seam cannot express refusal — while the caller hides the order advisory on the strength of the request alone
impact: A brand that path-optimizes (honors_clean_order False) but whose payload shape is list-of-dicts or positional-arrays — i.e. anything on eufy_room_clean, dreame_room_clean, or a future engine built off _SinglePhaseMixin — gets ONE batch dispatch when the user asks for strict order. The rooms are cleaned in the device's optimized order, and the standing advisory that would have told the user 'this vacuum cleans in the order saved in its own app' is suppressed because they asked for strict order. The user is told order is enforced while it silently is not. Neither shipped brand hits this today (Eufy honors order so effective_strict folds to False and the advisory is None anyway; Roborock is on the overriding engine).

title: DreameSegmentEngine's documented 'direct envelope (no command)' is unreachable — an omitted command defaults to Eufy's room_clean
impact: Whoever enables the shipped-but-unused dreame_room_clean template and follows the engine's own documentation produces a service call the device cannot execute — the clean never starts, and because `_dispatch_clean_payload` awaits `hass.services.async_call(..., blocking=True)` the failure surfaces as a raw HA service exception rather than anything that names the misconfiguration. Zero impact today (no Dreame adapter ships), but the engine is registered in `_DISPATCH_ENGINES` and therefore passes `_validate_adapter`'s template check, so it presents as ready.

title: An omitted dispatch.template silently resolves to the Eufy engine with no warning, and the claimed registration-time rejection does not exist
impact: A future brand's clean command is built in the wrong structural shape and shipped to its service. The failure mode is either a hard service error at start (best case) or a partially-parsed command the device acts on. The framework's own audibility mechanism for this exact class of silent-Eufy-fallback covers three engine seams and omits the actuation seam; per the campaign's sibling-sweep finding this is the vocabulary-by-hand-copied-comment pattern reappearing at the most consequential block.

title: Engine phase envelopes omit queue_room_ids/queue_rooms, making the run-plan group-union computation dead code and emptying queue_rooms on every phase advance
impact: No user-visible wrong result today, but both are unearned rescues rather than correct code. (a) is masked only because `included_room_ids` currently happens to equal the union of the groups' rooms — `apply_run_profile` disables every room then re-enables exactly the profile's room_group rooms (profiles/manager.py:1201-1242), and blocked rooms are already disabled out of `effective_rooms` (run_plan.py:1297-1298). Any future step type that scopes a subset of the enabled rooms silently widens the collapse to every included room. (b) is masked only by ordering: `_room_name_from_active_job` (jobs/active_job.py:619-627) scans `resolved_rooms` before `queue_rooms` and the current phase's room is always in the former, and learning/job_finalizer.py:298-300 re-reads `queue_live` when the snapshot's list is empty.

title: When NO target slug resolves live, dispatch falls back to the STALE stored ids — the exact wrong-room outcome the function exists to prevent
impact: The robot cleans rooms the user did not select — an arbitrary set of physical rooms determined by whatever the device happens to number 16/17/18 after the re-segment. The only signal is a WARNING in the log; the service returns started:true and the job UI reports the intended rooms.

title: Cancel is defeated by the phase watchdog: _cancel_in_flight is checked once, before two multi-second awaits, then the clean is dispatched unconditionally
impact: User presses Cancel Run. The robot heads for the dock, then turns around and cleans the next room. The integration has already finalized and discarded the job, so nothing tracks or will stop the run; the user must cancel again (or from the vendor app). On Eufy the same structural hole exists but the window is sub-second (no global_pre_calls, no live-id refresh).

title: A raising dispatch kills the phase watchdog task and wedges the run in 'started' forever
impact: One transient service error mid-run (robot briefly unavailable, cloud hiccup) leaves the job permanently 'started'. The completion gate never fires, so the run is never finalized, learning records nothing, and every subsequent start is blocked by the active-job check until the user manually hits Cancel Run. The only trace is an 'Task exception was never retrieved' entry in the HA log.

title: The mixed-batch water SAFETY pre-call is best-effort — if it fails the clean still dispatches and the robot wet-mops the vacuum-only rooms
impact: The robot wet-mops a room the user explicitly configured vacuum-only — on hardwood, rugs, or carpet. The user is shown a normal successful start; the only trace is a stack trace in the HA log. The failure mode is silent in exactly the case the feature was built to prevent.

title: A pre-call leaves the device in a modified state (and the stashed run steps consumed) when the clean then fails to start
impact: A failed start silently reconfigures the robot's global mop intensity and leaves it there. On a mixed-batch start that means water is now OFF for whatever the user does next from the vendor app.

title: The OFF-fallback lowercases the select's options for the membership test but then sends the lowercased string as the option value
impact: On a future brand whose select uses capitalized or numeric options, the mop-intensity pre-call silently no-ops and the run uses whatever water the device was last left on — the same physical outcome as DQ-ACT-5, reached without any transient failure.

title: Zone-clean pass count is never clamped on the Eufy branch — the clamp lives inside the device_mm branch Eufy never enters
impact: An automation / YAML / script call `eufy_vacuum.start_zone_clean` (or `clean_saved_zone`/`clean_saved_zones`) with clean_times above the device ceiling reaches the robot unmodified: the value lands in the SelectZonesClean protobuf and is sent on DPS 152. The device either rejects the whole ModeCtrlRequest — nothing is cleaned, yet dispatch_zone_clean still returns {"status": "dispatched", "clean_times": 9} and the service reports success — or performs an out-of-spec repeat count. Silent either way.

title: supports_zone_clean is honored by the card but never consulted by the actuation path
impact: A model catalog entry that declares supports_zone_clean: False — the exact 'a model that categorically cannot zone-clean had no way to say so' case the capability was added for — still gets a zone_clean/app_zoned_clean send_command dispatched at it from eufy_vacuum.start_zone_clean, clean_saved_zone(s), or a saved-zone job phase. The card hides the draw control, so the declaration looks respected while the actuator ignores it; the robot receives a command its model does not implement.

title: Per-zone SIZE bounds are enforced by coordinate-space branch, not by which bound the adapter declared — the other combination is silently ignored
impact: A brand/model that declares a bound on the axis its coordinate space does not match gets NO enforcement of a limit it explicitly declared: e.g. a device_mm brand (the natural shape for Dreame's vacuum_clean_segment sibling or any world-coordinate zone command) declaring zone_min_side_m 0.4 / zone_max_side_m 8.0 has those values silently dropped, and an out-of-range rectangle is converted and dispatched. The failure mode is the one this subsystem exists to prevent — a size the device will reject or clamp arbitrarily, sent with no refusal and no log line.

title: Eufy per-side bound check is skipped entirely when live-map dims are unreadable, while the mm branch REFUSES on the same missing input
impact: An automation-fired or saved-zone clean issued before the map source is warm sends a zone whose side is outside the device's 0.5-10 m range to the robot. The provider builds and sends the quad regardless (it validates neither side length nor area), so the firmware silently drops the command — the user sees status 'dispatched', no error, and no clean. The precise 'a zone side is too short/long' message the code was written to produce never fires.

title: zone_bounds is computed and shipped in the dashboard snapshot but has no consumer anywhere — and the card replaces the precise refusal message with a generic toast
impact: Roborock's declared ceiling is 3.05 m² (roborock/adapter.py:614) — about a 1.75 m square, smaller than many ordinary draws — so a user drawing a normal box gets a refusal on press, and the actionable text explaining WHY (with the actual and maximum m²) is thrown away in favour of a generic failure toast. The stated fix for 'the only way a user discovered an out-of-bounds box was to draw it' shipped only its backend half; the behaviour it was meant to remove is unchanged.

title: Every break/zone phase flips transit_capture_valid to False, so a stepped run's per-room learning silently degrades to an even split of the run's wall time — charge/wait dock time included
impact: Every run that uses the charge_wait / wait / zone step feature writes corrupted per-room baselines: the exact per-room area and wall-minutes that were captured are thrown away, and each room instead learns an even share of the whole run including the charging hold. Room time estimates, the water/battery estimator and the preflight 'expected minutes' inflate run after run, with no error or warning anywhere.

title: advance_active_job_phase resets completed_room_ids/completed_rooms and no code path ever refills them for a phased job, so an abnormally-ended sequenced run reports every room as missed
impact: Cancel a vac→charge→mop run (or a strict-order Roborock run) after 4 of 5 rooms are done and the 'Incomplete run' banner claims all 5 rooms were missed. Worse, the chronic-trouble counter increments miss_count for the 4 rooms that actually cleaned; after two such runs those healthy rooms are permanently flagged 'trouble' on their room tiles. The live card also shows 0-of-N rooms complete for the whole run.

title: A multi-room room_group phase is recorded as ONE room — the group's whole cleaning time, area and battery are attributed to its first room and every other room in the group vanishes from the record
impact: On a Eufy stepped run, the run review / history shows 'Kitchen — 34 min, 61 m²' (the combined figure for Kitchen AND Hallway) and shows nothing for Hallway. Any consumer of room_timings sees one room where two cleaned. If DQ-PH-1 is fixed without fixing this, that fabricated figure becomes Kitchen's learned baseline.

title: QueueEntry / PayloadItem / ActiveJobSnapshot describe a shape the module has never emitted, and disagree with build_active_job_state on the fields it does write
impact: No runtime effect — these are documentation only. But they are the first thing a reader (or a future brand adapter author) opens to learn the snapshot contract, and they describe a different system. The module comment at 19-24 admits this, which makes them knowingly-stale rather than accidentally-stale; the real contract lives implicitly in jobs/active_job.py:253-292 (_default_active_job) and is not cross-referenced.

title: advance_active_job_phase resets every per-phase pointer except _native_current_room_id, leaving a latent cross-phase carry-over that only the phases-gate currently hides
impact: None today. It is a tripwire under the phases-gate: relaxing active_job.py:937 (which is the natural fix for DQ-PH-2/DQ-PH-3, since a multi-room group phase genuinely needs intra-phase rollover) immediately activates duplicate room-finished events and phantom completions on every phase boundary.

title: water_level and carpet fan_speed use a DIFFERENT precedence than every sibling field (floor default OVERRIDES the profile), so applying a built-in mop profile immediately re-labels the room "custom"
impact: The user picks the built-in "Quick" or "Deep" mop profile for a hardwood/laminate/marble room; the save stores profile_name="custom" and the chip they just clicked deselects. Same for a plain vacuum room on low-pile carpet. Renaming a room, or changing any unrelated setting, also silently drops its profile label to "custom". The comment at manager.py:138-147 explicitly CLAIMS this asymmetry was closed by resolving the candidate under the room's floor_type — it was closed for vacuum rooms only, and the comment asserts a guard that does not cover mop rooms.

title: path_type resolves to the literal string "None" for any room backfilled by the startup migration, and that string reaches the Eufy wire payload
impact: An Eufy X10/X8 room-clean payload carries path_type:"None" instead of "wide"/"narrow" — an out-of-vocabulary enum the device did not ask for, on every run of any room that predates the path_type field. planning/run_plan.py:370 (`str(room.get("path_type","")).strip() or None`) also reads the raw room dict and produces the string 'None', so the run plan displays a path type of "None".

title: "granite" and "concrete" are user-selectable floor types with no entry in either brand's FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS, so the mop-with-no-water correction corrects to empty string
impact: A mop-mode room on a Granite or Concrete floor whose water_level is unset or "off" dispatches water_level="" — no water and no error, when the code's stated intent is to correct that exact combination. The same empty value also guarantees the room can never match a built-in profile (compounding PP-RES-2), so it is permanently labelled "custom".

title: get_available_profile_names hardcodes the four Eufy built-in keys, so get_available_profiles silently drops every user-saved custom profile and would return {} for a brand with different catalog keys
impact: sensor/profile.py:63-70 passes the user's stored profiles in and publishes `profile_count` / `profiles` / `profile_labels` from the result, so the "available room profiles" sensor always reports 2 or 4 and never lists a profile the user created — an automation reading that attribute cannot see custom profiles at all. No error is raised; the count simply looks plausible.

title: normalize_room_profile injects the Eufy literal "Quick" whenever the brand's normalize_defaults omits clean_intensity, and apply_room_profile_to_config PERSISTS it into Roborock room storage
impact: A Roborock user applies any room profile and the room permanently acquires clean_intensity="Quick" — a capitalized value for an axis the Roborock adapter declares no options for (clean_intensity_options deliberately absent), so the card's strict-equality chip row renders it as an unmatched/blank chip. It is stored, survives every re-save, and re-introduces the exact Eufy vocabulary that rooms/room_defaults.py + models/models.py:208 were changed hours ago to eliminate.

title: A room pointing at a deleted or renamed custom profile silently resolves to the default profile — the UI reports a profile the room is not running
impact: After deleting or renaming a custom room profile, every room that used it shows "Vacuum Only Quick" in the room editor and the run plan while actually running the deleted profile's suction/water/passes. The room editor's chip row and its profile label disagree, with no error and no orphan warning; there is no way for the user to tell the reference is broken.

title: resolve_profile_catalog's `or` fallbacks mean a brand cannot declare an intentionally EMPTY block — it silently inherits Eufy's
impact: No shipped brand hits this today (both declare non-empty blocks), but it is a structural seam a third brand categorically cannot express — the framework's own extension point silently substitutes Eufy vocabulary for a deliberate declaration, which is the exact class of defect the adapter seam exists to prevent.

title: Dead branch in resolve_profile_name_for_constraints, and the carpet downgrade only knows the four framework built-in names
impact: Dead code that reads as a live guard (a future edit to the alias table would silently change which branch fires). The custom-profile gap is display-only inconsistency today, because clean_mode is taken from the room regardless (see PP-RES-1) — but it means the label is downgraded for built-ins and not for custom profiles, so the same physical situation is described two different ways.

title: apply_room_profile_to_config's `catalog` brand-safety parameter is structurally unreachable on every production call — the guard exists, the test passes, and the code path can never take it
impact: On a Roborock, applying ANY room profile from the card writes Eufy suction vocabulary ("Standard"/"Max") into the room. At dispatch, jobs/active_job.py:1385-1393 filters the per-room live fan call against `fan_speed_options` — `if valid and str(wire_value) not in valid: continue` — so the call is silently dropped and the room is cleaned at whatever suction the device happened to be left on. No error, no log at the user's level; the card's strict-equality chip row shows nothing selected. The user explicitly selected a profile and the suction it names is never applied.

title: normalize_room_profile's third-level literals are the one fallback a brand CANNOT override — the more deliberately a brand omits an axis, the more certainly it gets the Eufy literal for it
impact: Two live effects. (1) Profile matching never converges on Roborock: `_match_profile_from_fields` (manager.py:157-171) resolves each candidate from a bare `{"profile_name": name}` — which has no `clean_intensity` key, so the profile's injected "Quick" wins — and compares it against a wizard-created Roborock room that honestly stores `clean_intensity=""` (rooms/room_manager.py:103, `_default("clean_intensity", "")`, since the Roborock profile omits it). "" != "quick", so every Roborock room's `profile_name` is rewritten to "custom" on every save — and this cause is INDEPENDENT of DQ-Q-2's missing vacuum_entity_id, so fixing the brand-blindness alone will not fix it. (2) It blocks the obvious fix for PP-CAP-1/DQ-PAY-1: threading the catalog into `get_room_profiles()` makes `apply_room_profile` hand a Roborock built-in (no clean_intensity) to `apply_room_profile_to_config`, which then back-fills "Quick" via this same line and PERSISTS the Eufy literal onto the room — turning a resolution-time artefact into stored data.

title: clean_intensity has no capability flag and reaches the Eufy wire on devices whose capability detection just concluded the intensity axis is absent
impact: On a Eufy model outside the x10/x8 families (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:226, `"supports_path_control": model_family in {"x10", "x8"}`) with no cleaning-intensity entity, the framework has determined the device has no intensity axis, suppresses path_type from the payload — and still sends `clean_intensity: "Quick"` (or "Deep") in every room dict of the room_clean command. The device either ignores an unsupported key or rejects the command; either way the framework's own capability contract is violated silently, and a brand with no intensity axis has no capability-level way to opt out (its only escape is the wire-rename map, `room_fields["clean_intensity"]["field_name"] = None`, which is a transport concern being used as a capability one).

title: get_available_profile_names hardcodes the four Eufy catalog KEYS and takes no catalog — get_available_profiles merges every user-created profile in and then filters all of them back out
impact: The 'Available cleaning profiles' diagnostic sensor (sensor/profile.py:63-70) reads its own custom-profile store, passes it in, and reports a count that can only ever be 2 or 4 — a user with five saved custom room profiles sees '4' and finds none of them in `extra_state_attributes["profiles"]` / `profile_labels`. For brand 3, the same call returns `{}` and the sensor reports '0 profiles available' for a fully-configured vacuum.

title: apply_capability_gate hardcodes the Eufy literal "Off" in three places for the framework's own 'no water' concept
impact: Contained today. `dispatch/manager.py:409` ranks with `str(room.get(field) or "").strip().lower()`, so the mop-intensity pre-call on a settable-mop Roborock still resolves "Off"→"off" correctly; and queue_engine.py:303 skips the water field entirely for vacuum-mode rooms, so it never reaches the wire. What it does corrupt is `resolved_rooms["water_level"]` (queue_engine.py:328) — the record learning, run history and the card's run summary read — where a Roborock run shows a water value that is not in the brand's own option list. It is also a live trap for the next brand: `active_job.py:1392` filters per-room live settings with a strict `str(wire_value) not in valid`, so the moment any adapter puts water_level in `per_room_live_settings`, this literal is silently dropped exactly as fan_speed is in PP-CAP-1.

title: resolve_profile_catalog uses `or` for every key, so a brand that explicitly declares an EMPTY block silently gets Eufy's
impact: No shipped brand declares an empty sub-block, so nothing is broken today. A brand-3 author who writes `"floor_type_water_defaults": {}` meaning 'this device has no water, do not apply surface defaults' gets Eufy's Low/Medium/Off table applied to its rooms with no warning, and the only diagnosis is reading resolve_profile_catalog.

title: apply_room_profile writes Eufy vocabulary onto Roborock rooms — the catalog it resolves is inert
impact: On Roborock, selecting any room profile from the card silently poisons the room. `jobs/active_job.py:1385-1393` filters `per_room_live_settings` values against `fan_speed_options` = {gentle,quiet,balanced,turbo,max} with a strict `str(wire_value) not in valid` — 'Max' and 'Standard' both fail, so the `vacuum.set_fan_speed` call for that room is DROPPED entirely and the robot cleans it at whatever suction was last on the device. The room editor's chip rows compare with strict `===` (src/renderers/room-editor.js:250, :275), so suction and water render with nothing selected right after the user picked a profile. A meaningless `clean_intensity` is stamped onto a brand that deliberately has no intensity axis.

title: Applying a mop room profile instantly rewrites the room's profile_name to "custom" — the profile the user just picked does not stay selected
impact: On Eufy — the primary shipped brand — a user taps the "Deep" or "Quick" mop profile chip on any hardwood, laminate, marble, granite or concrete room and the card immediately re-renders with the "Custom" chip highlighted instead (src/renderers/room-editor.js:144-148, :158). No error, no toast. The settings applied are correct; only the association is destroyed, so the room can never be recognised as being on a preset and the same tap fails every time. The same `_match_profile_from_fields` stamp runs in planning/run_plan.py:1310-1311, so the run-plan preview also reports "custom" for those rooms.

title: rename_room_profile changes the store key and silently orphans every room referencing it — no migration, no reference check, no warning
impact: A user renames a custom room profile from "Kitchen Deep" to "Kitchen Deep Clean" and every OTHER room using it loses its profile association. Those rooms' chip rows show nothing selected (strict `===` against the library keys, src/renderers/room-editor.js:158), `get_effective_room_details` reports `selected_profile_name='vacuum_quick'` / `resolved_profile_label='Vacuum Only Quick'` — a profile the user never chose — and the next field edit on any of them snaps `profile_name` to "custom" via `_finalize_room_update`, making the loss permanent. No error is shown at any point; the service returns `{"renamed": True}`.

title: get_effective_room_details resolves with no catalog — Eufy floor defaults override a Roborock carpet room, and "Quick" is injected where the brand has no intensity axis
impact: `get_effective_room_details` is what the room entity publishes as attributes (room_entities.py:178) and what `save_room_profile_from_room` persists (manager.py:430-464). So the divergence is not display-only: saving a Roborock carpet room as a profile bakes Eufy 'Max'/'Off' plus a phantom 'Quick' into stored data, which `apply_room_profile` then writes back onto real rooms, feeding PP-CRUD-1's silently-dropped set_fan_speed. On the entity, the reported fan_speed for a Roborock carpet room disagrees with what dispatch actually sends (queue_engine resolves the same room WITH the catalog and gets 'max').

title: save-a-room-as-a-profile is not a round trip: path_type is discarded and re-derived from clean_intensity
impact: path_type is a real wire field on Eufy X10/X8 (`"path_type": {"field_name": "path_type"}`, adapters/eufy/adapter.py:581, gated by supports_path_control at :226). So on an X10: set a room to the Narrow cleaning path, save it as a custom profile, apply that profile back — the robot now cleans that room in the WIDE path. The user's saved profile does not reproduce the room it was saved from, and nothing reports the change.

title: Protected-profile-name set is frozen from the Eufy in-code catalog, so a brand's own built-ins are unprotected and can be shadowed by a user profile
impact: For a future adapter with its own profile vocabulary, a user 'saving' a profile under one of the brand's built-in names would silently and permanently replace that built-in for dispatch while the card still labels it protected/undeletable — the built-in cannot be restored through any service.

title: _protected_room_config is the only writer in the finalize pipeline and it stamps the Eufy literal "Off" onto every non-mop room, on both brands
impact: On Roborock every vacuum-mode room's stored water_level is 'Off' where the brand's declared value is 'off'. Dispatch is safe (dispatch/manager.py:390 lowercases before rank lookup) and profile matching is safe (`_normalize_profile_match_value` folds 'off', manager.py:127-128), so the impact is confined to the card: the water chip row compares with strict `===` (src/renderers/room-editor.js:275) and renders nothing selected. Storage-level vocabulary pollution that any future consumer comparing strictly will inherit.

title: Generated profile ids are local-time second-resolution and saves have no exists check, so two saves in one second silently destroy the first
impact: A user's saved room profile or run profile is destroyed with no error and no way to recover it. Reachable from an automation or script that saves several profiles in a loop; not reachable from the card's own save flow, which derives a de-duplicated `custom_<slug>` key client-side (src/state/room-profiles.js:112-122). The DST fall-back hour makes a same-key collision possible an hour apart.

title: overwrite_run_profile unconditionally destroys a saved profile's step sequence; save_run_profile preserves it — same "snapshot the current run" contract, opposite behaviour
impact: A saved run "Downstairs, wait 30 min for the floor to dry, then Upstairs" (or any rooms->zone / multi-group run) loses its entire sequence the first time the user opens its editor and saves — e.g. just to fix a typo in the name or toggle the dashboard button. run_profile_steps() then back-fills a single room_group, so the next press of that profile runs every room in one flat batch: the wait never happens, and a zone step (real cleaning work) is never dispatched at all. Purely on the backend, an integrator who calls overwrite_run_profile to rename a profile gets the same silent flattening.

title: A stepped run profile silently discards the per-room settings it was saved with; apply falls back to whatever the rooms happen to be set to now
impact: User composes "Nightly": Kitchen + Bath on mop/High water, charge to 90%, then Bedrooms on vacuum — and saves it. Days later they switch the Kitchen to vacuum-only for a quick pass. Pressing the "Run Nightly" button (or calling apply_run_profile / start_run_profile) restores the right rooms in the right order with the charge break, but runs the Kitchen on VACUUM. No error, no warning, and the card shows the new settings as if they were the profile's. services.yaml:1476 advertises apply_run_profile as "Apply a saved run profile back onto room selection, order, and per-room settings" — the third promise is not kept for exactly the profiles that need it most.

title: start_run_profile mutates and persists every room's selection and settings BEFORE the start is allowed, and never reverts when the start refuses
impact: The user has a hand-built queue selected (say three rooms with tuned fan/water) and presses a saved-run-profile dashboard button while the vacuum is still finishing a job, or while enough rooms are path-blocked to trigger the reduced-run confirmation. Nothing starts, the button reports nothing at all (its return value is discarded), and their queue is gone: every room deselected, the profile's rooms selected instead, and those rooms' per-room settings overwritten with the profile's — saved to disk. There is no undo. For the confirmation flow specifically, the user is being asked "are you sure?" about a run whose side effects have already been applied and persisted, so answering "no" is not a no-op.

title: apply_run_profile leaves no backend record that the applied profile is stepped, so a plain Start runs it flat — or inherits the map's unrelated leftover breaks
impact: User presses "Apply" on a stepped profile, walks away, comes back to a reloaded dashboard (or starts it from a second tab / a phone), presses Start — and the run silently loses its structure: the charge-to-90% break never happens so the robot dies mid-run, a wait step is skipped, and a zone step is never cleaned at all. Same for any automation that does `apply_run_profile` then `start_cleaning`, which the service descriptions give no reason to think is wrong. Worse, if the map still carries queue_breaks from an earlier composition, the charge break lands after an arbitrary room of the profile's run.

title: Run-profile ids are generated at one-second resolution and assigned without a collision check, so two saves in the same second silently overwrite each other
impact: A script or automation that saves two run profiles back to back ("Quick" then "Deep" for the same map) ends up with one — the first is destroyed with no error, and the response even hands back the colliding id as if it were new. Under a DST fall-back the same second recurs an hour later, which can also collide a new save with an existing profile saved a year ago at that timestamp.

title: normalize_run_profile_steps passes arbitrary per-room fields through untouched, and the run-plan overlay treats them as authoritative settings — the one dispatch path that skips _protected_room_config
impact: A user captures a room group while a room is hardwood and set to mop, then later marks that room as carpet (rug moved in). Every other path in the system now refuses to mop it — the card shows Vacuum, and apply_run_profile rewrites the stored room to Vacuum — but the stepped run still dispatches clean_mode=mop for that room, dragging the mop plate across carpet. The UI never shows the value the robot was actually sent. The same overlay lets a hand-written set_run_profile_steps call inject any per-room setting straight into a dispatch payload without the protection pass.

title: Applying a profile whose rooms no longer exist silently deselects and persists every room on the map, and reports the failure as "profile_not_found"
impact: After a map rebuild or re-segmentation renumbers rooms, pressing a saved run profile deselects every room on the map, saves that to disk, and either says nothing (apply service / card) or blames a missing profile (start). The user's whole room selection is gone and the message points them at the wrong thing. In the partial case the run starts and quietly cleans fewer rooms than the profile names, with no indication that any were dropped.

title: A multi-room_group plan with no charge/wait/zone is silently flattened to ONE atomic dispatch — the card routes it as sequenced
impact: The canonical two-pass profile — "vacuum every room, then mop the kitchen and bath" — is saved, displayed as a multi-step sequenced run in the card's stepped preview, and then executed as ONE flat clean: rooms that appear in both groups are cleaned once with the SECOND group's settings (the vacuum pass is silently deleted), rooms only in the first group keep first-group settings. No warning, no log line, and the card keeps showing the two-phase plan it thought it dispatched.

title: Any plan whose FIRST surviving phase is a zone is refused with "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid" — and a live blocker rule can push a plan into that state
impact: A saved run that worked yesterday becomes unstartable the moment a door/occupancy sensor blocks the rooms in its first group — with an error that blames a corrupt payload rather than naming the blocked room. The rest of the plan (room group B and the zone) is perfectly runnable and preflight says so. There is no way for the user to recover except editing the profile.

title: _build_steps_phases can return an empty list; `phases[0]` then raises IndexError inside get_start_status, killing the whole dashboard snapshot (Roborock)
impact: For a Roborock user, turning on a blocker (e.g. the sensor behind a "don't clean while the baby naps" rule) while a charge/wait break sits in the queue makes the integration's dashboard snapshot service raise instead of returning "All selected rooms are blocked" — the card cannot render start status or job controls at all until the rule clears. Eufy is immune: the atomic engine always returns exactly one phase, so the same state reports the intended blocked message.

title: The collapse fallback's `all_ids` is provably always [] — and the unit test manufactures the very key the real engines never emit
impact: A stepped plan whose breaks are all trimmed (leading and/or trailing) runs as one flat clean using each room's GLOBAL stored settings instead of the per-group settings the card wrote into the step — e.g. `[room_group(kitchen: vacuum), room_group(kitchen: mop), charge_wait]` cleans the kitchen once, with whatever the room's persisted settings happen to be. The dead `all_ids` also means any future fix that assumes step-order is preserved here will silently not work.

title: A user-authored leading or trailing charge/wait step is silently deleted at dispatch while the card still shows it and stamps has_charge_steps
impact: A profile the user built as "wait 30 minutes, then clean" or "charge to 95%, then clean" starts cleaning immediately, at whatever battery level the robot is sitting at; "clean, then charge to 100%" never charges. The step remains visible in the profile editor and the stepped preview, and nothing is logged, so the user has no way to learn the step is inert.

title: A stepped Roborock run enforces clean order but still tells the user the order is advisory
impact: Every stepped Roborock run with two or more rooms displays "Cleaning order shown here is advisory: this vacuum cleans rooms in the order saved in its own app (set a cleaning Sequence there to enforce it) or optimizes the path itself" — on precisely the runs where the integration IS enforcing the order room-by-room. The user is told to go configure a Sequence in the Roborock app to fix a problem that does not exist on this run.

title: _settings_profile_display hardcodes the Eufy-era built-in profile-name set and takes no vacuum_entity_id, so a brand with its own profile keys renders every room as "Custom"
impact: A future adapter that declares its own `room_profiles.builtins` keys (the block is adapter-owned and free-form) gets `is_custom = True` for every room whose profile resolves cleanly, so the pre-run plan, the water-estimate room list and the job snapshot all label real presets as "<Room> Custom <Mode>", and `is_custom_profile` — which the card uses to decide whether to show the preset chip — is wrong for every room.

title: The water-off suppression in _settings_profile_display compares against the literal "off" instead of the brand's no-water value
impact: A brand whose no-water label is "None", "Closed" or a localized string gets "Water: None" appended to every vacuum-only room's profile subtitle in the pre-run plan — cosmetic, but it is the same hand-copied-literal family as DQ-Q-4/DQ-Q-6 and it sits three lines from a helper that already resolves the question properly.

title: Mid-job path-block report walks reachability over the QUEUE only, so any queued room whose access parent is not in the queue is reported blocked — and can cancel the job
impact: Running a subset of rooms (the normal case) plus any door/motion blocker rule: the first time that blocker entity changes state mid-run, rooms that the start plan judged perfectly accessible are declared blocked. With cancel_and_event the run is cancelled and the robot returns to the dock mid-job (job data finalized as incomplete); with pause_and_event the robot stops; with the default event_only the user gets a false "N rooms blocked" event naming rooms that are fine and will still be cleaned.

title: A room stamped profile_name="custom" is re-labelled as the brand's DEFAULT preset ("Vacuum Quick") with is_custom_profile=False — proven for any mop room on hardwood
impact: A kitchen the user set to the built-in "Quick" vacuum+mop profile is shown in the run plan / payload panel as "Kitchen Vacuum Quick", flagged as a stock preset rather than custom. Any user-saved profile is worse: its store key is `user_<timestamp>` (profiles/manager.py:73), so `_profile_name_label` renders it "User 20260730t142530" instead of the label the user typed. The card mirrors the same logic (src/renderers/metrics.js `_localizedProfile`, src/state/review.js:188), so it does not correct it.

title: _settings_profile_display's "selected != resolved" custom-detection arm is dead for every name the resolver can rewrite — a carpet-downgraded mop room is still labelled "Vacuum + Mop Quick"
impact: The run-plan / payload row for a carpeted room set to a vacuum+mop preset reads "Living Room Vacuum + Mop Quick" with is_custom_profile False, while the carpet constraint has already downgraded the run to vacuum-only. Nothing in the label or the subtitle tells the user the mop was dropped.

title: granite and concrete are user-selectable floor types but are absent from every floor_type_water_defaults table, so a mop room there resolves water_level "" and is estimated as if it were dry
impact: The learning panel's "Job will use N ml" under-counts by the entire floor-application volume for those rooms, and `not_enough_clean_water` / `low_clean_water_margin` (run_plan.py:488-496) — the source of the "Not enough clean water" start warning (core/manager.py:2917-2929) — never fire. The user starts a mop run the dock cannot finish. The same empty string is also written to the wire for Eufy (queue_engine.py:303-304 writes water_level whenever supports_water and mop mode).

title: A declared water_rates table REPLACES the core table wholesale, so an adapter that omits "off" bills 4.0 ml/min for water-off mop rooms — contradicting the comment that asserts the invariant
impact: For the next adapter that declares measured rates, every mop-mode room with water turned off is billed as if it were mopping at a mid-range flow rate, inflating the job total and firing spurious "Not enough clean water" start warnings — with no signal that the number came from a fallback rather than the brand's own measurement.

title: estimate_job_water_usage drops the timeline's source/sample_count provenance, so default-guess room timings are presented as a measured "Job will use N ml"
impact: On a fresh map, or any room whose settings combination has never been run (the learned key includes clean_mode, passes, carpet, intensity and edge_mopping), the entire water figure is derived from a constant guess yet is displayed identically to a figure backed by real samples — and can block-warn the user out of a run, or fail to warn on one the dock genuinely cannot finish.

title: _room_surface_labels is fed a key that resolved_rooms never carries, so floor_type_label is always None at both display sites
impact: Every consumer that reads `floor_type_label` off a resolved-room row gets null (src/renderers/rooms.js:1607, src/state/rooms.js:696). The room list happens to survive because it reads the label from the room ENTITY attributes instead, so this is a silently dead enrichment rather than a visible blank — but any future consumer of the payload/water rows inherits the null.

title: TypedDict drift: ProfileRecord's "all always present" claim is false for the shipped Roborock catalog, and capability_gated is declared bool but written as a dict
impact: No runtime crash today — every consumer routes through `normalize_room_profile`, which `.get()`s with defaults (and re-injects "Quick", the known DQ-Q-4 leak). The impact is that the TypedDicts no longer describe the data: a reader trusting ProfileRecord will bare-deref `clean_intensity` and KeyError on Roborock, and a reader trusting `capability_gated: bool` will get a dict.

title: Tank-remaining ml is unclamped while its own percent is clamped to [0,100], and robot_internal_tank_ml is reported but never used in any calculation
impact: A shortfall renders as a self-contradictory "-450 ml (0%)". And an adapter author is required by the schema to measure `robot_internal_tank_ml` on real hardware for a value the estimator never consults.

title: Cancel is defeated ACROSS _dispatch_active_phase's awaits — the watchdog re-sends a clean after return_to_base, then the run is finalized while the robot keeps cleaning
impact: The user presses Cancel Run, the robot returns to base, then immediately drives back out and cleans the phase's room. The job record is written as cancelled/completed and the active-job slot is cleared, so the ongoing clean is untracked, unrecorded, and no longer cancellable from the card — the user has to cancel again (or use the vacuum's own app). The window overlaps exactly the moment a user is most likely to hit Cancel: the between-room dock pause.

title: Every abnormal exit from the watchdog leaves _phase_dispatch_pending set, and that state is UN-REAPABLE BY DESIGN — the run wedges in 'started' forever and blocks all future starts
impact: One transient service failure (or a zone phase whose live map isn't loaded) permanently kills the run AND every future run: the card shows a job forever 'in progress' on a parked robot, scheduled/automated starts are blocked with 'A room-clean job is currently active', and nothing recovers it — not the reaper, not the completion gate, not an HA restart's normal path. Only a manual Cancel Run clears it. On Roborock nothing surfaces the stall at all (see guards), so the user's only symptom is that cleaning silently stopped happening.

title: has_native gates on the DECLARED entity-id string (always truthy on both shipped brands), so the coarse fallback is dead code and Eufy verifies phases against a signal its own adapter declares unusable as a live current-room source
impact: On a Eufy 'vacuum -> charge to 80% -> mop' profile, the mop phase is re-dispatched up to 3 times, 90 seconds apart, while the robot is already mopping — each room_clean restarts the clean, so the robot repeatedly abandons and restarts the same rooms. After the third attempt the phase gives up and the run wedges permanently per WD-2. The verification the docstring promises ('the device is ACTUALLY cleaning the target') never happens on Eufy, and the coarse check that WOULD have worked is unreachable.

title: An HA restart during a room_group or zone phase's un-confirmed window strands the run — the re-arm covers ONLY dock phases and the comment's claimed recovery path cannot fire
impact: Restart HA (or reload the integration) while a phased run is between rooms, and the run stops dead: the robot never leaves the dock, the card shows the job still 'started' forever, no error and no log line is emitted, the reaper never fires, and every future start is blocked with 'A room-clean job is currently active' until the user manually cancels.

title: Adapter-declared phase_timing overrides are applied with no clamping — poll_seconds: 0 pins the event loop in a hot loop, max_attempts: 0 dispatches nothing and wedges the phase
impact: A future brand adapter (the seam exists precisely so a third path-optimizing brand can declare its own profile) that ships a typo or a deliberate 0 either freezes Home Assistant's event loop for every integration on the box, or silently disables phase dispatch entirely. Neither shipped adapter trips it today — Eufy declares no phase_timing block and Roborock's values are sane — so this is a seam defect, not a live bug.

title: Cancel is LOST across _dispatch_active_phase's awaits — the watchdog re-sends a clean AFTER return_to_base and the robot is left cleaning with no job record
impact: The user presses Cancel Run, the card reports the job cancelled and cleared — and the vacuum keeps cleaning the room it was told to cancel, now completely untracked. No error is surfaced anywhere; the only trace is a WARNING in the log. This is the DQ-ACT-2 lead extended to its actual consequence: the loss is not merely 'cancel is delayed', it is 'cancel is undone and the robot physically keeps running'.

title: Cancelling a sequenced run reports the WRONG missed rooms — per-phase reset of queue_room_ids/completed_room_ids feeds the incomplete-run log and trouble-rooms counters
impact: After cancelling a stepped run the card's incomplete-run banner and the EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE automation payload name the wrong rooms — under-reporting (rooms silently never retried by a `retry_missed_rooms` automation) or over-reporting (already-clean rooms re-run). The chronic trouble-rooms detector is poisoned in the same motion: case (b) records a miss against every room of the run, so rooms that clean perfectly get flagged as chronic problem rooms.

title: Cancel OPENS the completion gate it is about to wait for — it clears _phase_dispatch_pending before return_to_base, and neither the gate nor maybe_advance_phase checks _cancel_in_flight
impact: A cancelled or charge-timed-out run is recorded as a successful full completion and fed into the learning set, so a truncated run's room timings/areas/battery deltas become the learned baseline. The user gets no cancelled record, no incomplete-run banner and no EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE, and the active-job snapshot's finalize_summary is then blanked to all-None when the cancel's own `mark_active_job_finalized` runs with the rejected result.

title: Pause+resume permanently kills the phase watchdog for room_group and zone phases — resume re-arms ONLY dock phases and never restores the dispatch guard
impact: A pause+resume during a stepped run silently skips a room or an entire saved-zone step, and the run then finalizes as a normal successful completion (the guard that would have stalled it is gone). The user sees a clean 'completed' record for a run that never touched one of its rooms. The in-code comment at active_job.py:2146-2148 asserts the opposite — 'a ROOM-group phase resumes guard-free and the completion gate advances normally' — which is true only when the robot actually IS cleaning that room, exactly the condition the watchdog exists to verify.

title: Pause has NO in-flight flag at all — a dispatch already inside _dispatch_active_phase lands after vacuum.pause and the robot cleans while the record says 'paused'
impact: The card shows Paused while the vacuum keeps cleaning — the user's Pause visibly did nothing and no error is shown. The pause interval is also charged as paused time against the room's timing, so the room's learned duration is understated by however long the 'paused' robot actually ran.

title: async_cancel_active_job is re-entrant — a second cancel arriving inside the 30 s confirm window overwrites finalize_summary with all-None
impact: The post-run summary on the card goes blank after a double cancel — no outcome, no learning verdict, no sanity flags — even though the record on disk is intact. An automation listening on EVENT_JOB_FINISHED fires twice, the second time with status='completed' for a run that was cancelled.

title: A multi-room room_group phase records ONLY queue_room_ids[0] — the group's whole time/area lands on one room, the other N-1 rooms produce no timing at all, and the run is still flagged high-confidence
impact: On any Eufy stepped run (a run profile or queue with a wait / charge / zone stop, e.g. 'vacuum kitchen+hall+living, wait 30 min, mop kitchen+hall+living'), the first room of each group permanently learns ~N x its true cleaning minutes and ~N x its true area, while the other rooms never accumulate a real observation. ETAs, the water/battery plan and the area-quality gate all skew, and nothing is flagged — the record reads as a fully-captured, valid run.

title: Phase 0's timing is attributed to the whole-run queue's first room, which need not be a room of phase 0 at all
impact: The first clean of a stepped run teaches the wrong room. A mop pass on the bathroom is learned as a kitchen vacuum sample (and ingested as high-confidence — see REC-1's transit_capture_valid path), so the kitchen's estimate drifts toward a room it never cleaned and the room that actually ran learns nothing. Silent: no warning, no invalid flag, and the mismatched slug is discarded rather than checked.

title: A phased job never records a completed room, so live progress freezes on the group's first room and the stall detector fires a false 'stuck' event mid-run
impact: On an Eufy stepped run the card shows 'Cleaning <first room of the group>' and 0 of N complete for the entire group (no room ever ticks off, no EVENT_ROOM_FINISHED for automations), and roughly two thirds of the way through each group the run is reported STALLED — a stall event plus a stuck badge with bogus elapsed/expected numbers — while the robot is cleaning correctly in a later room.

title: Both sample recorders still use the `started_at and not ended_at` predicate the module itself documents as permanently true after finalize, and fan the write out to every map bucket
impact: After a run finalizes, its stored record keeps mutating: last_cleaning_time_seconds / last_cleaning_area_m2 are overwritten and counter_samples keeps growing with post-run and other-map data, with a full store save per sensor tick. On a multi-map vacuum a job that stranded as 'started' without has_observed_active_lifecycle (which is_stranded_started, job_monitor.py:357, refuses to reap) accumulates a later run's entire counter stream; if that record is later finalized by Cancel Run, learning/job_finalizer.py:554-557 reads those foreign counters as the job's own totals.

title: Every counter sample carries battery=None — last_battery_percent is read but never written by anything, so per-room battery attribution is dead on both recording paths
impact: Per-room battery drain is never observed on either brand: every completed_job record's room_timings[].battery_delta is null, so the only per-room battery figure available anywhere is the even split total_battery_used / room_count (stats_rebuilder.py:433). A room that eats twice the battery of its neighbours is indistinguishable, and the recorded field silently reads 'no data' instead of surfacing as missing.

title: Mid-job recharge NEVER ends: the recharge-end branch is unreachable dead code, so recharge_seconds_accumulated is always 0 and every recharging run is silently held from learning
impact: Any run where the robot returns to dock to recharge mid-job (the common case for large multi-room Eufy jobs) is silently excluded from learning with an `extreme_idle_wall` blocker, and its stored duration is inflated by the full charge time. The user sees runs quietly not improving their estimates, with no error. A second recharge in one run is never recorded at all.

title: The two sample recorders still use the repudiated `started_at and not ended_at` predicate and write into EVERY map bucket, so a finished or stranded job silently absorbs another run's counters
impact: On a multi-map install, a run stranded as `started` on map A (the exact condition `poll_stranded_started_job` exists for) absorbs map B's live cleaning time and area while B runs; when the stranded reaper finalizes A as `interrupted` after the 5-minute grace, that record carries map B's numbers and is Restore-able into learning by the user, poisoning map A's room baselines. Even without a strand, every finalized bucket keeps accumulating foreign counter samples and re-persisting them to .storage.

title: Cancel clears `_phase_dispatch_pending` up front, so the return-to-base dock is read as phase completion and the job advances to the next phase during the 30 s cancel window
impact: Cancelling a multi-phase run (e.g. vacuum → charge-to-X% → mop) produces a cancellation record attributed to the phase that never ran: zero completed rooms and the wrong room set / room_count, so the run-incomplete 'missed rooms' report and the learning record both describe rooms the robot never touched. No error is surfaced — the cancel reports `cancelled: True`.

title: Strand exclusion consults only task_status against a narrower vocabulary — an Eufy dock service cycle reaps a healthy mid-run job as `interrupted`
impact: A healthy Eufy vacuum+mop run parked at the dock for a service cycle is finalized as `interrupted` mid-run. `mark_active_job_finalized` sets status='completed' and clears the slot; the robot then resumes and cleans the remaining rooms with NO active job, so that work is recorded nowhere (and `maybe_handle_external_run` will treat the resumed half as an app-started run needing manual review). Worse, the reaper fires EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE listing the not-yet-cleaned rooms (pause_timeout.py:142), so a documented `retry_missed_rooms` automation dispatches a NEW clean of those rooms while the robot is still mid-run on them.

title: async_finalize_stranded_job calls the finalizer unguarded — one raising finalize kills the entire reaper tick for every vacuum, every minute, forever
impact: One stranded job whose finalize raises permanently disables BOTH reapers for EVERY managed vacuum. Paused jobs past their timeout are never cancelled, stranded runs are never recovered, and the offending job itself stays status='started' forever — which suppresses external-run capture (external_run.py:91-96) so every subsequent app-started run also goes unrecorded. Only visible as a repeating 'Task exception was never retrieved' traceback; recovery requires Dev Tools.

title: _phase_dispatch_pending is a permanent strand exclusion — a watchdog that gives up wedges the run AND blinds the reaper that exists to recover it
impact: A run whose next phase the device ignores three times (or whose dispatch raises) sits at status='started' indefinitely with both automatic recovery paths disabled. The card shows a job running forever, external-run capture stays suppressed, and the stranded reaper — the sole automatic escape — is structurally unable to see it. Only a manual Cancel Run or an HA restart clears it, and nothing tells the user that.

title: A dispatched run the device never started can never be reaped, then the NEXT run's completion signals finalize the stale slot with the wrong run's data
impact: A dispatch the robot never acted on leaves a phantom 'running' job that no automatic path can clear, and the next app-started run is silently recorded against it: wrong rooms, wrong duration, wrong start time, fed into learning as a completed run. This is exactly the FN-1 mis-attribution the stranded reaper was built to prevent, and the reaper's own arming precondition excludes the case.

title: async_finalize_stranded_job reports success regardless of the finalizer's answer — a refused finalize still marks the slot 'completed' and fires a bogus EVENT_JOB_FINISHED
impact: On an overlapping tick the user gets two EVENT_JOB_FINISHED events for one run — one carrying real data, one claiming status 'completed' with job_id None for a run that was actually interrupted and, in the None/missing_started_at case, never written to disk at all. Automations that count runs or key off the finished status double-fire and mis-report; the run's real record can be silently absent while the slot reads 'completed'.

title: The vacuum-state busy branch is unreachable for every HA-standard vacuum state — an errored or externally-cleaning robot classifies as "ready" and Start dispatches at it
impact: The card shows "Ready to start cleaning." and an enabled Start button while the robot is sitting on the floor in an error/stuck state or paused mid-run. Pressing Start passes the only start gate and dispatches a real clean command (app_segment_clean / room clean) at a robot that is faulted or already mid-run, on top of a run the framework is not tracking.

title: invalid_payload uses phase 0's room count as the whole run's room count — a saved run profile whose first step is a zone is accepted on save but can never start
impact: A user saves a run profile like "clean the hallway zone first, then the bedrooms", presses its exposed button, and gets "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." every time, with rooms visibly selected and a valid queue. Nothing names the real cause (the step ordering); the profile is permanently unstartable and the only fix is reordering steps the UI never said were order-constrained.

title: PreflightResult declares `available` with a documented contract the producer never honours, and omits two keys the producer writes
impact: Latent trap rather than live misbehaviour: nothing reads `available` today (manager.get_start_status derives the all-blocked case from included_room_count instead, core/manager.py:2834). Any future consumer that trusts the declared contract — the obvious one being a card gating the Start button on preflight.available — would treat a fully-blocked plan as runnable. The undeclared keys mean the fan-out provenance the card would need to say "quiet mode from the Bedroom rule" is invisible to anyone reading the type.

title: BlockedRoomEntry.source documents "access_graph" for graph-propagated blocks; the producer writes "access_dependency", and the wrong literal is hand-copied into an exposed sensor attribute's type
impact: The blocked-room `source` is surfaced as the `last_block_source` attribute on a per-room HA sensor. A user (or a future card branch) writing an automation template against the documented `access_graph` value silently never matches — the attribute always reads `access_dependency` or `direct_rule`. Purely a contract lie today; the trap is that the documented value looks authoritative in two places at once.

title: slugify_room_name has no uniqueness guarantee and nothing enforces one — two rooms can share a slug, and on Roborock the second one dispatches to the FIRST one's segment id
impact: A user with two rooms whose names collide under slugify (two 'Bedroom's, or 'Bed & Bath' vs 'Bed and Bath') selects room B and the robot cleans room A instead, with no warning in the log and no error in the UI. On a confirmed re-map, room B's per-room settings, access grants and rules are permanently replaced by room A's and never listed as dropped.

title: discover_rooms_for_vacuum's single-map fallback serves ANOTHER map's room list and relabels it with the REQUESTED map_id, defeating the map_id filter at both room writers
impact: On a multi-map (multi-floor) Roborock, importing or re-saving one floor writes the OTHER floor's rooms into that floor's bucket, destroying its stored per-room settings; and a live-id dispatch resolves 'bedroom' to the other floor's segment id, so the robot cleans the wrong floor's room. No error is surfaced — the map_id on every room looks correct because it was stamped from the request.

title: A room name that slugifies to empty passes discovery's only validation and is then silently deleted by plan_migration and silently un-cleanable by dispatch
impact: A room named with only punctuation loses every stored setting permanently and without any 'dropped' report the moment the user confirms a re-map, and on Roborock it can never be cleaned — it is silently skipped from every run.

title: Drift keys its history by bare device room_id across ALL maps but feeds it only the ACTIVE map's discovery, so a multi-map vacuum's inactive rooms decay toward 'removed' and colliding ids mask each other
impact: A user with an upstairs and a downstairs map is repeatedly told that the rooms on whichever floor is not currently active have been removed from the vacuum, with the wrong floor's name attached; and a room genuinely deleted on one floor is never reported because a same-numbered room on the other floor keeps resetting its counter.

title: adapters/eufy/discovery.py is a dead, divergent second implementation of get_active_map_id / discover_rooms_for_vacuum with hand-copied sentinel and key literals
impact: No user impact today (dead code), but it is a green-tested Eufy-flavoured copy of the identity functions sitting in the adapter package a future brand port would read first — reviving it re-introduces the 'null' sentinel gap and Eufy attribute-key defaults into room identity.

title: RoomRecord documents grants_access_to as 'list[str] — room slugs' but every producer and consumer stores integer room ids
impact: No current runtime defect; it is a loaded trap on the only place a developer looks up the field's namespace, in the exact subsystem where mixing the id and slug namespaces produces wrong-room behaviour.

title: Reconciliation never runs in production: no trigger, no schedule, no UI — the reviews are computed into a payload nothing reads
impact: Stored room ids stay permanently diverged from the device's live ids after any re-segment. Every id-keyed consumer (floor-type confirmations, access-graph grants, rule status, per-room settings, room history) stays bound to the wrong physical room, and the user is never told anything changed — this is the upstream cause of the campaign's DQ-DE-1 wrong-room dispatch.

title: Two rooms with the same name collapse into one identity: phantom id_changed on an unchanged map, and migrate overwrites one room's settings with the other's
impact: On Roborock the robot cleans the wrong bathroom/bedroom when the user selects one of two same-named rooms. In reconciliation, a stable map permanently reports a false identity shift, and confirming it silently replaces one room's floor type, cleaning settings and access grants with the other room's and orphans it in the access graph — stored user data destroyed with no error and no 'dropped' entry.

title: A room renamed AND renumbered in the same edit is invisible to reconciliation — and migrate then deletes its stored data as if it were a stranger
impact: The single most common real re-segment on the shipping Roborock path produces no review at all, and the affected room silently loses its floor type, profile, cleaning settings, rules and access grants — the room then behaves as an unconfigured stranger with no error shown.

title: The reachable room writer (save_managed_rooms/build_managed_rooms) carries settings by numeric id only, so a renumber stamps one room's floor type and access grants onto a different physical room
impact: After a re-segment the robot runs the wrong room's settings on the wrong physical room — carpet/mop decisions inverted (mopping a carpeted room) and reachability grants pointing at the wrong neighbours, with no error and no indication the settings moved.

title: migrate replaces the whole room map from one discovery snapshot — any room missing from that snapshot is permanently deleted, guarded only by 'the list wasn't empty'
impact: One flaky or partially-named discovery turns a confirmation about id shifts into permanent deletion of rooms' entire configuration, with no preview, no undo, and no backup — the deletion bypasses drift's deliberate 3-pass removal confirmation entirely.

title: migrate applies a plan the user never saw: it never re-checks the reviews, and rebuilds the map even when there are none
impact: The confirmation is not bound to what was shown, so a migration can silently apply a different id remap (and a different set of dropped rooms) than the one the user approved.

title: Applying a 'renamed' review orphans that room's learned baselines, while the code comment claims history follows the room regardless
impact: Renaming a room in the vendor app and confirming the resulting review silently discards that room's accumulated duration and water learning; time and consumable estimates degrade with no error, and the docstring tells a maintainer the opposite.

title: action='ignore' writes reconciliation_dismissed_at that no code ever reads — dismissed reviews resurface on every discovery
impact: Dismissal is a no-op: identical reviews are recomputed on every discovery forever, including the permanent phantom review from REC-2. A maintainer reading the docstring believes suppression exists.

title: save_managed_rooms unconditionally replaces map_bucket["rooms"] — an empty selection or an empty discovery cache silently destroys every stored room on the map
impact: Every per-room setting for the map is destroyed with no confirmation and no error: profile, clean_mode/fan_speed/water_level/passes, floor_type, order, custom color, is_dock_room, is_transition, grants_access_to (the whole access graph) and rules. The service returns status success with room_count 0. Reachable in two clicks from the shipped card: the setup room editor's Save button is never disabled on an empty selection (src/renderers/setup.js:380-385) and `enabledRoomIds` is `state.setupRoomEditorEnabledIds?.() ?? []` (src/bindings/setup.js:288), which is [] when the user unchecks all rooms or when the editor's room list failed to load. Deleting the same data through the intended path requires passing setup/protection.py's protection gate and typing the map name; this path has no gate at all.

title: build_managed_rooms matches stored rooms by numeric id while room identity is the slug — a re-save after a re-segment transplants the previous occupant's access grants, rules and dock flag onto a different physical room and erases the reconciliation evidence
impact: After any re-segment followed by the ordinary rescan-and-save, rooms silently carry the wrong configuration: the wrong room is flagged as the dock room, access grants point through rooms that are no longer adjacent (so rule-driven runs are blocked or allowed incorrectly via planning/run_plan.py:943-1005), and per-room suction/water/passes belong to a different room — with no warning and no way to recover, since the id_changed review is destroyed by the same save. The reconcile_room service and the `reconciliation` payload have NO frontend consumer at all (no reference to reconcile_room or reconciliation anywhere in src/ or dist/), so the docstring's "surfaces as a review the user confirms — never an auto-migration" (room_crud.py:58-62) describes a flow the shipped card cannot perform; the only thing that ever touches renumbered rooms is this id-keyed blind save.

title: save_managed_rooms auto-confirms floor type for every room it writes, permanently satisfying the onboarding_required start gate with the guessed value "hardwood"
impact: The gate whose entire purpose is to force the user to declare carpet vs hardwood before the first clean is satisfied by a guess, on the very first import, for rooms the user has not looked at. A carpeted room reads as user-confirmed hardwood, so the carpet/mop invariants applied at core/manager.py:2497 and the "water tank is attached, the mop will wet the carpet rooms: X" advisory (planning/run_plan.py:679-700) never fire — the robot wet-mops carpet with no warning. The card shows the room as "Hardwood", indistinguishable from a value the user chose.

title: remove_map leaves the map's saved run-profile library, queue state and onboarding state behind; re-importing the same map_id resurrects run profiles holding room ids from the deleted segmentation
impact: The user deletes a map precisely to discard its stale room identities, re-imports, and their saved run profiles are still listed showing the old room NAMES ("Kitchen, Den") while the ids underneath now address whatever rooms occupy those segment numbers after re-segmentation. Starting the profile enables and dispatches the wrong physical rooms, and additionally overwrites those rooms' fan speed, water level, passes and order with the dead room's settings. No error, no warning; the card's label actively reassures the user it is cleaning the rooms it names. On Roborock a re-segment renumbers ids, so divergence is the expected case, not the edge case. The delete flow's protection gate (setup/protection.py) reinforces the false belief by enumerating learning data and rules as things at risk and never mentioning the run-profile library.

title: A re-save resurrects a room the user explicitly rejected as a phantom — build_managed_rooms never consults rejected_rooms
impact: A phantom segment the user deliberately banished comes back as a fully approved, enabled room with entities and a place in the clean queue, and the robot is sent to clean it on the next run. The user is never told; drift still suppresses it from new_rooms, so the one surface that would have flagged a new room stays silent. Reachable via the `save_managed_rooms` service (enabled_room_ids is vol.Optional) and via a map re-import, which passes enabled_room_ids=None (setup/workflow.py:215-219).
