title: Both room writers auto-enable and auto-approve rooms the user has never seen (DQ-Q-5 extension: the live instance is save_managed_rooms, not rebuild_map)
impact: A segment that appeared since the last save — a re-segment splitting one room in two, or a stray CV artefact — is added to the map already enabled, already approved and already floor-type-confirmed by the next `save_managed_rooms` call with no enabled_room_ids. It joins the clean queue and is cleaned on the following run without the user ever having seen it or been offered the choice, and the drift 'new room' signal that exists to surface it stays quiet because is_configured is already True.

title: get_managed_rooms returns the live stored rule dicts and metadata sub-objects by reference despite copying the outer containers
impact: Any consumer that treats this response as a detached snapshot and mutates a rule entry writes straight through into persisted storage, so a change that was never meant to be saved is persisted by the next async_save. Latent today — no in-tree caller was observed mutating a returned rule — but the partial copying signals an intent to detach that the code does not deliver.

title: async_refresh_room_source returns None on success AND on every failure/skip path, and the cache carries no freshness stamp — dispatch cannot tell a fresh live snapshot from an arbitrarily old one, and rewrites the wire payload with stale segment ids while believing it re-resolved live
impact: The robot physically cleans a different room than the one selected. No error surfaces in the UI; the only trace is a WARNING line from source_refresh that the dispatch path never inspects. This is the upstream cause of audit #7's DQ-DE-1: stale ids reach the wire not only via the stored payload but via the 'live' re-resolution that was supposed to prevent it.

title: set_cached_room_source is called unconditionally on every successful service call, so a response the flatten shim does not recognise (or an empty maps list) silently REPLACES a good cache with {} — logged at DEBUG only
impact: Every room silently disappears from the setup tab, the card, and the room picker; after three passes the drift system reports the user's entire room set as removed. Any job whose targets can no longer be resolved degrades to the stored-id path (SRC-1) or to nothing. No warning or error is emitted at any point.

title: flatten_maps_response keys the cache by map NAME with last-writer-wins and no collision detection; a collapsed cache chains into room_discovery's single-map fallback and serves one map's segment ids for a different map_id
impact: In a multi-map (multi-floor) Roborock home, a map whose cache key collides vanishes from discovery, and jobs targeting it can be dispatched against the surviving map's segment ids — the robot cleans the equivalently-named room on the wrong floor. Nothing is logged at the point of loss.

title: No in-flight coalescing or lock on the refresh: triggers spawn unbounded concurrent get_maps cloud calls, and an older response landing last becomes the resident cached snapshot — including one that started before a map switch and lands after it
impact: Redundant cloud calls raise the probability of the get_maps failure that triggers SRC-1's wrong-room dispatch. When a pre-switch response wins the race, the cache holds the previous map's segment ids under the current map's key, which a later dispatch resolves as live.

title: The room-source cache is never invalidated — not on config-entry unload/reload, not on map switch, not when a vacuum is unmanaged — and it keeps hass.data[DOMAIN] alive so the unload cleanup never fires
impact: Right after a reload — the moment the user is most likely to be reconfiguring rooms — discovery and dispatch can resolve against a snapshot from before the reload with no indication of its age. Stale entries for removed/renamed vacuums persist for the life of the HA process and defeat the DOMAIN-slot cleanup.

title: Mid-run reachability is queue-scoped while preflight is graph-scoped — a run that omits the dock room reports EVERY remaining room as access_blocked and can cancel the job
impact: A perfectly valid access graph plus a normal partial run (user cleans the bedroom, not the entryway the dock sits in) turns any watched blocker entity's state change into a spurious 'path blocked' verdict on every unfinished room. With path_block_action=cancel_and_event the run is aborted mid-clean and the rooms are never cleaned; with pause_and_event the robot stops until the pause timeout. The event names no blocking room (blocked_by_room_id=None), so the user cannot diagnose it. On event_only it still fires a false EVENT_PATH_BLOCKED that user automations act on.

title: A room with no inbound edge makes the whole graph 'partial', hard-blocking every run on the map, and no shipped surface names the offending room
impact: After a map rebuild that discovers even one new room, every Start on that map is refused with 'Room access graph is partially configured. Complete it or clear all access settings to allow basic runs.' — a message that names no room. The user's only listed remedies are guesswork or wiping the whole graph, and the backend does know the answer but the card never asks for it. Users who never configured an access graph are unaffected (blank stays blank).

title: get_access_graph_health emits no verdict — the "runs are allowed" empty graph and the "every run is blocked" partial graph are indistinguishable, and the report's own remediation moves the user from the first into the second
impact: The one service documented as the access-graph diagnostic cannot answer the only question that matters — "are my runs blocked right now?". Following its single actionable instruction on a fresh map (mark a dock room) silently disables all cleaning until every other room is wired in; likewise a routine map rebuild that adds one room stops the vacuum from starting, and the health report shows only "Room X needs an inbound dependency" advisories.

title: The structural gate on every per-room edit is absolute, not a delta: one stored graph violation rejects unrelated edits (fan speed, enable, color) with "The requested access links would make the graph invalid."
impact: After a Roborock re-segment + migrate, the user can no longer change ANY room setting on that map — changing a room's fan speed or disabling a room fails with an error claiming they requested illegal access links, which they did not. The message points at the wrong feature entirely, so the actual cause (two rooms now granting access to the same segment) is undiscoverable from the error.

title: get_room_access_editor marks every unselected target unselectable when the graph is already broken elsewhere, with the contentless reason "Not selectable due to graph legality."
impact: A consumer of the documented editor service sees every link greyed out with a message that explains nothing and blames the edge being offered rather than the pre-existing violation. The user cannot tell what to fix; the actual blocker is on rooms the payload never mentions.

title: Every access-graph issue message is a hard-coded English literal and is rendered verbatim in the card on all 18 shipped locales
impact: On any non-English install the room-access modal's issue list and its save-error banner are English, including for AR/HE where they are injected into an RTL layout. This is the one place in the access feature where the user is told what is wrong, and it is the one place that bypasses i18n.

title: The per-room editor's issue list drops graph-scoped issues, so it reports a room as problem-free on a map whose graph is invalid and blocking runs
impact: The per-room diagnostic reports a clean bill of health for a room on a map where cleaning is blocked, and never surfaces the one issue ("no dock room") that is causing it. The user auditing rooms one at a time will find nothing wrong.

title: The card's access modal renders an existing edge into the dock room as "Missing Room N" — an edge that exists is displayed as a stale reference to a room that does not
impact: The editor misrepresents the stored graph: a live room is labelled missing/stale, inviting the user to delete a valid edge. Conversely they cannot re-create it, because the dock room is filtered out of the selectable list — so one accidental removal is unrecoverable through the UI.

title: Eufy in-memory map/pose source has NO vacuum identity — a second Eufy robot is served the FIRST robot's map, rooms, pose and render raster
impact: Arithmetic, robot #2 (Eufy 'Bella', map 200x260 px @ 5 cm/px) while robot #1 ('Alfred', 240x180 px) is coordinators[0]: the card for Bella renders Alfred's raster and Alfred's room bboxes. (a) ROOM TAP — src/state/map.js:975 `deviceRoomIdAtContentPct` letterboxes the tap into normalized space and returns the `number` of the smallest map_state_source bbox containing it. Tapping the region labelled 'Kitchen' at content pct (0.20,0.66) matches Alfred's room 3 bbox [0.10,0.55,0.32,0.78] -> the card dispatches room-clean for room id 3 on BELLA, whose room 3 is a different physical room. Robot cleans the wrong room, no error. (b) ZONE DRAW — the user drags a box over Alfred's raster; the card ships normalized [0.10,0.55]-[0.32,0.78] and the fork de-normalizes against BELLA's own map: side_x = 0.22*200*5/100 = 2.20 m (user saw 0.22*240*5/100 = 2.64 m), side_y = 0.23*260*5/100 = 2.99 m (user saw 0.23*180*5/100 = 2.07 m), centred at (0.21*200, 0.665*260) = (42,173) px on a map whose content is unrelated. Wrong place AND wrong size. (c) the robot dot, dock and current_room shown for Bella are Alfred's — `async_get_map_live_pose` reads the same unfiltered candidates, so the card's 2s live-pose merge does not rescue it. (d) map_overlays sensor for Bella publishes Alfred's room as its recorded state; saved-zone `area_m2`/`room_number` filing is computed against Alfred's raster.

title: Sticky last-known-good hold re-serves a frozen current_room/robot_anchor as `present: True`; the `stale` flag it sets has NO consumer, so a docked Roborock reports a phantom room for up to 6 hours
impact: Every time a Roborock docks, the map_overlays sensor (sensor/map_overlays.py:73-84, which checks only `res.get('present')` and never `stale`) keeps reporting the last room NAME as its state for up to `_STALE_MAP_TTL_SECONDS` = 6 hours. That state is the recorded value — the sensor's stated purpose is 'a clean room-over-time history' for automations/templates and the recorder — so every dock injects a 6-hour phantom occupancy of the last-cleaned room into the history. Automations templated on the room sensor fire against a room the robot left hours ago. On the card the frozen robot dot and highlighted room render as live with no badge or dimming: exactly the 'stale in the kitchen ghost' the live-pose feature was built to kill, reintroduced by the retention path and unmarked. Before the sticky-hold shipped the sensor correctly went 'unavailable' on dock.

title: The storage-path mtime cache early-return omits the `map_id` check its sibling `_commit_result` performs, so map A's geometry is returned as map B's answer with `present: True`
impact: For the window between a map switch and the fork's next store write, the card's room bboxes, the map-tap room resolution (`deviceRoomIdAtContentPct`) and the map_overlays sensor all describe the PREVIOUS floor's rooms while the backdrop shows the new one — a tap resolves to the old map's room number and dispatches a clean of the wrong room, with no error and no staleness indication. Narrower than LC-1: for Eufy this branch is only the fallback (`_refresh_eufy_map_source` is memory-primary and its `_mem_rooms_cache` is keyed by a content sha1, which IS correct), so it is reachable on installs whose fork exposes no in-memory `_map_data` (legacy builds, other forks, post-#136 attr drift) or during the startup window before the coordinator populates it.

title: The same mtime early-return skips `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result`, freezing the robot/dock/current_room/path overlays for as long as the store file is unchanged
impact: The map_overlays sensor's state (current room) and its `robot_anchor`/`dock_anchor`/`robot_heading` attributes stop advancing while the robot is cleaning — they only step forward when the fork happens to flush its Store — so the recorded room-over-time history for these installs shows the robot jumping between rooms at save-throttle granularity instead of tracking the run. Not user-visible on the card, which is rescued by the separate ~2s `get_map_live_pose` poll that `mapOverlayData()` (src/state/map.js:1055-1070) folds over the snapshot; the sensor has no such rescue because it reads only `_map_state_source_cache`.

title: `_commit_result` is blind last-writer-wins across the storage path's two executor awaits — a refresh started before a map switch can commit after a newer one
impact: Until the next tick (up to 60s, sooner if the card is polling), the snapshot and the map_overlays sensor serve the previous map's rooms/anchors under the new map — and since neither consumer compares `entry['map_id']` to the map they are rendering, nothing flags it. Self-correcting: the next stat sees the newer mtime, mismatches the committed one, and re-reads. Rated LOW because the window is one executor round-trip and the wrong state is transient, but it is a real gap ACROSS an await, not a synchronous-block false positive.

title: Live-pose room lookup projects a MEMORY-frame robot pixel through STORAGE-frame geometry (no memory fallback, no store_version guard) — feeds room attribution at 2 s
impact: listeners/pose_sampler.py:197 is the per-tick (~2 s) sampler that produces `current_room` for per-room attribution. A wrong room id here is written into the run's room timeline and into learned history: the user sees 'cleaned the Living Room for 8 minutes' when the robot was in the Kitchen, with no error anywhere. In the missing-store case the run produces no per-room attribution at all while the map renders normally, so nothing signals that attribution silently stopped.

title: zone_membership scans the entire room_outline raster with a per-cell normalize_rendered before the bbox reject, synchronously on the event loop — measured ~0.10 s per zone, ~1.0 s per dashboard read
impact: On the first card load after zones exist without a stored area_m2, the whole Home Assistant event loop stalls for roughly a second — every other integration's updates, websocket pushes and service calls freeze with it. Drawing a new zone stalls it for ~0.1 s. Nothing logs; the user just sees the UI hitch.

title: normalize_rendered CLAMPS out-of-grid pixels onto the map border instead of rejecting them, so off-grid raster cells and bad poses fold onto an edge rather than disappearing — diverging from the card's own decoder, which drops them
impact: A room whose segmentation extends past the main grid gets a tap-region and label box pinned to the map edge. A saved zone drawn against the right edge can be filed to the wrong room because off-grid cells were swept into its dominance vote. A hazard layer read in the wrong frame renders as a plausible-looking stripe glued to the map border rather than not rendering at all — the failure looks like data instead of like an error.

title: correspondences_from_mapdata's docstring claims clamped corners are skipped; _mapdata_projector silently clamps with no detection, leaving the affine round-trip check as the only guard
impact: No live mis-dispatch today. The risk is that the docstring reads as an implemented safety guard, so a future change to the projector, the trim/rotate config, or the residual tolerance would remove the only real protection without anyone noticing the claimed one was never there. Overlay-side, a no-go zone drawn past the map edge renders with its outside vertices collapsed onto the border.

title: A room's normalized bbox excludes its last pixel row/column while width_m/height_m on the same dict include it (+1) — the two size descriptors disagree by exactly one cell, and Roborock's equivalent omits the +1
impact: resolve_furnished_render ships per-room art placement transforms while the card places art inside the room's bbox and sizes to width_m/height_m — furnished art is scaled ~2.5% too large in a 2 m room and ~10% too large in a 0.5 m room, and the error grows as rooms get smaller. Room labels (src/renderers/map.js:566) and the bbox tap-target (src/state/map.js deviceRoomIdAtContentPct) are biased half a cell toward the top-left, so the last row/column of a room is not tappable.

title: zone_membership's docstring says the dominance vote counts cells 'whose centre falls inside the zone polygon'; the code tests the cell's top-left corner
impact: The >=90% floor-dominance filing of a saved zone is computed over a cell set biased by half a cell on each boundary. For the Eufy minimum 0.5 m zone (10 cells across) that is a ~5% shift in the counted set per edge, enough to flip a borderline vote and file a zone under the neighbouring room (or leave it Unassigned). Filing only — it never affects dispatch, per the docstring, which I confirmed: room_number is written to the zone record at mapping_services.py:2507 and never read by the dispatch path.

title: Eufy in-memory map/pose source has NO device selection — every vacuum gets coordinators[0]'s map
impact: With two or more Eufy robots, the second (and third...) vacuum's entire map identity is the first robot's: room numbers, room names, bboxes, the room-id raster, current_room, robot/dock anchors and the trail. `async_get_map_data_dict` hands robot B vacuum A's raster, so `zone_membership` files saved zones against the wrong home and `current_room_for_pixel` attributes B's run to A's rooms (poisoning learned per-room history). `async_get_map_render_data` renders A's floor plan on B's card. Tapping a room region on B dispatches the room NUMBER carried by A's bbox — B cleans the wrong room. Nothing logs an error; the diagnostics breadcrumb reports a confident `pose_at`/`mapdata_at`.

title: Content version hashes ONLY the room raster, but the cache it gates holds the grid geometry the fork mutates independently
impact: During and after any run in which the map grows, or across any session where Eufy re-localizes its coordinate origin (a documented behaviour of this device), the robot dot lands metres from where the robot is, the room bboxes/tap-regions are scaled against a dead grid, and `current_room` resolves to the WRONG room. Because current_room is the input to live rollover and per-room attribution, cleaning time and coverage are written into the wrong room's learned history — stored room data silently corrupted, with no error and no absent marker (the result is `present: True`, so `_commit_result`'s stale-hold logic never engages). It self-heals only when a full MapBackup frame delivers a different raster.

title: A dropped/renamed upstream geometry field degrades to a confidently WRONG map, not a loud absent one
impact: After an upstream fork schema change, room regions, current-room and the robot anchor are all displaced by a large fixed offset with no warning in the log and no `unavailable` state — the card looks live and is wrong. In the zero-rooms variant the map vanishes permanently (until HA restart or a re-map) even though the `.storage` fallback holds a perfectly good copy.

title: Room-outline offset is the exact NEGATION of the fork renderer's — overlays desync from the live backdrop whenever the outline origin differs from the map origin
impact: On any Eufy map whose room-outline origin differs from the map origin (VA's own notes record an X10 map at +105 cells), the card's room tap-regions, room labels, current-room highlight and robot dot sit displaced by twice the offset relative to the live fork camera backdrop they are drawn over — a visibly mis-registered map with no error. The VA-rendered backdrop is unaffected (it consumes VA's own `ro_dx`/`ro_dy` from `render_data_from_storage`, so it is self-consistent), which makes the defect appear and disappear with the backdrop toggle and look like a card bug.

title: Two room extractors disagree on the input coordinate frame and the dead one is the one under test
impact: No user impact today (dead code). The trap is for the next brand adapter: the extractor that LOOKS canonical (it lives in the pure module, it has the descriptive name, it is the one with unit tests) divides raw device coordinates by image dimensions, which for any parser handing back millimetres yields bboxes clamped to a corner of the map. Test coverage on the unused function also inflates confidence in the extraction layer that ships.

title: Roborock MapData lookup never binds the found map to the requested map_id — a multi-map (multi-floor) device converts drawn zones in the wrong floor's coordinate frame
impact: On a Roborock with more than one saved map (a two-storey home — the exact case the adapter's `active_map = select.{id}_selected_map` block exists for), the user draws a zone box on the upstairs map and the robot vacuums the corresponding rectangle of the downstairs map. No error, no warning: the 'refuse rather than mis-dispatch' safety gate is satisfied because it only checks that the affine reproduces the correspondences it was fitted from. The same wrong-map geometry is also committed to _map_state_source_cache under the requested map_id (map_source_coordinator.py:101), so room bboxes, tap-to-select hit-testing and the m² chips all show the other floor's rooms.

title: No device scoping anywhere in the Roborock candidate walk — on a two-vacuum Roborock account the card's rendered raster and the diagnostics drift report come from an arbitrary robot
impact: A household with two Roborock vacuums: the VA-rendered map backdrop for robot B shows robot A's floor plan, painted with robot B's room names. Because src/state/map.js gates zone drawing on `isVaRenderActive()` (canDrawZone = supportsZoneClean() && (isLiveBackdropActive() || isVaRenderActive())), the user draws a zone on that wrong floor plan; the normalized rect is then converted by get_live_mapdata_obj's (correct-robot) projector and dispatched — a wrong-area clean the refuse-gate cannot see, since the affine it validates is self-consistent. Diagnostics for robot B likewise report robot A's geometry drift, and diagnostics._self_check:169-170 reads `roborock_geometry_drift.present` as 'this vacuum's map is available', so a robot with no usable map is reported healthy.

title: roborock_result_from_candidates hard-returns on the first duck-typed MapData match, so one false positive permanently blanks the Roborock map source — and the stale-hold masks it for six hours
impact: A change in the HA core roborock integration's in-memory shape (or any provider object that happens to expose `.rooms` and `.image`) silently kills the entire Roborock map source: rooms, current room, robot/dock anchors, no-go/wall/path overlays, tap-to-select and zone drawing all stop. The user sees a normal-looking six-hour-old map with a frozen robot and no badge, then the map vanishes with reason `no_room_geometry` — while a fully valid MapData is present on the next, untried candidate root.

title: rooms_from_mapdata publishes the live segment number as the room's only identity and synthesizes the name, so after a Roborock re-map a tap on room A selects room B
impact: After the robot re-maps (an app-initiated re-scan, or the automatic re-map some models do after a large layout change), the live map's room labels and tap targets are shifted onto the wrong rooms with no visible error. The user taps the Kitchen on the card and the robot cleans the Bathroom. The map still looks right — the bboxes are correct geometry — only the identity attached to them is wrong.

title: roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates pairs a MapData and a MapContent found by two independent BFS walks with no check they are the same map, and reports present:True regardless of the verdict
impact: The on-device decode validator — the tool the notes record as having turned Roborock calibration 'from eyeball to data' — can report a bogus systematic drift that sends the maintainer hunting a flip/trim bug that does not exist, or conversely mark a device 'map available' in self_check when the geometry it validated belongs to a different robot or floor.

title: image_entity_object silently drops the only per-vacuum candidate root on any HA-internals change, while the presence gate still reports the map as present
impact: An HA core refactor of the entity-component registry (or an image platform load order change) turns the per-vacuum map lookup into an account-wide guess with no error, no warning log, and a presence gate that still says the map is available. On a single-vacuum install this happens to keep working, which is why it would ship unnoticed; on a multi-vacuum install it silently produces another robot's map (see RB-2).

title: _walk and _structure_tree can only descend objects exposing __dict__, so a slotted/C-extension node is both an undiscoverable dead end and an uninformative diagnostic
impact: When a python-roborock or HA core release moves the map behind a slotted container, the Roborock map source goes absent with reason `no_parsed_map` and a diagnostics dump that gives the maintainer nothing to tune — the failure looks like 'the vacuum has no map' rather than 'the introspector could not walk here'.

title: correspondences_from_mapdata's docstring claims clamped corners are skipped; the code feeds them into the least-squares fit, turning a rare edge case into an unexplained zone refusal
impact: If any room bbox corner projects outside the rendered image (rotation/trim edge cases), zone cleaning refuses with 'map projection failed validation' for the whole vacuum and no diagnostic points at the single bad corner — where the documented behaviour would have dropped that corner and fitted on the rest.

title: Live pose is normalized and room-looked-up against .storage geometry while the map it is drawn on is memory-PRIMARY — the one reader never repointed
impact: During the window between a map re-segmentation/expansion and the fork's next throttled store save, the card draws the robot dot and live trail in a different coordinate frame than the map underneath it, the current-room highlight lands on the wrong room, and — silently, with no error — every pose sample buffered for room attribution carries the wrong room id, so an external run's learned per-room history is written against rooms the robot never entered.

title: `stale` / `stale_since` / `stale_reason` are written by the hold path and read by nothing — the docstring's "the card dims/badges it" is false
impact: When the map source drops out transiently — the documented Roborock case is the cloud map entity going unavailable as the vacuum idles/docks, reason `no_parsed_map` — the map-overlays sensor keeps reporting the last room the robot was seen in as its live state, writing it into the recorder's room-over-time history for up to six hours, and the card keeps drawing the frozen robot/dock/trail as live. Nothing anywhere tells the user, an automation, or a template that the data is held rather than current.

title: The pose-geometry .storage read skips the `store_version` guard that every other reader of the same file applies
impact: After a fork store-schema bump, the map keeps rendering correctly from memory while the robot dot, the live trail and the current-room highlight are computed from stale-schema geometry — and the one designed signal for that condition (the `store_version_mismatch` warning) never fires, so the wrongness is undetectable from the logs.

title: The live pose carries no freshness stamp, so a frozen `_robot_pixel` is reported as `present: True` forever — and the fork's own `_last_robot_render` timestamp is ignored
impact: When the fork's map/pose channel stalls while the state channel keeps flowing, the card shows a confident live robot dot parked at a position the robot left long ago, and the pose sampler records that same wrong room every tick into the run's attribution buffer — with no staleness indicator anywhere and no way for a consumer to tell a stationary robot from a dead feed.

title: `_refresh_storage_map_source`'s mtime early-return bypasses the live-pose override entirely, re-serving the frozen pose it exists to kill
impact: On the storage backend the dashboard snapshot and the map-overlays sensor report the robot at a position and in a room it left minutes ago, with no error and no staleness marker — and the sensor's recorded room-over-time history inherits the frozen value.

title: `resolve_furnished_render` passes a stored placement transform through with no map-geometry stamp, so a re-mapped floor plan silently misaligns the art
impact: After the vacuum re-maps or expands its floor plan, the furnished digital-twin art keeps rendering at its old placement over a map that has moved and rescaled underneath it — off by metres — with nothing in the payload, the log, or the UI indicating the saved placement no longer matches the map it was aligned to.

title: An off-grid robot pixel is clamped onto the map edge and reported as a confident anchor — "off the map" is indistinguishable from "at the edge"
impact: A robot whose reported pixel falls outside the map grid is drawn pinned to the map border as if that were its real position, and the live trail accumulates that clamped point (src/state/map.js:1032 `accumulateTrail`), so a genuine "position unknown" renders as a confident wrong position instead of hiding the marker.

title: end_job has only ONE caller (successful finalize) — every cancel/abort/strand path leaves the tracker permanently stuck on the finished job's map and rooms
impact: Cancelling a run — via the cancel service, a path-blocker auto-cancel, or a paused-job timeout — silently breaks live room attribution for every subsequent run until HA restarts. src/controllers/learning-controller.js:146-176 consumes `eufy_vacuum_room_completed`, pushes `{room_id, actual_duration_minutes: duration_seconds/60}` into the completed-rooms list and calls `_reanchorTimeline()`, so the card's live ETA timeline is reanchored on room ids from a stale (possibly different-map) room set, or gets no updates at all because the rooms are already in `fired_rooms`. No error is logged and nothing in the UI indicates the tracker is stale.

title: resume_sampling is provably unreachable — _sampling_paused is a one-way latch, so all room attribution stops permanently at the first mid-job recharge
impact: As soon as a run docks for an unplanned low-battery recharge, live per-room attribution dies for the whole rest of the run: no further `eufy_vacuum_room_completed` events, no dwell accrual, and the card's ETA timeline stops reanchoring — silently, with the job still shown as running. Combined with TRK-1, if that run is later cancelled rather than completed, `end_job` never runs either and the latch survives into every subsequent job.

title: The HOLD path keeps ACCRUING dwell and movement for a room the robot has already left, inflating duration_seconds and forcing confidence to 1.0
impact: src/controllers/learning-controller.js:154-164 reads `duration_seconds`, records it as the room's `actual_duration_minutes` (620/60 = 10.3 min instead of 0.3 min), adds it to `_jobProgress.completedRoomMinutes`, and calls `_reanchorTimeline()`. Every room that precedes a transition room, a dock pass, or any window where the device's native current-room reads blank is reported with a wildly inflated dwell and a fabricated confidence of 1.0, skewing the card's live remaining-time estimate for the rest of the run. Rooms that were barely touched are reported as confidently completed.

title: The last room of every job never fires room_completed — end_job resets state without flushing the held room
impact: Every completed run is missing dwell data for its last room. The card's completed-room list and the reanchored ETA timeline are permanently short one room per job, so the run appears to end with a room still outstanding. Because the loss is systematic rather than intermittent, any learning consumer that aggregates these dwell figures under-counts the room the robot happens to finish on — typically the same room every run, given a stable queue order.

title: _norm_room_name normalises differently from slugify_room_name — it merges room identities that rooms/ keeps distinct, and lacks the NFC canonicalisation slugify was given specifically to prevent this
impact: Case (a): live dwell is attributed to the wrong room id whenever two rooms' names differ only in a separator character, and the card's reanchored timeline marks the wrong room complete. Case (b): for non-ASCII room names in a decomposed form the tracker never matches, so `_detect_current_room` returns None every tick and — per TRK-3 — the entire run's dwell is credited to whatever room matched last, or nothing is ever attributed if none ever matched. The integration ships 18 language packs, so non-ASCII room names are an expected configuration. In both cases the tracker's answer disagrees with the pose sampler's answer for the same device signal, with no error surfaced.

title: Dock-drift append rewrites the entire log file on every reading, and a failed write silently forfeits that drift event via the already-committed _last_dock_pos
impact: On an SD-card or eMMC HA install the rewrite amplification is real flash wear for a purely diagnostic log; the cost scales with how often the reported docked position jitters, which is exactly what the log exists to measure. Separately, the drift timeline the log is meant to provide can contain silent gaps and misleading dx/dy deltas after any transient write error, undermining its diagnostic purpose at the moment it matters.

title: start_job/end_job are dispatched to an executor thread on the strength of a comment describing disk I/O that start_job does not perform
impact: No user-visible failure proven: the individual dict operations are GIL-atomic and the interleaving window is a handful of bytecodes, so at worst one position sample is misrouted at job start. The real cost is that a false comment currently justifies threading loop-owned mutable state, which is the kind of claim a future change would build on — and it defeats the single-event-loop reasoning that makes the rest of this state machine analysable.

title: dock_events treats any arrival at a trigger value as a NEW dock cycle — a startup, an entity re-add, or an `unavailable` blip mid-cycle re-records the event and increments the durable counter
impact: Maintenance data drifts upward silently and permanently: dry-start / dust-empty / mop-wash counts inflate by one per HA restart or connectivity blip that lands inside a dock cycle, and the 'last washed / last dried / last emptied' timestamps shown on the Base Station tab are reset to the moment of the blip rather than the moment of the real cycle. mop_wash_count also feeds the post-job water amendment's `mop_wash_count_at_finalization`, so inflated wash counts propagate into the completed-job water actuals. No error is surfaced anywhere.

title: lifecycle registers a state listener + timer (post-job water amendment) whose unsubs are function-local and unreachable from lifecycle.remove()/async_unload_entry — the only unsub leak among the eight modules
impact: An unloaded/reloaded integration keeps a live state subscription and a pending timer for up to 180 s and rewrites a completed-job learning file after teardown. Because the leaked `_commit` reads the live water_level entity at fire time, a reload mid-window can stamp `water_amended_at` / `actual_*` water figures derived from post-teardown state onto a finished job record; the user sees no error and no indication the write came from a dead entry.

title: Per-vacuum teardown never re-registers listeners, and the documented 'a subscription to a now-deleted entity is inert' invariant is false — discovery keeps running passes for the deleted vacuum and re-creates its setup_progress bucket
impact: After deleting one vacuum from a multi-vacuum install, an orphaned `setup_progress` entry for it is written back to .storage and survives restarts, and a background discovery pass (including a brand service call on Roborock) keeps firing for the removed vacuum until the entry is reloaded or HA restarts. Nothing is user-visible today because the resurrected bucket is empty and `get_known_vacuum_ids()` (manager.py:2966-2969) unions only vacuums/maps/active_jobs — but the invariant the design leans on is not actually held by the code, so any future writer reached from a snapshot-based listener resurrects real data.

title: dock_events.register() never reads the adapter's `dock_events.enabled` flag — a brand that declares enabled:False but inherits triggers still records dock events
impact: A future adapter that copies the Eufy dock_events block and flips `enabled: False` to opt out gets the opposite of what it declared: dock events are recorded and counters incremented, while the Base Station UI tab is hidden — so the data accumulates with no surface to inspect or correct it. Fails toward Eufy behaviour, silently, which is the recurring shape of this seam.

title: The exactly-once claim's REFUSAL dict is consumed as a successful finalize — the duplicate EVENT_JOB_FINISHED survived the fix and now carries an all-null payload
impact: The documented public automation trigger `eufy_vacuum_job_finished` (docs/advanced/02-events.md; docs/dev/02-ha-integration.md:438 documents an 11-key contract) fires twice on a normal completed run, and the FIRST of the two claims status "completed" with every data field null. A user automation that notifies "{{ trigger.event.data.room_count }} rooms in {{ trigger.event.data.duration_minutes }} min" renders "None rooms in None min" or throws a template error, then is immediately followed by a second, correct notification. Nothing is logged as an error — the debug line asserts "Auto-finalized job". Additionally mark_active_job_finalized is invoked with the refusal, blanking the stored finalize_summary (all values None); the real finalize normally overwrites it a moment later, but the two paths race on separate executor hops, so on a slow/contended executor the card's post-run summary is left permanently blank — no outcome, no learning verdict, no sanity flags — which is the identical user-visible symptom already recorded for A2-CAN-6.

title: _process tasks are untracked — remove() drops only the subscription, so a config-entry reload orphans an in-flight finalize bound to the dead manager
impact: Reload the integration (Configure -> options change, HACS update, Dev-Tools reload) in the seconds after a run docks and the run's finalization lands in a manager that is no longer authoritative: the live manager still shows the job as `started`, so the card keeps displaying an in-progress run, manual start stays blocked, and the run is subsequently either finalized a second time or reaped and recorded as `interrupted` rather than `completed` — which changes whether it feeds learning. No error is surfaced on either side.

title: The inline mop-wash detector diverges from the dedicated dock_events listener: hard-coded Eufy wash vocabulary as a fallback, and no same-state guard against attribute-only re-triggers
impact: `observed_mop_wash_count` on the active job is inflated. That value is written into the completed-job record as `actual_mop_wash_count` and is handed to register_post_job_water_amendment at lifecycle.py:398 as `mop_wash_count_at_finalization`, which is the baseline the post-job amendment compares against to decide whether a further wash happened after finalization. An over-count therefore both overstates the run's water usage in the learning record and can suppress the legitimate post-job water amendment, with no error shown. For a future brand that declares an empty last_mop_wash trigger list, mop washes are counted against Eufy's words on a dock that has none.

title: is_job_active() treats a NOT-YET-ADDED / removed job_active entity as "no job running", defeating the Roborock mid-recharge completion guard
impact: A Roborock run that docked mid-job to recharge is auto-finalized while the robot is still going to resume. No error is surfaced: the user sees a "completed" job whose duration/room set covers only the first half. mark_active_job_finalized clears the active_job slot, so the resumed second half has no dispatched job to attribute to (it becomes an orphan/external run). Worse, the truncated record is written to the learning history as a normal completed job and feeds the per-room minute estimates, durably skewing every subsequent time estimate for those rooms.

title: completion_secondary_satisfied() returns True from a config FLAG without verifying the entity it delegates to exists; the "Invariant" asserted in the caller is never validated
impact: For a brand-3 adapter written against Roborock's pattern, the completion gate silently degrades to "task_status equals one string" with no secondary confirmation at all — while has_observed_active_lifecycle never arms, so the gate is instead permanently closed and every job strands as status:started until the 5-minute stranded reaper writes it up as `interrupted`. Every run of that brand is recorded as interrupted and held from learning, with no diagnostic pointing at the missing entity declaration.

title: completed_finalize_signals() docstring claims it returns "" for unavailable entities; it actually returns the literal "unavailable"/"unknown"
impact: No wrong result on either shipped brand today. Latent: it is a false description of behaviour in the one place a new adapter author reads to choose their sentinel vocabulary, and it makes 'entity does not exist' indistinguishable from 'entity says the run is over'.

title: _common owns the completion QUESTION but not its vocabulary defaults — the clear-sentinel and completion-status fallbacks exist as two hand-copied literals in different modules
impact: No wrong result today (the two literal sets are identical). Latent divergence: changing the generic completion fallback in one place silently leaves the completion gate and the stranded reaper judging the same run against different vocabularies, which presents as jobs being reaped as `interrupted` while the gate believes they completed (or vice versa) — a defect that would appear to live in the reaper, not here.

title: get_adapter_value() is a second, independent implementation of the identical lookup already shipped in adapters/registry.py
impact: No behavioural difference today. A fix or semantic change applied to one implementation (e.g. distinguishing a declared null from an absent key, or adding a diagnostic when a declared block is the wrong type) would silently miss every listener, since the listeners all route through the copy that is not the registry's own.

title: The listener layer never uses either canonical in-flight predicate — it hand-inlines the status set that dispatched_job_is_in_flight declares itself "THE single answer" to
impact: No wrong result today (the inlined literal matches the constant). Latent: adding a status to _DISPATCHED_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES updates the two predicates and misses lifecycle.py:137, so the completion gate would stop processing runs in the new status while the rest of the integration considers them live — presenting as jobs that never finalize. The is_job_active naming collision is a standing invitation for a future caller to read its False as "no run in progress" and silently take the Eufy path.

title: Sampler cadence collapses to min() across all vacuums while the attribution engine multiplies tick counts by each vacuum's OWN declared interval_s — Roborock is sampled at 2.0s but its ticks are valued at 5.0s
impact: On an install with both shipped brands (the maintainer's own Alfred/Eufy + Ivy/Roborock setup), every Roborock app-started run writes per-room durations 2.5x too long: external_ingest.build_pose_only_record:649 computes `active_s = int(round(entry["n"] * interval_s))` from the inflated tick count, and that `time_active_s` lands in the durable learning record feeding per-room time estimates. `per_room[rid]["dwell_s"]` (room_attribution_engines.py:148) is inflated identically. Separately, the 3000-sample buffer cap (_MAX_POSE_SAMPLES) was sized for the declared cadence — at the real 2.0s cadence it holds ~100 min instead of ~250 min, so a long Roborock whole-house run silently del-oldest-evicts its earliest rooms and those rooms drop out of the attributed set entirely. No error is logged in either case.

title: The sampling timer is fire-and-forget: a tick slower than interval_s overlaps the next tick, double-recording samples and stamping stale pose content with a fresh timestamp
impact: On a slower host or with a large map raster, an external run buffers more samples than ticks elapsed, and `active_s = round(entry["n"] * interval_s)` (external_ingest.py:649) turns the surplus into over-reported per-room cleaning durations in the learning record. Because `record_pose_sample` stamps `t` at APPEND time rather than read time, a sample whose pose was read one interval earlier is written with the later timestamp, so `_dominant_room` window matching (external_ingest.py:427) can mis-assign a counter segment near a room boundary by up to one interval. The buffer also fills faster, bringing the 3000-sample eviction of the run's start forward. Non-deterministic and entirely silent.

title: _is_parked has no working fallback on the native_current_room path — when task_status is unreadable it returns 'not parked', the opposite of what its own docstring claims
impact: Every docked/parked tick in that window is treated as floor-cleaning and `_resolve_managed_room_id` resolves whatever `active_cleaning_target` reads — which on Roborock reverts to the DOCK's room name when parked (documented in adapters/roborock/adapter.py:552-554). Those ticks are recorded against the dock's managed room instead of being nulled to None, inflating that room's tick count (and therefore `time_active_s` in build_pose_only_record) and fragmenting the neighbouring room runs. A future adapter declaring the native source without an active_run_task_states vocabulary would attribute the ENTIRE parked tail of every run — the exact ~13-minute dock-sitting failure the docstring says this function exists to prevent — to the dock's room.

title: A zero or negative interval_s survives adapter registration (warn-only) and then splits the sampler in two: register() drops it, _sample_vacuum_once does not
impact: Single-vacuum case: room-attribution pose sampling is silently disabled for the whole install — external runs finalize with no pose_samples and fall back to counter-only attribution, with no error surfaced anywhere. Multi-vacuum case: the vacuum IS sampled, but the engine resolves interval_s to 0.0 (or negative) via `_resolve`'s `float(value)`, so `active_s = round(entry["n"] * 0.0)` writes 0-second (or negative-second) per-room cleaning times into the learning record.

title: _handle_pose_tick has no per-vacuum exception guard, and only the live_pose read is wrapped — one vacuum raising drops every later vacuum from that tick
impact: A deterministic raise on one vacuum silently costs the other vacuum(s) their entire pose stream for the duration of the run — room attribution for those runs degrades to the counter-only path with no user-visible indication. The traceback is logged once per tick by HA's task exception handler, so it is noisy in the log but nothing correlates it to the missing attribution. Alphabetical ordering means the Eufy entity precedes the Roborock one on the maintainer's install, so the Eufy path's failures are the ones that would silence Roborock sampling.

title: Module docstring still declares the sampler 'Capture-only / inert — nothing consumes pose_samples yet', but the W5c consumption wire has landed
impact: No runtime effect on its own, but it materially understates blast radius: every defect in this file is currently read by maintainers as affecting an inert capture buffer, when in fact the samples drive which rooms an external run is recorded as having cleaned, the per-room durations written to the learning record, and — via reconcile_dispatched_identity's 'rescued' branch — the room identity stamped on a DISPATCHED run's timings. That framing is plausibly why this layer went eleven audits without review.

title: job_progress ticker gates on a hand-copied {"started","paused"} literal, so app-started (external) runs never get the Lever B live current-room refresh or a progress tick
impact: A run the user starts from the vendor app on a Roborock is captured, but its per-room attribution is reconstructed from stale `current_room` values — consecutive rooms collapse into one or land on the wrong room boundary, and that wrong attribution is written into durable learned per-room stats with no error surfaced. Separately, on both brands the dashboard does not auto-refresh during an app-started run (the tick event the card listens for is never fired), so the panel looks frozen while the robot is actually cleaning.

title: `last_battery_percent` has no writer anywhere in production, so every counter sample carries battery=None and per-room `battery_delta` is permanently null on both dispatch paths
impact: Every archived run, on every brand, on both the atomic and strict-order dispatch paths, records `battery_delta: null` for every room. The per-room battery-consumption figure the run archive and diagnostics expose is permanently blank, and any future consumer that reads it (e.g. per-room battery estimation) would silently see "no data" rather than an error.

title: `_duration_state_to_seconds` silently treats any unrecognized unit as seconds, and re-resolves the unit per event with no mid-run consistency check
impact: Latent. On the two shipped brands the resolved units are "s" (Eufy, absent → seconds) and the adapter hint "min" (Roborock, bare number), both handled correctly and test-covered, so no wrong value reaches a user today. The exposure is that a brand or HA release publishing an unhandled duration unit, or flipping the unit mid-run, produces a silently wrong learned run duration with no warning to diagnose from.

title: Station-water subscription guesses an entity key that exists nowhere, ignores the adapter's `supports_station_water` declaration, and swallows every lookup failure silently
impact: No wrong value on either shipped brand today (Eufy's `sensor.<vac>_water_level` is the station tank and is correct; Roborock never subscribes). The exposure is for the next adapter: an entities key named `water_level` that means "mop intensity 1-3" would be recorded and archived as the run's ending station-water percentage with no validation and no error, and a capabilities lookup failure produces the same silent blank with nothing in the log to explain it.

title: watch_map's type annotation and the `int` value_type branch are both stale — the annotation declares 3-tuples while all three writers store 4-tuples, and no entry ever uses `int`
impact: None today — purely a maintenance hazard. The annotation actively misdescribes the structure a future contributor must match, and the dead branch implies an int-valued metric channel that does not exist.

title: A blocker sensor going `unavailable` satisfies every negating rule operator, so a Zigbee/cloud dropout pauses or CANCELS a live run (return_to_base)
impact: A battery-powered contact/occupancy sensor dropping off the mesh for one poll — routine on Zigbee/Z-Wave and on Eufy's push-only MQTT — physically aborts a clean in progress: the robot stops mid-room and drives home. The run is recorded as `cancelled`, its rooms land in the incomplete_run_log, and the learning sample is discarded. The user sees a path-blocked event naming a door that never actually opened.

title: path_blockers spawns unbounded concurrent `_process` tasks; a second blocker event inside the 30s cancel-confirm window double-cancels and the loser deterministically nulls the run's finalize_summary
impact: A cancelled run reports itself as completed. `sensor` lifecycle (sensor/lifecycle.py:199-202) returns "finalized" instead of "cancelled"; the card summary (jobs/active_job.py:1558-1568) reads "Job completed" instead of "Job cancelled"; the stored pointer to the learning record (job_id/job_path/finalized_at) is nulled, so the run is no longer navigable from the active-job record. Any automation triggering on eufy_vacuum_job_finished with `status == completed` fires for a run the robot never finished — and it fires twice.

title: dock_events treats a first-sighting (old_state=None) and an unavailable-recovery as a fresh dock cycle, inflating maintenance counters and resetting last_dry_start
impact: Maintenance counters drift upward with no user action — every HA restart during a dry or wash cycle adds a phantom cycle. The Base Station tab shows the dry as having started at the restart time rather than the real start, and consumable/maintenance advice derived from mop_wash_count / dust_empty_count / dry_start_count is silently wrong. The counters are persisted, so the error is durable and only correctable via `set_dock_event_count`.

title: The 1-minute reap ticker has no in-flight guard while each reap blocks up to ~35s, so two reapable slots guarantee overlapping ticks and a duplicate cancel
impact: After a multi-vacuum outage the auto-cancelled runs report as "completed"/"finalized" instead of "cancelled", lose their job_id/job_path pointer, and fire duplicate job-finished events — so a `retry_missed_rooms`-style automation sees an extra completed run for a job that was reaped.

title: A discovery pass on the active map is scored against configured rooms across ALL maps, so switching maps makes the other map's rooms accrue "removed" strikes
impact: On a multi-floor/multi-map setup, switching maps makes the setup tab report rooms as removed from the vacuum and flips setup_complete out of sync (setup/status.py:193-218), prompting the user to delete room configuration — including its learning history — for rooms that still exist and are simply on the other map.

title: Discovery triggers survive per-vacuum deletion and re-create a setup_progress record for the deleted vacuum — the "subscription to a deleted entity is inert" comment is false
impact: Deleting a vacuum's device leaves a resurrected setup_progress skeleton in storage that survives restarts and shows up in diagnostics. Cosmetic today because `vacuums` stays deleted so the card and `get_known_vacuum_ids` ignore it — but it silently violates the documented "delete is complete and cannot resurrect" contract that _teardown_vacuum was written to guarantee.

title: get_manager() is re-fetched after a device-length await, so a config-entry reload mid-dispatch loses the just-started job record (or raises a bare KeyError)
impact: The robot is cleaning but the integration has no active-job record: the card shows no run in progress, no per-room progress or attribution, no learning sample, and no finalization. In path (b) nothing is logged at all — a clean success response with the job silently gone. In path (a) the user gets a raw `KeyError` traceback in the log because line 156 sits OUTSIDE the handler's try/except (lines 151-154).

title: resolved_call_data's docstring claims an unresolvable map_id always raises; discover_rooms is the one consumer that silently falls through and persists the payload under an empty-string map key
impact: Pressing "Discover rooms" — exactly what a user does when the active_map sensor is stale/unavailable — returns a clean success (the service is registered without supports_response, and the handler's `except Exception -> HomeAssistantError` at rooms.py:141 never fires because nothing raises). The rooms are cached under `""` while every reader (room_crud.py:132/233/365/412, setup/drift.py) keys by the real map id, so the setup panel shows zero discovered rooms with no error, and a stale `discovery[""]` bucket is persisted permanently.

title: Sixteen registered services documented as public API have no services.yaml descriptor, including set_dock_event_count whose five dock siblings all have one
impact: A YAML author who follows docs/advanced/03-services.md to `set_dock_event_count` or any setup_* service finds it in Developer Tools -> Actions with no name, no description, and no field UI — just a bare data editor with no hint of the allowed `event_type` values (which the voluptuous schema restricts to three literals). No runtime failure, but the documented surface and the HA-side surface disagree.

title: get_room_profiles is the only one of the 79 registrations with no schema, so caller-supplied scoping arguments are accepted and silently ignored
impact: A caller who passes `vacuum_entity_id` or `map_id` — a reasonable assumption given that every neighbouring room-profile service requires `vacuum_entity_id` — gets the global profile library back with no indication the argument was ignored. Compare `setup_get_status`, which is also argument-free but declares `vol.Schema({})` (services/setup.py:86) and therefore REJECTS extra keys.

title: The debug-capture auto-stop timer is not cancelled on unload, so an orphaned timer from before a reload kills a capture started after it
impact: User starts a capture with `max_minutes: 60`, reloads the integration, starts a new capture — the new capture silently stops at the old timer's deadline, logged only as 'debug capture auto-stopped after 60 min'. Diagnostic tooling only; no user data affected.

title: start_selected_rooms discards every refusal — no supports_response, no exception, DEBUG log only; docs promise a response it cannot return
impact: An automation that calls `eufy_vacuum.start_selected_rooms` at 09:00 gets a green checkmark whether the robot started or was refused for any of eleven reasons. The house is not cleaned, no error, no notification, nothing in the log above DEBUG. The documented recovery workflow (read confirmation_required, retry with confirm_token) is impossible on this service — the token can only be obtained by separately calling get_start_status first, which the docs never say.

title: start_zone_clean is the only start service with zero preconditions — it dispatches to the robot mid-job and strands the tracked room job
impact: Called while a tracked room job is running, the robot abandons the in-flight room clean and starts a zone clean, while the integration's active_job stays `started` with its full room list, timers, and counter/pose sample buffers. When the device docks, the lifecycle listener finalizes the ROOM job against the zone run's durations and battery delta — the learning record is written for rooms that were never cleaned, and the completed rooms are attributed wrongly. No warning is shown at any point; the service returns `{"status": "dispatched"}` which looks like a clean success.

title: clear_active_job destroys a running job's record unconditionally and returns nothing — no status precondition, no supports_response, immediate persist
impact: A user or automation clearing what they believe is a stale job while the robot is actually mid-run permanently loses that run's learning data — the run is never finalized, per-room durations are gone, and the incomplete-run log is never written, so retry_missed_rooms has nothing to act on. The robot keeps cleaning with no integration-side record. Because there is no response, the caller cannot even tell whether there WAS a live job it just destroyed.

title: start_zone_clean clean_times has no upper bound; the schema comment claims a dispatch-side per-brand ceiling that exists only on the Roborock branch
impact: On a Eufy, `service: eufy_vacuum.start_zone_clean` with `clean_times: 200` from YAML — or a template that produces a bad number — is forwarded verbatim to the device. The robot either repeats the zone far beyond what the user or the UI implies is possible, or the provider rejects the command and the zone clean silently does nothing. The comment in the service file is the reason nobody added the bound, and it is describing behaviour only one of the two shipped brands has.

title: Break schemas do not enforce the break_type→parameter dependency, and the two sibling schemas disagree on which break types exist
impact: A YAML user builds a stepped queue with `add_queue_break: {break_type: wait, after_index: 2}`, gets a successful service call, and the break is never added. Their next run is a flat clean with no pause — the robot cleans straight through, and the only signal was a response field they had no reason to capture. These services have no card caller at all (src/ grep: only constants.js declares the names), so YAML is the sole surface and nothing else validates.

title: get_queue_steps returns `breaks` in a shape set_queue_breaks rejects — the documented read-modify-write round trip fails validation
impact: The obvious automation pattern — call get_queue_steps into a response_variable, edit one break's minutes, send the list back through set_queue_breaks — fails with a voluptuous error the user has to reverse-engineer, because the read shape and the write shape of the same store differ. Anyone building the reorder flow the manager docstring anticipates must hand-write a flattening step that is documented nowhere.

title: async_save() sits after the try/except in every job_control handler — a raise after dispatch leaves a running job in memory only
impact: The robot is cleaning, the user sees a red "Failed to start cleaning: …" error, and the active job exists only in RAM. A restart or reload before the next unrelated save orphans the run: it is never finalized, never learned from, and the card shows no job while the vacuum is mid-clean. The error message also misrepresents what happened — the start did not fail, a post-dispatch step did.

title: Queue mutators create and persist a storage bucket for any syntactically-valid entity id, including one that is not a vacuum this integration manages
impact: A typo in an automation permanently accumulates junk vacuum/map entries in the integration's store, with no error and a response that says only "needs_two_rooms" rather than "unknown vacuum". Storage junk rather than a functional break, but it is created by a call that reported failure.

title: resolved_call_data's docstring claims a "clear error" on unresolvable map_id; the actual failure is a bare TypeError, and no service in either module raises ServiceValidationError
impact: A user on an adapter that declares no `active_map` entity (scalar/Tuya Eufy, or any brand-3 adapter) who omits `map_id` — which every schema marks Optional and every services.yaml field describes as "Leave blank to use the current active map" — gets a Python TypeError instead of "this vacuum needs an explicit map_id". The docstring is the reason no one added the check.

title: save_managed_rooms silently wipes a map's entire saved room configuration when the discovery cache for that map is empty
impact: An automation or script calling eufy_vacuum.save_managed_rooms against a map it has not just re-discovered permanently destroys all of that map's room configuration. The service is registered WITHOUT supports_response and the handler returns None (services/rooms.py:236-237, 251-254), so the caller receives no error, no response, and no room_count — nothing at all. The user discovers it when the room entities vanish and the next Start finds an empty queue.

title: enabled_room_ids: null coerces to [] and wipes every managed room — the exact opposite of omitting the key
impact: A YAML author who writes `enabled_room_ids:` with a blank value (a key with no value is None in YAML — the single most common YAML slip) gets total destruction of that map's room configuration, while the DOCUMENTED behaviour for that field (docs/advanced/03-services.md:255, 'Omit to keep all rooms enabled') is the opposite. No error, no response (the service has no supports_response). Same for an explicit `enabled_room_ids: []`, which no documentation covers.

title: save_managed_rooms stamps every room's floor type as user-confirmed while its schema makes it structurally impossible to supply one
impact: A carpeted room created through this service is recorded as hardwood and confirmed, so the user is never asked. The carpet invariants in _protected_room_config (profiles/manager.py:98-105 — force water 'Off', edge_mopping False, downgrade mop modes) key off floor_type and therefore never fire for it. When the user subsequently applies a mop profile to the map (apply_room_profile with vacuum_mop_deep), that room gets water 'Medium' + edge mopping from FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS['hardwood']='Low'/profile water and the robot wet-mops carpet, with the readiness gate showing green.

title: services.yaml advertises required fields that the voluptuous schemas reject — three services fail outright when the user fills the form HA renders
impact: A user who opens Developer Tools -> Actions, picks 'Save user room profile', and fills in every field HA marks required gets a hard validation failure and cannot save a custom profile through the UI at all. The card has a `saveUserRoomProfile` wrapper (src/actions/room-profiles.js:26) with no caller, so Developer Tools IS the only surface for these two services — they are effectively uncallable as documented. For save_managed_rooms the advertised carpet/floor-type workflow is impossible, which is the direct cause of ROOMS-3.

title: apply_room_profile silently no-ops on unknown room ids and returns a success-shaped response with no way to tell
impact: An automation that applies a named profile to rooms after a re-segment renumbered them (Roborock does this routinely) reports success while changing nothing — the rooms clean at their old settings and the user has no signal. supports_response=True is declared (room_profiles.py:230-233), so the card DOES receive the payload; there is simply nothing in it to branch on. This is the same 'failure returns the success shape' seam the card audit flagged one layer up.

title: update_room_fields accepts any clean_mode string; a casing/spelling variant keeps water in storage and in the UI but silently drops it from the wire payload
impact: A hand-written automation that sets clean_mode to 'Vacuum_Mop' or 'Mop' (there is no enumeration anywhere for the user to copy the exact token from) produces a room the card shows as mopping at water 'Medium' with edge mopping on, while the payload actually dispatched carries no water_level and no edge_mopping field at all — the robot runs the pad dry over the room. No error, no warning log, and get_payload_state confirms nothing because the field is simply absent.

title: save_user_room_profile silently overwrites an existing custom profile and reports saved: true, while its sibling rename_room_profile refuses the identical collision
impact: An automation that re-saves a profile under a name the user already uses replaces the user's saved settings with no warning and a success response. The card has no caller for this service (src/actions/room-profiles.js:26 defines saveUserRoomProfile; grepping src/ finds no invocation), so there is no UI confirmation dialog behind it either. Docs disclose the 'legacy user slot' default (docs/advanced/03-services.md:955) but say nothing about the explicit-profile_name clobber.

title: delete_room_profile / rename_room_profile leave dangling profile_name references on rooms, which then silently resolve to a built-in preset
impact: After deleting or renaming a custom profile, every room that used it reports selected_profile_name/'selected_profile_label' as 'vacuum_quick'/'Vacuum Only Quick' in the room editor and in get_effective_room_details, while its stored per-room fields are still the deleted profile's mop settings. The room reads as a built-in preset it does not match until the next write to that room, when _finalize_room_update snaps profile_name to 'custom'. Dispatch is NOT affected — apply_room_profile_to_config copies all six settings onto the room, so room_config.get(...) wins in resolve_room_profile_for_room — which is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH.

title: update_room_fields accepts any fan_speed string; on Roborock an unrecognised value leaves the device's previous suction in place with no error
impact: A room configured through the service with a slightly-off fan speed cleans at the wrong suction indefinitely. The card shows the value the user typed, get_payload_state echoes it back, and nothing anywhere reports that the device never received it. As with ROOMS-6 there is no enumeration in services.yaml (bare `text: {}`, services.yaml:167-170) or in docs/advanced/03-services.md for the user to copy the exact token from.

title: save_managed_rooms is the most destructive service in the area and the only mutation registered without supports_response
impact: The one service in this area that can replace a map's entire room set wholesale gives the caller nothing to check — not room_count, not the resulting room list. An automation cannot detect ROOMS-1 or ROOMS-2 even defensively, because there is no response to inspect. The UI equivalent setup_save_rooms at least returns `{'status': 'success', 'room_count': N}` (services/setup.py:226).

title: Error-surfacing is inconsistent across the area: rooms.py wraps 4 of 5 handlers, room_profiles.py wraps 0 of 8, access_graph.py wraps 0 of 2
impact: The same root cause produces a readable error from one service and an unhandled-exception traceback plus a generic 'Unknown error' toast from its sibling. For the supports_response services the websocket call is rejected either way, so the card cannot distinguish 'no active map configured' from an internal bug.

title: setup_save_rooms rebuilds the map from the stale/absent `data["discovery"]` cache and REPLACES the map's rooms wholesale — returns {"status": "success"}
impact: The user opens Setup → a configured map → the room editor (which shows the rooms via setup_get_map_rooms), changes a floor-type chip, clicks Save, and every room on that map is deleted along with its rules and access-graph links. The card shows no error; the service returns "success" and the response's own room_count is 0. HA entities for those rooms are torn down. Queue/run-profiles referencing those rooms break. There is no undo.

title: save_adapter_config accepts a two-key config and registers it OVER the live code adapter — every omitted block silently resolves to Eufy behaviour on a Roborock
impact: A Roborock is driven with Eufy vocabulary and Eufy learning engines from the moment the call returns until the next reload: wrong fan/water strings sent to the robot, room boundaries learned from a counter signal Roborock never emits, external-run attribution from a pose engine that has no input, and the setup panel loses the Import Active Map step mid-onboarding. Nothing is shown to the caller — the service has no supports_response and raises nothing.

title: delete_adapter_config unregisters the CURRENTLY REGISTERED adapter — after startup that is the code adapter — leaving the vacuum with no adapter at all
impact: A Roborock user who once experimented with save_adapter_config, then later calls delete_adapter_config to clean up, silently converts their Roborock into a vacuum driven by the Eufy dispatch engine and Eufy defaults until the integration is reloaded. The next cleaning run sends Eufy-shaped commands. The service returns nothing and logs only at DEBUG.

title: save_adapter_config / delete_adapter_config declare no supports_response and return None on every rejection path — a rejected write is indistinguishable from a successful one
impact: An automation or script calling save_adapter_config with a config missing adapter_id gets a clean successful service call and continues to the next step; nothing was written. The only evidence is a log line the user is not looking at. There is no return value the caller could branch on even if they wanted to.

title: save_adapter_config persists to storage BEFORE registering, so a config the registry flags as invalid is written to disk anyway and reloaded at every restart
impact: A user building a custom adapter types a template name that does not exist. The call succeeds silently, the config is written to .storage, and every subsequent cleaning run is dispatched with the Eufy payload shape — on a Roborock that means the wrong service and the wrong arguments reach the robot. Recovering requires knowing that delete_adapter_config exists (which then triggers SETUP-3).

title: setup_reject_rooms permanently deletes rooms from EVERY map for the vacuum with no map scoping, no protection gate, no confirmation and no way back
impact: A YAML/automation caller, or a user clicking Reject on a room the drift panel surfaced, silently loses that room's configuration on maps they were not looking at. Room entities disappear, run profiles and queues referencing them break, and no re-import can bring the room back because the id is now in rejected_rooms.

title: Three setup handlers subscript data["map_id"] after resolved_call_data and raise a bare KeyError — the helper's docstring claims the manager raises a clear error instead
impact: A YAML caller following docs/advanced/03-services.md (which documents map_id as optional on all three) gets an opaque `KeyError: 'map_id'` and an aborted automation whenever the vacuum is offline or HA has just restarted, instead of the documented clear error. The shipped card always sends map_id, so this is reachable only from the public YAML surface — which is exactly the surface the docs advertise.

title: setup_save_rooms stamps the setup step complete unconditionally, unlike both of its sibling step-advancing handlers
impact: The setup panel reports the wizard complete and `setup_complete: true` for a vacuum whose map now has zero configured rooms. The user is told onboarding finished; the queue has nothing to build from.

title: adapter `setup.steps` is never validated at registration despite two docstrings and the schema claiming it is; two declared step IDs have no completion writer and strand the wizard permanently
impact: Either the wizard silently skips a mandatory step and declares setup complete, or it pins next_step to a step no service can ever mark done and the user is stranded with a permanently incomplete onboarding panel and setup_complete false forever.

title: floor_types accepts any string; an unrecognised value is silently clamped to "hardwood" at read time, so a mistyped carpet becomes a wet-mopped carpet
impact: A YAML caller sets a floor type with a typo or picks a documented-but-unmapped value; the service returns success and the stored value is silently discarded. In the carpet case the robot mops a carpet with water at the hardwood default. In the granite/concrete case the room's water level resolves to empty.

title: setup_delete_map auto-resolves an omitted map_id to whatever map happens to be active at call time
impact: An automation written while the upstairs map was active later deletes the downstairs map, taking its rooms, queue, job records and learned history with it. docs/advanced/03-services.md:1498 flags the operation as irreversible; nothing flags that the target is dynamic.

title: setup_get_map_rooms returns a success-shaped empty room list when the runtime manager is missing — the caller cannot tell "integration not loaded" from "map has no rooms"
impact: During the reload window that setup_add_vacuum itself schedules (services/setup.py:165), the room editor opens with zero rooms and no error. If the user then clicks Save, the card sends `enabled_room_ids: []` (src/bindings/setup.js:288), which is the SETUP-1 wipe.

title: setup_set_map_camera stores an unvalidated entity_id and reports success even when the entity does not exist
impact: A typo in the camera entity id is confirmed as set. The Map view then shows no live backdrop and the user has no signal connecting the two — the stored value looks correct in setup_get_status (status.py:207) because that field is echoed back verbatim.

title: get_vacuum_capabilities uses the raising get_manager() while its siblings in the same module use the tolerant .get() form, and it writes storage on a read-shaped service
impact: Calling the capability service during a reload produces an unhandled KeyError instead of a clean error, and a read-only-looking call touches .storage on every invocation.

title: None of the 10 setup_* services and 5 of the 6 adapter-config services have services.yaml or translation entries
impact: In Developer Tools → Actions these 15 services appear with the raw slug and no field editors, so the only way to call them correctly is to hand-write YAML from the prose docs — for services including the two most destructive in the integration (setup_delete_map, setup_reject_rooms), whose confirmation_token and room_ids semantics are exactly what a field description would carry.

title: save_run_profile never inspects the manager's `saved` flag — a save that stored nothing returns a success-shaped response and raises nothing
impact: An automation whose 'save my current selection as a profile' step runs when the queue is empty (e.g. after a run, where `_clear_room_selections_after_start` turns every room off on a successful start) reports success and saves nothing; the profile silently does not exist. Same via the card: `src/bindings/run-profiles.js:101` only tests `result?.ok === false`, and no run-profile service ever returns an `ok` key, so the card closes the editor and shows no error.

title: apply_run_profile persists a full room-selection wipe and reports no error when the profile's rooms no longer exist on the map
impact: After room ids churn (map rebuild / factory reset — Eufy re-scan renumbers segments; a Roborock map re-save likewise), applying an older profile clears the user's entire current room selection, applies nothing, and neither HA nor the card shows an error — the card's post-apply `refreshDashboardSnapshot` just renders 0 rooms selected. The user's next Start does nothing or is blocked. Partial mismatch is equally silent: `applied` is True whenever at least one room matched, so a profile that half-resolved silently cleans a subset.

title: overwrite_run_profile exposes the step-sequence destruction with no warning, no confirmation, no response signal — and commits it with async_save
impact: A user (or automation) that overwrites a stepped profile — vacuum group A, charge to 95%, mop group B, or a mop-dry `wait` — loses the charge/wait boundaries permanently and irrecoverably at the moment of the call. The next `start_run_profile` then runs every room in one uninterrupted phase: the robot skips the charge stop it was configured to take and skips the mop-dry pause. Nothing in the response, the log (debug-level only), the service description or the docs says the sequence was dropped, and the card's editor shows the back-filled single group as if that were the saved plan.

title: set_run_profile_steps accepts a bare `list` and silently drops or clamps every malformed step; only 'at least one room_group survived' is enforced
