impact: A YAML author who mistypes a step type or a percent field gets `saved: True` and a profile that has lost its charge stop — the robot then runs the whole sequence in one go and can strand mid-run instead of docking to charge, or skips a mop-dry wait. services.yaml:1437-1468 compounds it: the documented step vocabulary omits `zone` entirely (which the normalizer supports), so a caller following the service description cannot know which of their steps were understood, and the response's `steps` array is the only place the truth appears.

title: rename_run_profile accepts a blank name and silently relabels the profile 'Untitled', returning renamed:True — the sibling save rejects the same input
impact: An automation renaming a profile from a template that renders empty (`name: "{{ states('input_text.profile_name') }}"` while the helper is empty/unknown/unavailable) destroys the profile's label — the user's named run becomes 'Untitled' with no error and no way to recover the old name, and if it happens to several profiles they become indistinguishable in the card's list.

title: overwrite_run_profile with no rooms enabled returns overwritten:False as a success — the raise gate matches one literal reason, not the failure flag
impact: An automation that refreshes a stored profile after a run — the common 'clean these rooms, then remember what I just did' shape — silently no-ops when the selection has already been cleared, and the user believes the profile was updated. The caller cannot distinguish it from success without knowing which of five verb-flag keys this particular service uses.

title: get_saved_run_profiles and get_dashboard_snapshot lack the package's try/except wrap; an unresolvable map_id surfaces as a raw TypeError, contradicting resolved_call_data's docstring
impact: During an HA restart or while the vacuum's active_map entity is unavailable, the card's primary read (get_dashboard_snapshot) and the run-profile library read fail with an unactionable internal error instead of a message telling the user to pass map_id.

title: No service here checks that vacuum_entity_id is a vacuum this integration manages; unknown ids create durable storage buckets, and a read service writes
impact: A typo'd entity id in an automation gets a plausible-looking response (`{"vacuum_entity_id": "vacuum.typo", "pause_timeout_minutes_default": 0}`) instead of an error, so the user's real setting change appears to have worked; the orphan buckets accumulate in .storage and are never garbage-collected.

title: Dock actions return performed:true / "Dock action sent." when the resolved button entity has no state — the press is silently dropped by HA
impact: User taps Wash Mop on the card (or calls eufy_vacuum.wash_mop from an automation), gets a success response and a success toast, and the mop is never washed. Nothing in the response or the raised-error path distinguishes this from a real dock action; the only trace is a WARNING in the HA core log from a different integration's logger.

title: set_maintenance_interval accepts ANY component string, persists it, and returns saved:true — its sibling reset_maintenance raises ServiceValidationError for exactly that input
impact: An automation that copies a working Eufy call to a Roborock (or just typos the component) gets `{"saved": true, "component": "rolling_brush", "interval_hours": 240.0}` back, no error and no log warning, while the interval it meant to change is untouched. The junk key is persisted into the storage file permanently and never pruned. Calling the sibling reset_maintenance with the same wrong string correctly errors out — so the two halves of the same workflow disagree about whether the input is valid.

title: set_maintenance_interval bypasses the min/max its own docstring claims, and interval_hours: 0 silently turns off the consumable's alert
impact: A YAML typo (`interval_hours: 0`, or hours vs. days confusion producing 10 instead of 240) permanently disables the replace-me alert for that filter/brush with a success response, or pushes the interval past the adapter's declared ceiling so the part is never flagged. No error is shown at any layer and the number entity's own bounds do not protect the slot.

title: acknowledge_error returns the same {"acknowledged": true} whether the latch was deleted, merely MARKED, or was never there — and both docstrings still describe the pre-audit delete semantics
impact: A caller (card or automation) that wants to confirm the alert was cleared cannot: `acknowledged: true` is returned for a vacuum with no error at all, and the mid-run case reports the same success while the latch is deliberately still present. A caller checking `reason` to explain a failure gets a KeyError-shaped absence for the most likely real failure (wrong entity id) and a value only for the least likely one (tracker not loaded). Anyone reading services/errors.py to understand acknowledge semantics is told the latch is deleted, which is exactly the behaviour audit #5 removed.

title: get_recent_errors — a read-only service — creates and persists a durable error_tracker record for any entity_id the caller names
impact: A mistyped or foreign `vacuum_entity_id` in an automation looks like a healthy vacuum with a clean error history — the user concludes there are no errors when in fact they queried nothing. The storage file accumulates permanent phantom vacuum records that no cleanup path removes (`remove_vacuum_record` only fires on real device removal), and each one grows the file every restart.

title: set_dock_event_count overwrites and immediately saves a durable counter for any entity_id, with no managed-vacuum check and no way back except the response body
impact: An automation aimed at the wrong entity id silently seeds a phantom dock_events branch that persists forever and reports success. Aimed at the RIGHT id with a wrong count, it destroys the mop-wash/dust-empty/dry-start lifetime count with no confirmation and no undo — those counters feed the upkeep snapshot's dock_counts, so the user's consumable history is silently rewritten.

title: get_dock_action_status raises a raw TypeError when map_id cannot be auto-resolved — the only unwrapped handler in the three modules, and _common's docstring claims the opposite
impact: Both brands hit this in the restart window and whenever the active-map entity reads unknown/unavailable (Eufy's `sensor.<id>_active_map` before the first map sync; Roborock's `select.<id>_selected_map` while the coordinator is still loading). The card polls dock action status, so the user sees a failed card panel and the log fills with tracebacks instead of a readable "active map not known yet" message. The four write services fail with a Python signature string as their user-facing error text.

title: Dock event-type vocabulary is hand-copied into three places, none derived from the adapter that declares it
impact: No user-visible defect on either shipped brand today. A third adapter that names its dock events differently gets `set_dock_event_count` rejecting every one of its own declared event types at the schema, with the fix requiring three coordinated edits across two files.

title: Mutate-then-save is not atomic in all three write services: a save failure surfaces an error while the change has already taken effect in memory
impact: On a storage write failure the user sees "Failed to save maintenance interval" (or, for the dock/reset services, an unhandled traceback) and reasonably re-checks or re-enters the value — but the change is already live and will be persisted by the next save. Rare (needs a failing storage write) but the error message actively misleads about what state the system is in.

title: async_initialize spawns loop-lifetime work with no teardown — after a config-entry reload the PREVIOUS manager writes its stale self.data over the live store
impact: Every change persisted after a reload can be silently reverted. Concrete: user runs setup_add_vacuum, which saves the new vacuum then schedules a reload (services/setup.py:166); 2-5 minutes later the pre-reload manager's external-run grace timer fires, calls _finalize_external_run and async_save, and the store goes back to the snapshot without vacuum #2. The UI keeps showing the new vacuum (the live manager's in-memory dict) until the next HA restart, when it is gone — along with any rooms, profiles, themes, queue edits or job state saved in the same window. Same shape via Options-flow reload and the integration page Reload button. The orphaned charge/wait poller can also still call maybe_advance_phase and dispatch the next room, so a second manager and a dead one can both drive the same physical run.

title: Room-history preload overwrites the persisted cache with {} whenever the rebuild throws, and marks the cache ready so it never retries
impact: Every room's cleaning-history sensor and the card's last-cleaned/last-mopped chips read 'never cleaned' for the rest of the HA run, with nothing shown to the user (the only signal is a log line). The blank state is then persisted. It also silently weakens a destructive-action guard: setup/protection.py:63-72 derives the 'has_learning_data' protection reason from data['room_history'][vac][map] being non-empty, so a map that does have history drops a reason and can fall from 'high' (typed confirmation) to a lower protection level for map deletion.

title: Startup re-seed of the bundled theme library resurrects themes the user deleted, and re-points default_theme_id
impact: A user who curates the theme library — deleting the bundled themes they do not want, with a confirm dialog implying it stuck — finds all of them back in the picker after the next HA restart, silently and with no error. If the deleted theme was the global default, the default is silently re-pointed at theme_follow_ha, changing the rendered theme for every vacuum that is not individually pinned.

title: The startup backfill and setup_progress migration hard-code Eufy vocabulary and structurally cannot consult the adapter
impact: No divergence on the two shipped brands today. A third brand whose room_profiles.default_profile is not 'vacuum_quick' would have any legacy room missing profile_name stamped with another brand's profile key at startup (get_room_profile falls back to the catalog default for an unknown name, so it degrades rather than crashes); a brand declaring a different setup-step vocabulary would have a pre-state-machine install stamped complete against step ids it does not declare, leaving its real first step showing as incomplete forever.

title: Room-update fan-out identifies "stale" entities by unique_id PREFIX, so a room edit on one vacuum permanently deletes a sibling vacuum's entities from the entity registry
impact: On any multi-vacuum install where one vacuum's entity_id is another's plus a numeric suffix (HA's own default for a second identical robot), the first room edit — toggling a room switch, applying a room profile, saving rooms, reordering the queue — on vacuum A's map "2" silently deletes ALL of vacuum B's room switches, room number entities, room-history sensors and rule-status sensors from the entity registry. Registry deletion is durable and takes the user's customizations with it: renamed entity_ids, custom names, icons and area assignments are gone, and every automation, script and dashboard card referencing those entity_ids breaks. No error is surfaced anywhere — the sweep logs nothing and `_notify_rooms_updated`'s try/except never fires because this is not an exception path. The entities reappear (as fresh, un-customized registry entries) only after a config-entry reload or HA restart.

title: async_preload_room_history_cache replaces the whole per-vacuum room_history subtree AFTER an executor await, silently discarding any room-history written during that await
impact: A run that finishes while a room-history rebuild is in flight has its per-room "last cleaned / last vacuumed / last mopped" timestamps reverted to the previous run's values on every room-history sensor, and the wrong values are then persisted. Nothing is logged. The condition is not self-correcting within the process — the ready-flag suppresses further rebuilds — so it persists until an HA restart or an explicit invalidation (save_managed_rooms / reconcile_room / apply_room_profile all `discard` the ready flag). The rebuild is scheduled at every platform setup (sensor/__init__.py:227) and after each of those invalidations, so the window overlaps the single most common event in the integration: a run ending.

title: The manager's four own callback registries append without a duplicate check while the theme registry they delegate to dedupes, and unregister removes only one copy
impact: Latent today. If any future caller registers a room-update callback twice — or if the path_blockers `remove()`/`register()` pairing is ever broken so its `remove` no-ops — that subscriber survives config-entry unload and keeps firing against torn-down entities, and its stale-entity sweep runs twice per room change. The behavioural difference between the theme pair and the other four is invisible at the call site.

title: remove_vacuum_record wipes every bucket the five callback registries exist to mirror and fires none of them, dropping the notification obligation its narrower sibling remove_map documents
impact: Contained today by HA's own device-deletion sweep, so no user-visible breakage on the shipped path. The residual is that the in-memory `entity_map` / `room_history_entities` / `room_rule_status_entities` dicts in switch.py, number.py and sensor/__init__.py keep hard references to the deleted vacuum's (now-removed) entity objects until the next reload, and the path_blockers watch_map keeps watching its blocker entities. The real cost is contract drift: the file's most destructive method is the one that documents the least, so the next caller added for `remove_vacuum_record` — a diagnostics reset, a bulk cleanup service — inherits none of the notification duty that `remove_map` spells out.

title: Three of the four fan-out subscribers call async_write_ha_state() unguarded while the fourth routes through a hass-is-None guard, so one bad entity aborts the rest of that subscriber's sync silently
impact: When it triggers, some of a map's room switches or number entities silently fail to appear after a room change, with only an "Room update callback failed for ... map ..." ERROR in the log and no user-facing signal. They appear on the next room update or after a reload. The trigger requires a second notification for the same vacuum/map before the previous `async_add_entities` task has drained (or a write against an already-removed entity), so it is narrow — but the guard that would make it impossible already exists one platform over.

title: mop_active collapses "tank sensor unreadable" into a definite False, so the card confidently reports "Vacuuming" and hides the water-level control on Roborock
impact: On a Roborock S6 (observe-only tank, supports_water_control False) the card takes mop_active at face value: `showWaterLevel()` (src/state/room-editor.js:417-429) returns `mopActive` directly for observe-only brands, and `_renderMopStateIndicator` (src/renderers/room-editor.js:353-366) renders a read-only "Vacuuming" badge for any non-null value. So whenever the water-box sensor is unavailable — a routinely-hit state on a vacuum that sleeps — the room editor tells the user the robot is set to VACUUM and removes the water-level picker, even though the tank is attached and the next run will mop. No error, no "unknown" state, no way for the user to tell it is a sensor dropout rather than a real reading. If the binary_sensor is disabled-by-default in the entity registry on some HA/Roborock versions, the wrong answer is permanent rather than transient.

title: get_dashboard_snapshot composes get_job_progress_snapshot TWICE, so job_progress and job_control in the same payload can describe different rooms — and every side effect in the progress composer fires twice per card poll
impact: During a multi-room run the card can render a timeline that highlights room B as in-progress while the status line above it reads "Cleaning C" and C is also drawn as an upcoming room — a self-contradicting view with no error, exactly when the user opens the card after leaving it closed. It also doubles the room catch-up rate (two rooms advance per poll instead of one), which is load-bearing behaviour nobody chose, and doubles the on-loop cost of the most frequently called service in the integration.

title: The snapshot has no read of the exactly-once finalize claim, so across the finalize await it reports a finished run as actively cleaning and offers Pause / Cancel on it
impact: For the duration of the finalize (a stats rebuild over a long history is easily seconds), the card shows "Cleaning <room>" with a live queue and enabled Pause / Cancel buttons for a run that is already over and being written to disk. Pressing Pause sends a real pause command to a robot that has already docked; pressing Cancel sends a stop/return_to_base to a docked robot, then reaches the finalize chokepoint, is refused with `reason: "finalize_in_flight"` (learning/manager.py:710-716), and `mark_active_job_finalized` is then called with that refusal as the finalize_result — so the user's Cancel is silently swallowed and the resulting `finalize_summary.status` is None.

title: zone_max invents Eufy's device limit (10) for any brand that declares none, while the dispatch gate enforces no cap at all when the key is absent
impact: A future adapter that declares no `zone_max` gets a card that silently stops the zone draw at 10 boxes with no explanation, while the backend would happily have dispatched more — a limit the user is shown but that the device and the server do not have. Zero impact today: both shipped adapters declare `zone_max` explicitly (eufy 10 at adapters/eufy/adapter.py:807, roborock 5 at adapters/roborock/adapter.py:612).

title: get_start_status validates PHASE 0's room count as if it were the whole job — a stepped run whose first phase is a zone is refused with a false "invalid payload" error
impact: A run profile like "clean the entryway zone, then the kitchen", or any rooms+zone queue whose first room happens to be blocked by a room rule that moment, refuses to start and reports "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." The rooms and the zone are all perfectly runnable; the message points the user at a payload problem that does not exist, and there is no way to act on it from the card. Saved Zones (v1.6.0) ship on both brands, so this is live today.

title: start_selected_rooms dispatches phase 0 with no phase_type branch, unlike its phase_runner sibling — and _build_steps_phases' docstring claims a guard that does not exist
impact: Latent today: the only thing stopping a segment-clean command with an empty room list from reaching the robot is the accidental `payload_room_count <= 0` block described in START-1, which is a side effect of the zone phase having no rooms rather than an intentional guard. If START-1 is fixed by relaxing that block (the obvious fix), the robot receives a room_clean/app_segment_clean with no segments — on Roborock a params list with no `segments` key, which the device may interpret as a full-house clean. The docstring reads as a guarantee and will lead whoever fixes START-1 to assume phase 0 is safe to dispatch.

title: get_start_status can never surface a non-blocking lifecycle warning message — preflight's "ready" text shadows it, making dock-drying starts show warning=True with the message "Ready to start cleaning."
impact: Every start attempt during the post-mop dock-drying window — which follows every mop run on both brands — returns a warning flag whose explanatory text says "Ready to start cleaning." and whose reason is "ready". The card raises a caution the user cannot interpret, and the actual reason (the dock is mid-dry) is never shown. The same shadowing silently discards any future non-blocking lifecycle state added to build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle.

title: save_managed_rooms facade wipes every stored room for a map when the discovery cache is empty — the precondition its sibling reconcile_room has
impact: Every per-room setting for that map is permanently destroyed and persisted: floor types, per-room map fill colours, clean mode/fan/water/intensity/passes/edge-mopping overrides, room order, enabled state, is_dock_room / is_transition flags, the whole grants_access_to access graph and all per-room rules. The room switch/number/sensor entities for that map disappear. The user sees no error — the setup room editor they just saved from was populated from the SAVED rooms (setup_get_map_rooms -> get_managed_rooms), not from the discovery cache the save actually rebuilds from, so the UI showed the rooms right up to the moment they were deleted. Recovery requires re-doing the entire room configuration by hand.

title: discover_rooms facade overwrites a good persisted discovery cache with an empty one whenever the room source is momentarily unreadable
impact: On its own the user sees a discover_rooms call that reports 0 rooms and silently forgets the last known good room list. Combined with FACADE-1 it is the loaded gun: after one blip-time discovery, the next Save in the Setup room editor (or any automation calling save_managed_rooms) silently deletes the entire room configuration for that map. Also degrades the identity-shift review: `compute_reconciliation` is run against an empty discovered set, so genuine re-segment/rename reviews are not produced.

title: rebuild_map facade has the same unguarded total-wipe as save_managed_rooms, with no in-repo caller to compensate
impact: Latent today — grep shows no production caller (only core/manager.py, room_crud.py and tests reference it) — but it is a public method on the singleton manager, documented alongside the other room/map operations, and destroys the identical durable data with no confirmation the instant anything wires a service, repair flow, or automation to it. It is the exact shape audit #13 flagged one layer up: a destructive manager method whose precondition was never written down anywhere.

title: save_user_room_profile facade silently overwrites the existing 'user_1' profile when profile_name is omitted, while its sibling mints a unique id
impact: A user (or automation) that saves two custom room profiles without supplying profile_name ends up with one: the second silently replaces the first, and both calls report saved=True. Every room whose stored `profile_name` is `user_1` then resolves through the REPLACEMENT profile — `get_room_profile` merges stored profiles over the built-ins by key, so the label, and any field the room does not itself carry, come from the new profile. The rooms' displayed profile and the settings shown in the editor change with no notification, and no rooms-updated callback fires (unlike apply_room_profile, which notifies and refreshes derived state). services.yaml documents the fallback as 'Omit to keep the legacy user slot', so the behaviour is deliberate — but the service is named/described as 'Save a custom room profile' and offers no error path, which is why this is a real trap rather than a documented mode.

title: services.yaml declares a REQUIRED 'carpet' field on save_user_room_profile and overwrite_room_profile that the voluptuous schema rejects
impact: Calling either service exactly as the HA Developer Tools > Actions form renders it — the form marks Carpet required, so a user filling it in will include it — fails validation with an opaque 'extra keys not allowed' error. The two services are usable only by hand-writing YAML that omits a field the docs say is required. The card is unaffected (it does not call save_user_room_profile, and its overwrite wrapper does not send carpet).

title: Dock-action gate is blind to app-started (external) runs — every dock action reports "Ready" and fires while the robot is mid-run at the dock
impact: The user starts a clean from the Eufy app. The robot returns to the dock to recharge ("Charging (Resume)") or wash the pad mid-run. The card's Base Station tab shows Wash Mop / Dry Mop / Empty Dust as Ready. Tapping Dry Mop starts a multi-hour dock dry cycle on a robot that is about to resume cleaning; tapping Empty Dust / Wash Mop injects an extra dock cycle. There is no error and no warning. Secondarily, the resulting dock_status transition is recorded by listeners/dock_events.py -> `record_dock_event`, bumping `mop_wash_count`, which is what `core/water_amendment.py` consumes as `mop_wash_count_at_finalization` — so the captured external run is finalized with wrong water actuals that then feed learning.

title: Dock action returns performed=True / "Dock action sent." when the resolved button entity exists only in the registry (disabled or not loaded) — a silent no-op reported as success
impact: A user who has disabled the upstream wash/dry/empty button entity (or whose upstream integration is reloading) sees the dock control offered as Ready, taps it, gets a success response, and the dock does nothing. There is no error surfaced anywhere in the card or the service result — the only trace is an HA core log line the user is not looking at.

title: refresh_vacuum_capabilities does NOT reproduce startup's detect_capabilities inputs — it silently drops the dock-button entity candidates, contradicting the comment above it
impact: On an Eufy model outside the x10/x8 hint families that nevertheless exposes wash/dry/empty dock buttons, running the `eufy_vacuum.get_vacuum_capabilities` service (schema default refresh=True, and it async_save()s the result — services/adapter_config.py:195-204) or hitting the model_family self-heal permanently rewrites the stored snapshot with supports_mop_wash/mop_dry/empty_dust False. The Base Station dock controls then report "This vacuum does not support that dock action" for a device that demonstrably does, with no indication that a refresh caused it.

title: remove_vacuum_record drops data["room_history"][vacuum] but leaves the _room_history_cache_ready marker — three sibling call sites invalidate it, the one that DELETES the data does not
impact: On a multi-vacuum config entry, a user who deletes vacuum B's device and then re-adds the same vacuum entity (import map / save rooms) sees an empty Room Cleaning History panel for it — no history rows, no error, no way to force a rebuild — until HA is restarted. `ensure_runtime` likewise hands back vacuum B's pre-removal VacuumRuntimeState (stale selected_map_id / selected_room_ids / active_map_id) instead of a fresh one.

title: get_managed_vacuums reads data["capabilities"] raw and reports supports_* as None when no snapshot exists, unlike its sibling get_vacuum_capabilities which detects on demand
impact: Latent today: the only consumer, setup/status.py:171, reads just `vacuum_entity_id` from the returned items. Any future consumer of the four supports_* fields (or a diagnostics dump) would read `null` and treat it as "unsupported" rather than "not yet detected".

title: Panels registered outside async_setup_entry are never tracked, so unload can't remove them and setup silently re-adds the "no vacuum configured" fallback panel
impact: Right after onboarding a vacuum through the panel (the documented primary path — the config flow's vacuum field is optional and the default notes text tells the user to add the vacuum from the sidebar panel), the sidebar shows a duplicate "Vacuum Agent" entry that renders the "no vacuum configured, go to Settings -> Configure" placeholder, and it comes back on every reload. The real vacuum panel is never removed when the integration is unloaded, disabled or deleted, so it lingers in the sidebar pointing at a dead backend until HA is restarted. Every second and later vacuum is affected unconditionally, since the config entry can carry only one vacuum_entity_id and all others must be added through add_vacuum. No error is shown — the duplicate-registration ValueError is logged at DEBUG.

title: async_setup_entry has no failure unwind, and HA never calls async_unload_entry for an entry that failed setup — a mid-setup raise orphans every subsystem registered so far and the next reload builds a second live copy
impact: After any setup failure (a corrupt/hand-edited storage block reaching an unguarded ensure_record, an ImportError in a lazily-imported listener module after an update, an exception in any service registration), the integration is left half-built with no cleanup, and reloading — the obvious user action, and what the options flow does automatically — duplicates every state listener and timer. The duplicated old subsystems keep writing an increasingly stale copy of the whole storage blob over the live one, so room/job/learning edits made after the reload silently disappear. Nothing surfaces this beyond the single "Error setting up entry" traceback from the original failure.

title: Five learning services registered during setup are missing from async_unregister_learning_services, so they survive unload as ghost services
impact: After the integration is unloaded, disabled or deleted, those five eufy_vacuum.* services stay listed and callable in Developer Tools and in automations. Calling one raises an unhandled KeyError from `hass.data[DOMAIN]["runtime"]` (learning/services.py:252-254) instead of HA's clean "service not found", so an automation that touches process_pending_runs or confirm_external_run fails with a traceback rather than a comprehensible error. No data is lost — every one of the five handlers resolves the core manager before doing any work.

title: Panels registered outside async_setup_entry are never tracked, so unload cannot remove them — and setup then re-adds the "no vacuum configured" fallback panel next to the working one
impact: After adding a vacuum through the panel (the advertised onboarding path), the sidebar shows two "Vacuum Agent" entries and one of them tells the user the integration is not set up yet — with no error or log warning above debug level. Disabling or removing the integration leaves a dead sidebar entry behind until Home Assistant is restarted.

title: async_unregister_learning_services removes 16 of the 21 services async_register_learning_services registers — 5 survive unload and 3 raise a bare KeyError when called
impact: After disabling or removing the integration, 5 eufy_vacuum services stay listed in Developer Tools and remain selectable in automations/scripts; calling confirm_external_run, get_external_pending_runs or discard_external_run produces a raw KeyError traceback instead of "service not found". The three affected services are the external-run review wizard's backend, so an automation built on them fails obscurely rather than reporting the integration is gone.

title: Post-job water-amendment listener + 180s timer, and two hass.data[DOMAIN] cache keys, are created outside setup and never removed by unload
impact: Latent: an orphaned dock-status subscription and timer outlive the integration and can write a job JSON after the entry has been unloaded or deleted; hass.data[DOMAIN] is never actually cleared on unload. Job ids are timestamp-based (learning/job_finalizer.py:484) so the stale job-id set does not suppress a later amendment.

title: Changing the vacuum in the options flow ADDS a second managed vacuum instead of replacing the first — the old pick is never reconciled away
impact: A user who picked the wrong entity at install (or renamed their vacuum entity and updated the option to match) ends up with TWO sidebar panels, both titled "Vacuum Agent" by default and therefore indistinguishable, two service devices, and two complete duplicate entity sets — with no error and no hint that a cleanup step is required. In the entity-rename case the abandoned record is the one holding all the maps, learning history, room profiles and battery stats, while the newly added one starts empty. The options screen's own translated description ("Pick the vacuum entity this integration should manage", singular) and the class docstring at config_flow.py:81-86 ("editing the vacuum entity", "Saving a new value ... registers the panel for the chosen vacuum") both read as replace. Recovery exists but is non-obvious: the user must find the stale service device and delete it to reach `_teardown_vacuum`.

title: The options flow rebuilds the options dict from the stale form snapshot, so a submit can resurrect a vacuum that was deleted while the dialog was open
impact: A user who deletes a vacuum's device while the Configure dialog is open in another tab sees the vacuum reappear after saving the dialog — as an empty shell that has lost all its learning history and maps. No error is shown, and the deletion appears to have silently failed.

title: Panels registered outside async_setup_entry are never tracked, so unload never removes them
impact: After adding a second (or third) vacuum from the setup panel, that vacuum's sidebar entry is orphaned: disabling, unloading or deleting the integration leaves it in the sidebar pointing at a webcomponent that is no longer served, until the user restarts HA. This is precisely the 'still there after disable' symptom the code calls out at __init__.py:623.

title: Five learning services are registered on setup but missing from the unregister list, so they survive unload and entry removal
impact: After the user disables, unloads, or DELETES the integration, eufy_vacuum.confirm_external_run / discard_external_run / get_external_pending_runs / process_pending_runs / set_learning_processing are still listed and callable in Developer Tools until HA is restarted. confirm/discard/get_external_pending_runs resolve the core manager via _get_core_manager (learning/services.py:252-254) which does a bare `hass.data[DOMAIN]['runtime']` and raises KeyError; the other two return {'error':'manager_unavailable'}. Inconsistent, unexplained service surface for a removed integration.

title: Unload stops the debug capture but never cancels its auto-stop timer, which then kills a later capture
impact: Reload the integration while a timed debug capture is armed (max_minutes), then start a new capture: the orphaned timer fires at the ORIGINAL deadline and silently stops the new capture, logging 'debug capture auto-stopped after N min' for an N the user never set on that capture. The user loses the diagnostic trace they were collecting, with no error.

title: Post-job water-amendment state listener and 180s timeout are never cancelled by unload
impact: For up to timeout_seconds (default 180s) after a job finalizes, an unloaded/removed integration still holds a live state subscription and a pending timer, and can still spawn a task that rewrites the job JSON file on disk (via hass.async_create_task at :222) after the user has disabled or deleted the integration. The written data is correct, so there is no wrong result — the defect is the uncancelled loop-lifetime work and the permanently retained hass.data[DOMAIN] dict.

title: Confidence breakpoint table has a dead band at 0.79–0.80; the best-learned rooms fall through it and render as LOW / red "error"
impact: The single most reliably-learned room in the house is badged red "Low confidence" on the card, and drags the whole job estimate to red with it — while a demonstrably worse-learned room next to it shows amber "Medium". Users are trained to distrust exactly the numbers they should trust, and the learning system appears not to be working after dozens of successful runs.

title: App-started (external) runs contribute battery=0.0 samples; the estimator consumes a learned 0.0 as a real number and derives battery_warning / mid_job_recharge_risk = False from it
impact: The card tells the user a 5-room job will finish with 15% left and shows no battery warning and no mid-job-recharge risk, when the job actually needs 40% and the robot will strand and dock mid-run. A user who mostly starts runs from the vendor app — precisely the user external ingest was built for — gets a battery model that converges on "this job is free".

title: _find_room_match Pass 1 can NEVER match a Roborock room: it compares the raw "" intensity against the rebuilder's normalized "standard", so every Roborock room takes a permanent -0.15 intensity-mismatch penalty
impact: Roborock users see their room and job estimates permanently badged one confidence tier lower — often red "Low" instead of amber "Medium" — no matter how many clean runs they accumulate, because the estimator believes it is reading data from a different clean-intensity setting that Roborock does not even have.

title: Estimate consumes avg_minutes with no outlier rejection and no band check, and a single poisoned sample scores MEDIUM confidence because stddev of one sample is 0 by construction
impact: A single bad archived run — one multi-room phase that credited the group's whole time to room[0] — moves the displayed job ETA by an order of magnitude, and when it is the room's FIRST run it does so under an amber "Medium confidence" badge. The user plans around a 15-hour ETA, or writes the feature off as broken.

title: HIGH confidence is mathematically unreachable for any real room, yet _learning_velocity reports runs_to_high=0 at 10 samples and runs_to_medium=0 always
impact: The card advertises a HIGH/green confidence tier that no room can ever reach, counts the user down to it over ten runs, then reports "0 runs remaining" while the badge stays amber or red. An unlearned room is simultaneously scored LOW and told it needs zero more runs to be reliable. The learning-velocity feature actively misinforms.

title: _find_room_match relaxed passes return the lexicographically-first bucket and ignore sample_count entirely — a 1-sample bucket beats a 30-sample one
impact: Changing one room setting the user has not run before throws away every accumulated sample for that room and answers from whichever adjacent bucket happens to sort first, which is systematically the slowest bucket for intensity and the fastest for passes. The displayed room duration can be off by more than 2x while the room's real, well-supported history sits unread.

title: _load_mop_wash_config hard-codes Eufy's wash-frequency bounds (15/20/25) in the brand-agnostic estimator while the adapter already declares wash_frequency_bounds
impact: On any brand whose wash cadence falls outside Eufy's 15-25 minute helper range, the ETA carries a wrong mop-wash overhead and the payload reports a wash interval the dock is not set to. Eufy itself is unaffected because its helper bounds happen to equal the literals.

title: is_mop raw-compares clean_mode against a hand-copied literal set while the very same function canonicalizes it for the stats lookup
impact: Latent today: both shipped adapters put canonical tokens ("vacuum"/"mop"/"vacuum_mop") into resolved_rooms, so is_mop resolves correctly. A brand or a restored older payload carrying a display-string mode silently loses all mop-wash overhead from the ETA while every other part of the estimate matches its learned data — the divergence is invisible because the room lookup still succeeds.

title: estimate() runs ensure_dirs (four mkdir syscalls) three times per call on the event loop, even on full cache hits
impact: Recurring blocking filesystem I/O on the HA event loop on every dashboard snapshot. On a network-mounted config directory this can surface as HA's "blocking call inside the event loop" warning or as UI stutter, without any incorrect output.

title: A single transient read failure makes record_estimate_accuracy silently overwrite the entire accuracy history with one job's rooms
impact: Concrete: store holds 14 room keys / 60 graded samples; one OSError while reading learned/accuracy_stats.json during a 2-room job's finalize rewrites the file with 2 keys at sample_count 1. The 12 lost keys had mean_abs_pct_error ~0.20+, which _score_room_confidence turns into the full -0.20 accuracy penalty; with the history gone _drift_ratio_for_room returns 0.0, so every one of those rooms' confidence JUMPS +0.20 on the very next estimate — e.g. 0.60 (MEDIUM/warning) to 0.80 (HIGH/success). The card presents a newly "high confidence" ETA whose entire supporting evidence was just destroyed, with no user-visible signal. Recoverable only if the user happens to run rebuild_accuracy_stats.

title: reanchor_timeline ignores its own reanchor_at parameter — every ETA is anchored to job start plus the sum of room durations, so all wall-clock dead time is invisible and "Done at" times slide into the past
impact: Concrete: 3 rooms at 10 min each, overhead 7.02, started 12:00. R1 completes at 12:10 with actual_duration 10.0. The user pauses the vacuum at 12:10 and resumes at 12:40. At 12:45 the card refreshes and reanchors with completed=[R1:10]: R2 eta_at = 12:00+20 = 12:20 (25 minutes in the PAST), R3 = 12:30, job_eta_at = 12:00+37.02 = 12:37 (8 minutes in the past). The live banner renders "Cleaning Kitchen — done at 12:20" at 12:45, and it never self-corrects: the timeline stays pinned to sum-of-actuals no matter how much real time elapses. Same failure for any mid-job dock/recharge that is bracketed by a pause, which is exactly the mid_job_recharge_risk state this payload advertises.

title: Reanchoring drops inter-room transit from remaining rooms while keeping it in overhead — remaining ETAs jump earlier then later (oscillation) and the job ETA inflates by one transit leg per completed room on a run that is exactly on estimate
impact: Concrete: 3 rooms × 10 min estimated, learned transit 2.0 min per boundary, overhead 7.02 (startup 1 + transitions 4 + recharge 0.12 + dust 0.9 + return 1), started 12:00. Original timeline: R2 eta 12:22, R3 eta 12:34, job eta 12:37.02. Every room then runs EXACTLY on estimate. After R1 (actual 10.0): R2 -> 12:20, R3 -> 12:30 (both jumped ~2-4 min EARLIER), job eta unchanged 12:37. After R2 (actual 12.0 = 2 transit + 10 clean): R3 -> 12:32 (jumped 2 min BACK OUT), job eta -> 12:39.02. So the user watches R3's "done at" go 12:34 -> 12:30 -> 12:32 with nothing having gone wrong. At completion the job eta reads 12:41.02 against a real finish of ~12:35. Scaled to an 8-room queue with a 2-min learned transit, the job ETA inflates by ~14 minutes over a perfectly on-schedule run.

title: A skipped room can never be resolved: it holds "current" for the rest of the run, adds its full estimate to every later room's ETA, and permanently blocks all_completed
impact: Concrete: queue Den(6 est) / Kitchen(10 est) / Hall(8 est); the robot skips Den and Kitchen completes with actual 10. Loop order: Den unresolved -> remaining_cursor 6, eta start+6; Kitchen completed -> actual_elapsed 10, eta start+10; Hall -> start 10+6 = 16, end 24, eta start+24 — 6 minutes later than the truth, for the whole rest of the run. next_room()/`current` point at Den, so get_next_room reports "Den, done at <past time>" while the robot is in Hall. rooms_remaining stays 2 and all_completed stays False, so the "All rooms complete / returning to dock" banner never fires for that job.

title: Completed-room slug matching is keyed on the literal string "none" — the documented slug fallback is dead, and a room with a null slug is marked complete before it is cleaned
impact: Concrete: 3-room queue where R2's stored slug is null. R1 completes with actual 9.0, so completed_by_slug = {"none": 9.0}. On the next reanchor R2 is not in completed_by_id, but its slug normalizes to "none" and hits the fallback: R2 is marked completed=True, progress_percent=100, remaining_minutes=0.0, actual_duration_minutes=9.0, and actual_elapsed jumps to 18. The card shows 2 of 3 rooms done, next_room() advances to R3, and R3's ETA is computed from an 18-minute elapsed that never happened — all while the robot has not yet entered R2.

title: The "exact vs allocated" quality flag is recorded and never used — job-average actuals are blended into the same drift mean, permanently capping affected rooms below HIGH confidence while the card promises they will get there
impact: Concrete: a 5-room job whose real per-room times are Bathroom 3 / Kitchen 15 / Living 20 / Hall 4 / Den 18 (60 min total) grades every room against actual_per_room = 12.0. Bathroom (estimated 3) records pct_error = |12-3|/3 = 3.00; Living (estimated 20) records 0.40. Every room lands at or above the 0.20 saturation threshold, so all five take the FULL -0.20 accuracy penalty forever, despite the estimates being correct. Bathroom's confidence ceiling becomes 0.55 base + 0.25 max sample bonus - 0.20 = 0.60 — it can never leave MEDIUM. Meanwhile _learning_velocity (258-273) computes runs_to_high purely from sample count and ignores penalties by construction, so after 10 runs the card reports runs_to_high = 0 while current_tier stays "medium": the "N more runs to a reliable estimate" promise silently never lands.

title: A non-dict `rooms` block crashes both accuracy readers — including estimate() on the event loop — while the sibling reader in the same subsystem explicitly tolerates it
impact: A hand-edited or older accuracy_stats.json with a list-shaped `rooms` block takes down the entire job-progress snapshot on every card refresh (no estimate, no timeline, no live banner) rather than degrading to zero drift, and every finalize's accuracy fold raises out of _finalize_claimed after the archive write has already happened.

title: An empty room_timing on a charge/wait/zone phase is read as "capture failed", so every stepped run with a break or a zone is stripped of its accurate per-room timings and learns an even split instead
impact: Using the flagship charge-break step (vac -> charge to X% -> mop) or queueing a saved zone alongside rooms silently downgrades that run's learning from exact per-room capture to an even time split, and contributes zero area. A Kitchen-only run afterwards is predicted at 22.5 min instead of 30 — the user sees a confident learned number that is 25% wrong, and the more they use stepped runs the worse the baselines get. Nothing surfaces that the run was not fully learned.

title: read_json turns a corrupt or unreadable file into None, and the trouble-rooms read-modify-write then overwrites the file with a one-job store — permanently destroying history that has no rebuilder by design
impact: A transient network-share hiccup, or one legacy-corrupt file predating the atomic-write fix, silently wipes the chronic-trouble-room history: rooms the card has been correctly flagging as repeatedly missed stop being flagged, and dozens of runs of evidence are gone with no error shown and no service that can rebuild them. The only symptom is the warning line in the log next to a finalize that looks successful.

title: A failed or absent read is cached as None for the life of the process, and load_*_stats has no bypass — so _reload_learning_stats_now's documented "guarantees the current on-disk stats" is false
impact: One unlucky read at startup makes the card report no learned data / cold-start estimates for the whole HA session, and the two escape hatches a maintainer would reach for (the "reload now" helper and the cache invalidator) both silently fail to re-read disk. Recovery requires an HA restart or a full stats rebuild.

title: ensure_dirs runs inside every path getter, so the caches that exist to keep the loop-bound estimate off disk still issue ~32 blocking filesystem syscalls per dashboard snapshot
impact: Sustained blocking filesystem I/O on the HA event loop whenever a card is open — measurable UI latency and HA's "Detected blocking call ... by custom integration 'eufy_vacuum'" warnings on a network-mounted config dir, despite a caching layer built and documented specifically to prevent it.

title: get_completed_job_path interpolates an unvalidated job_id into a filesystem path, giving exclude/restore_learning_job an arbitrary *.json overwrite primitive — the exact hole the sibling module already hardened
impact: An authenticated HA user or any automation/script/dashboard that can call eufy_vacuum.exclude_learning_job can overwrite or create JSON files anywhere the HA process can write, corrupting unrelated integration data; the service returns its normal success payload with the traversed path echoed in job_path.

title: get_paths derives the archive directory from the entity_id's object_id, so renaming the vacuum entity silently orphans all learned history and the predictor restarts from cold with no notice
impact: Renaming the vacuum entity throws away months of learned per-room timings, accuracy stats and trouble-room history from the user's point of view — estimates silently revert to cold-start guesses with no warning, no migration prompt and no hint that the data is sitting intact in a directory named after the old entity id.

title: write_json is rename-atomic but not durable — no fsync before os.replace, so a power loss can leave a zero-length learned file that read_json then reports as "no data"
impact: A power cut during a stats write can leave the learned file empty; on the next run the integration reports no learned history rather than an error, and the trouble-rooms accumulator then overwrites what remains (IO-2).

title: append_job_csv_row / append_room_csv_rows are dead, and each CSV header is a hand-copied literal duplicated between the dead append writer and the live rebuild writer
impact: None today (the append path never runs). Latent: a future schema column added to one copy of a header and not the other, or a re-enabled append writer, silently produces a misaligned exports CSV that a user opens in a spreadsheet and reads as fact.

title: The final room of EVERY non-completed run is recorded as "missed"; on a stranded run the documented retry automation re-dispatches the robot in an unbounded loop
impact: An unattended robot repeatedly leaves the dock to re-clean a room that is already clean, and each retry destroys the user's saved room selection (`set_rooms_enabled_subset` disables every other room on the map). Even without the automation, the card banner names an already-cleaned room as missed on every cancelled/interrupted run, and the one-click retry rewrites the user's selection to it.

title: clear_incomplete_run's docstring claim "(full clean)" is false — ANY completed run erases the missed-room record, and it is unrecoverable because completed_room_ids is never persisted in the job archive
impact: The user-facing "these rooms were missed" record — the only place the missed set exists — is silently and permanently destroyed by an unrelated later run, so rooms that were skipped are never retried and the user is never told.

title: trouble_rooms.json is keyed by raw room_id and scoped per-vacuum, so its counters silently reattach to the wrong physical room after a re-segment or on a second map — the one id-keyed store reconcile-migrate forgets
impact: A room that has never been missed is permanently badged "chronically missed, 67%" on its card tile, while the room that actually is missed shows clean — and there is no rebuild, service or UI action that can correct it (see STATE-5).

title: incomplete_run.json's missed_room_ids survive a re-segment and a map switch, and the card applies them to whatever map is active — wiping the user's selection and enabling the wrong rooms
impact: One click on a banner the user cannot dismiss durably (STATE-8) silently destroys their current room selection and arms the robot to clean rooms on the wrong floor / the wrong rooms after a re-segment.

title: trouble_rooms is a raw-counter store with no rebuilder, no clear service and a denominator that only advances when the room is queued — the "decays on its own" justification for excluding it from repair does not hold
impact: A permanent, unclearable "chronically missed" warning on a room tile, with the only remedy being manual deletion of trouble_rooms.json from the config share — which is exactly the repair path the design note declared unnecessary.

title: build_completed_job_payload's `queue` block prefers the LIVE queue over the job's own — a room switch flipped mid-run makes both the missed-rooms banner and trouble_rooms name a room that was never in the run
impact: The missed-rooms banner names a room that was never cleaned in that job — often as an unnamed "Room N" — and omits the room that actually was missed; the phantom room then accrues a permanent chronic-trouble badge.

title: load_live_snapshot performs 4 mkdir syscalls plus an open()/read() on the Home Assistant event loop at every cold finalize
impact: The event loop stalls for the duration of a network filesystem mkdir×4 + read at the moment a job finishes, delaying every other entity update in Home Assistant, and HA logs a blocking-call warning.

title: The live snapshot has no clear: last_job_snapshot.json and _live_snapshot_cache are never invalidated after a run, and the stale snapshot's job_id outranks the active job's — a failed snapshot save makes the next finalize overwrite the previous job's record
impact: A completed run's permanent history record is silently replaced by a later run's, corrupting the learning corpus that every duration/battery/water prediction is built from, with no error surfaced.

title: Dismissing the incomplete-run banner is client-only and no clear service is exposed, so the banner returns on every card load
impact: "Dismiss" does not dismiss — the missed-rooms alert reappears on every dashboard reload until the user either accepts the retry (which rewrites their room selection) or happens to complete another run.

title: exclude_learning_job / restore_learning_job report "stats rebuilt" but never rebuild the three incremental accumulators — the excluded run's poison stays in accuracy_stats, learned_zones and battery aggregates
impact: The user's one tool for removing a known-bad run is silently ~partial. Estimates for the affected rooms keep the poisoned confidence penalty and zone averages after the UI has told them the run was excluded and stats rebuilt. Recovery requires separately calling rebuild_learning_stats, which nothing documents or hints at.

title: finalize_learning_job fires eufy_vacuum_job_finished with a FABRICATED status "completed" when the finalize was rejected, and (no supports_response) tells the caller nothing
impact: Automations and the card's eufy_vacuum_job_finished subscription (src/controllers/learning-controller.js:75) receive a confident "completed" for a run that was cancelled or was never finalized by this call, with every identifying field null. A duplicate finalize produces a second job-finished announcement. Automations keyed on status == 'completed' (notify, run the next profile, mark the floor clean) fire on a failed run.

title: retry_missed_rooms permanently destroys the map's room-enable selection and persists it to disk even when the start was BLOCKED and nothing ran
impact: A failed automatic retry silently and permanently reduces the user's cleaning selection from 11 rooms to 2. The next scheduled or manual "Clean" cleans 2 rooms and reports success. On the SUCCESS path the same permanent reduction happens too — the retry redefines the map's selection rather than performing a one-shot run — and neither the docs nor the response say so.

title: record_estimate_accuracy's schema requires no keys at all; an entry missing map_id/slug writes a permanently unreadable durable record and returns a confident success payload
impact: An automation written against the service (which the docs encourage: 03-services.md:1287 "Records estimated-vs-actual minutes per room after a job completes, feeding the estimator's accuracy tracking") but missing map_id gets a success response with a real-looking mean_abs_pct_error_after, while the estimator's accuracy tracking is never affected and the durable store accumulates junk keys.

title: record_estimate_accuracy writes accuracy_stats to disk but never invalidates the manager's in-memory accuracy cache, so estimates keep serving the pre-write numbers
impact: A caller records real accuracy data, receives a success payload with the new mean, and the card's per-room estimates and confidence scores do not change. Looks like the learning system ignored the data; the user is likely to call the service repeatedly, compounding SVC-4-style accumulation.

title: rebuild_learning_stats blanks accuracy_stats before replaying it; any failure after the blank leaves the store empty and the service reports nothing at all
impact: A user-initiated "rebuild" can leave every room's accuracy history — the input to the confidence penalty on every estimate — wiped, while the UI shows the rebuild as having succeeded. Recoverable only by noticing the symptom and re-running the same service.

title: Five registered services are never unregistered, surviving integration unload as phantom entries that fail with an unhandled KeyError
impact: After removing or reloading the integration, five services (including the destructive discard_external_run) remain visible and callable in the HA service picker and Developer Tools, each failing with an opaque KeyError traceback instead of disappearing.

title: invalidate-then-preload is a no-op when a preload is already in flight, letting a stale in-flight load repopulate the cache with pre-rebuild data
impact: After an exclude, restore, or rebuild, the card can keep showing pre-rebuild estimates and confidence until some later event invalidates the cache — making a correct repair look like it did nothing.

title: Schemas mark map_id Required on three services the documentation marks optional, so an automation written from the docs fails validation
impact: An automation authored from the published service reference fails at call time with a schema error on three services, two of which the docs specifically position for manual/edge-case use ("historical corrections").

title: overwrite_theme WIPES the target theme's entire palette when the vacuum has no active theme — ok:True, persisted, no undo
impact: A single `eufy_vacuum.overwrite_theme` service call (documented service, callable from any automation/script/dev-tools) permanently empties a named, hand-authored theme. The service reports success, the card shows no error, and there is no undo or backup — the theme survives as a name with no palette.

title: overwrite_theme replaces the target with a copy of a DIFFERENT theme (the vacuum's active one), and silently repoints the vacuum at the target
impact: An automation or dev-tools call naming any theme other than the currently active one destroys that theme's palette, replacing it with a duplicate of the active theme, and moves the vacuum onto it. Reported as success; nothing in the response distinguishes 'saved your edits' from 'cloned A over B'.

title: delete_theme of a bundled/core theme is silently undone at the next HA restart — the seeder re-adds it
impact: A user who curates their preset grid by deleting bundled themes they will never use sees them all reappear after any HA restart or integration reload, with no error and no explanation. The action can never be completed, only repeated.

title: overwrite_theme can permanently replace a bundled theme's palette while preserving source:"core", so user content keeps claiming to be shipped
impact: The shipped Signal/High Contrast/Colorblind Safe palettes can be replaced by arbitrary user content that the gallery still labels and filters as a bundled 'core' theme, and the shipped version is unrecoverable except by the non-obvious delete-then-restart sequence. A user who exports and shares it ships their own palette under the bundled theme's name and provenance.

title: delete_theme nulls the active pointer but leaves the vacuum's dirty working draft orphaned; the next save writes a theme containing only the deltas
impact: After deleting the theme they were editing, the user still sees unsaved-edit state; clicking Save prompts for a name and creates a theme containing ONLY the handful of tokens they touched, silently dropping the entire base palette they believed they were editing. No error at any step.

title: rename_theme writes into the raw stored entry with no isinstance-dict guard, unlike set_theme_tags — a corrupt entry raises TypeError out of the service
impact: An unhandled TypeError surfaces from the rename_theme service instead of a clean ServiceValidationError, if storage is ever corrupted or hand-edited. Latent — no in-tree path writes a non-dict library entry.

title: set_theme_tags silently discards tags past 16 or longer than 32 chars and still returns ok:True
impact: A user adding a 17th vibe tag, or importing a theme whose tags are long, watches tags vanish after the round-trip with no explanation of the limit. Cosmetic; nothing else is lost.

title: rename_theme accepts a blank/whitespace name and silently stores "Untitled"; no duplicate-name check on rename or save_theme_as_new
impact: A rename with an accidentally blank value silently renames the theme to 'Untitled' rather than being rejected; repeated saves/renames can produce several identically named presets that the grid renders indistinguishably (src/renderers/theme.js:527 shows `theme.name || id`), leaving the user to guess which one to delete.

title: delete_theme clears active_theme_id but leaves the deleted theme's working draft and draft_dirty in place — the orphan draft bleeds over the card's default look forever and survives restart
impact: A user activates a theme, tweaks a dozen tokens in the editor, decides they do not want that theme and deletes it from the Themes grid (the card's confirm dialog says nothing about drafts, src/bindings/theme.js:1221). The card immediately drops to its default look — except for the dozen leftover tokens from the theme they just deleted, which keep overriding it on every browser and across every restart, with no theme selected to explain them. The footer's 'Discard' and 'Save as new' buttons stay enabled because they key off draft_dirty (src/renderers/theme.js:1042, 1120-1133) and the label flips to 'Save as new' because activeThemeId is null. If the user takes that offer, save_theme_as_new resolves against active_entry=None (manager.py:259) and writes a library theme containing ONLY those dozen orphan keys, ok:true, no warning. The only cure is pressing Discard, which nothing tells them to do.

title: set_active_theme destroys the working draft unconditionally with no confirmation, no undo and no same-id short-circuit — clicking the already-active preset tile silently wipes every unsaved edit
impact: A user spends time in the token editor tuning twenty colours and radii, switches to the Themes tab to compare against another preset — or just clicks the tile that is already highlighted as active, which looks like a no-op — and every unsaved edit is gone instantly. No confirmation, no toast, no undo, and the change is persisted (services.py:218 awaits async_save) so reopening the card or another browser will not bring it back. The presets grid is the default sub-tab (src/state/theme.js activeSubTab: 'presets'), so browsing themes is the normal way to reach this.

title: set_active_theme's global-default branch is the only mutator that returns without firing _notify_updated, leaving the theme sensor's default_theme_id attribute stale
impact: An automation or script that calls eufy_vacuum.set_active_theme with only theme_id (the documented 'set the global default' form, services.yaml:2086-2087) gets ok:true, but every theme-state sensor keeps reporting the previous default_theme_id in its attributes. Any template, automation condition or dashboard reading that attribute is wrong until an unrelated theme mutation happens to fire the callback, or HA restarts. The card masks it because it re-reads default_theme_id from the get_theme_library service rather than the sensor (src/state/theme.js:344), which is exactly why the gap has gone unnoticed.

title: _get_vacuum_theme creates per-vacuum draft state for ANY well-formed entity id, so update_working_draft / revert_draft / set_active_theme return ok:true for a vacuum that does not exist and persist a record nothing can reach
impact: A user writing a theme automation, or copying a call between two vacuums and mistyping the entity id, gets back {"ok": true, "draft_dirty": true} — a success response describing edits that landed nowhere. The card for the real vacuum shows no change and there is no error, no log line (manager.py contains only two _LOGGER/raise sites in 668 lines, both in _notify_updated's exception handler), so the natural conclusion is that theming is broken rather than that the id is wrong. Each distinct bad id leaves a permanent orphan block under data['theme']['vacuums'] that no sensor reads and no teardown path removes.

title: Every update_working_draft triggers an immediate full Store.async_save of the entire integration data dict, and the card fires it on `input` — once per keystroke in text and number token fields
impact: Typing a 25-character font stack into a theme token field issues 25 full-store writes back to back. On an HA Green / Raspberry Pi with SD or eMMC storage this is visible editor lag and real flash wear, and it scales with the size of the user's stored data rather than with the size of the edit. Nothing surfaces the cost — the edit works, it is just expensive every single time.

title: _import_scoped strips matching keys out of the working draft but never recomputes draft_dirty, so the draft can be left empty with the dirty flag stuck True
impact: After a scoped floor-texture import the card's footer keeps 'Discard' and 'Save changes' enabled (src/renderers/theme.js:1042, 1120-1133 gate purely on draft_dirty) with an empty draft behind them. The user sees a persistent 'you have unsaved changes' affordance with nothing to save; pressing Save writes the active theme back over itself unchanged, which is harmless but tells them nothing, and only that or Discard clears the flag.

title: _minimal_theme_mutation_response cannot express 'there is now no active theme' — a None active_theme_id is dropped from the payload rather than sent as null
impact: A card whose cached activeThemeId is stale — for example after another browser tab or an automation deleted the active theme — keeps showing that dead theme as selected through any number of draft updates or reverts, because every response quietly omits the correction. It self-heals only when the theme sensor's push lands (setBackendThemeState, src/state/theme.js:330, which does read null correctly), so the window is short; but the response contract itself has no way to say null, and DRAFT-1's post-delete state is exactly the case it cannot describe.

title: import_theme performs no key validation; the card applies every imported key as a real CSS declaration on the card host, so one imported theme file can render the card permanently blank
impact: A user uploads a community/shared theme JSON containing `"tokens": {"display": "none"}` (or position/visibility/opacity). Import succeeds with no error. When they activate it, the card element gets `display:none` inline and the whole card — including the theme editor they would use to switch back — disappears. Because the theme is now the persisted active theme, it re-applies on every page reload; the card never comes back. There is no in-card recovery: the user must go to Developer Tools and hand-call eufy_vacuum.set_active_theme or eufy_vacuum.delete_theme with an id they can no longer see. No error is shown at any point.

title: _import_scoped clears a floor namespace in all three buckets but only re-applies the buckets the payload happens to contain, silently destroying per-layer opacity settings while reporting success
impact: A user who has tuned their wood-floor layer opacities imports a colors-only 'oak palette' file — hand-authored, shared by another user, or exported by an older build from before the layer-opacity tokens shipped in v1.6.0. The card shows the danger-confirm listing 'wood', then toasts success. Their --evcc-floor-wood-depth-opacity / -grain-opacity / -seam-opacity values are gone from the stored theme, silently, with no undo, no backup and no log line. The floors visibly change in a way they did not ask for and they have no way to know which settings were destroyed.

title: A scoped import rewrites the ACTIVE library entry in place with no core/provenance check, permanently corrupting a bundled preloaded theme that the seeder will never repair
impact: The user's bundled 'Follow HA' (or any core) theme is permanently altered — its floor namespace now holds an imported palette. The Source facet still labels it `core`, so the card presents it as the shipped theme it no longer is. Every vacuum pointed at that theme inherits the change. There is no 'restore built-in theme' path: deleting it and restarting does re-seed it, but that also clears it from every vacuum's active_theme_id (manager.py:391-393) — a non-obvious, lossy workaround the UI never suggests.

title: set_active_theme with vacuum_entity_id=None returns without firing _notify_updated — the only mutation in the module that skips the callback fan-out, leaving default_theme_id stale in HA state
impact: A user (or automation) sets the global default theme. The change is persisted, but the sensor.<vacuum>_theme_state attribute default_theme_id keeps reporting the OLD value until some unrelated theme mutation happens to fire the callback. Anything reading HA state rather than calling the service — template sensors, automations, a second browser session, another dashboard's card instance — shows and acts on the wrong default with no error. The originating card self-corrects only because it separately re-calls get_theme_library afterwards, which masks the bug for the person who made the change.

title: Import name de-duplication appends '(imported)' at most once, so repeated imports of the same theme produce multiple indistinguishable library entries
impact: After importing the same theme file three or more times (a normal thing to do while iterating on a shared theme, or after a failed-looking import), the library lists two or more entries all named 'Ocean (imported)'. The card's summary list carries only id/theme_id/name (manager.py:241), so the user cannot tell them apart and has no reliable way to pick which one to delete or activate.

title: _clean_theme_tags coerces non-string items with str(), reachable only through the unvalidated import payload, and silently drops rather than truncates over-long and over-count tags
impact: An imported theme arrives with junk tags like `{'a': 1}` or `none` shown in the card's tag/filter UI, which the user then has to notice and clean up by hand. Separately, a theme legitimately tagged with a 40-character phrase or a 20-tag set loses those tags entirely on import or on set_theme_tags with no indication that anything was discarded — the mutation reports ok=True either way.

title: The _get_theme_library_entries docstring claims write-time normalization that does not exist — _normalize_theme_entry is called from two sites and both are read paths
impact: No direct user-visible symptom on its own — this is the enabling condition for PORT-1 and PORT-2. Its cost is that a maintainer reading this docstring reasonably concludes stored theme entries are already sanitised and adds the next writer without a validator, exactly as _import_scoped did. The comment is a claim, not a guard.

title: No mapping write service can tell "this map exists" from "this map does not" — every schema takes a free-form map_id and every handler mints the bucket, so an edit against a non-existent map is persisted to a phantom bucket and reported as saved
brands: Both, but the rename trigger is Roborock-specific (map_id = user-editable map NAME from the select entity state). Eufy's numeric map ids make the accidental rename case unlikely; the empty/sentinel map_id case affects both.
impact: Every geometry edit the user makes after a vendor-side map rename silently lands on a different bucket than the one holding their previous work, and the previous work becomes permanently unreachable — the write reports success, nothing warns, and no service can recover it. Common path (stable map name) is unaffected; the trigger is a map rename in the vendor app, a hand-written map_id, or a template that resolves to a sentinel.

title: `clean_times` has no upper bound, defended by a sibling comment claiming dispatch enforces the per-brand ceiling — dispatch clamps it only on the Roborock (`zone_coords: device_mm`) branch; the Eufy branch ships it verbatim
brands: Eufy (unclamped). Roborock is protected by the device_mm-branch clamp.
impact: A user who types a pass count above the device's ceiling on a Eufy gets a success toast and a {"cleaned": true} response while the device either silently ignores the pass count or rejects the whole zone_clean command and does not clean at all. Reachable from Developer Tools and from any automation; the card's own UI is the only thing keeping the value sane.

title: `_saved_zone_coord`'s docstring claims it "mirrors the hidden-regions sanitizer" but omits that sanitizer's degenerate-drop — a zone that can be saved but can NEVER be cleaned, with no service able to repair its geometry
brands: Both — the geometry layer is brand-independent; only the final dispatch conversion differs.
impact: A saved zone can enter storage in a state where every attempt to clean it fails with a generic error toast, and the user's only recourse is to delete and redraw it — the named zone is not repairable. The card's own converter (src/cards/zone-geometry.js:71-72, MIN_SIDE 0.01) drops these at draw time, so this bites only automations, Developer Tools calls, and any future card path that bypasses `rectToNormalized`.

title: services.yaml documents map_id as optional ("Leave blank to use the current active map") on 8 mapping services whose schemas make it `vol.Required`; the integration's shared resolver `resolved_call_data` is used 59 times elsewhere and zero times in this file
impact: Eight documented service calls fail with a raw voluptuous error when used exactly as their own UI documentation instructs, and the same field passed as an empty/sentinel string silently writes to the wrong bucket instead. The card is unaffected because activeMapId() always returns something — but that fallback is itself the literal "1", so on a vacuum whose active-map entity is unavailable the card's edits route to bucket "1" rather than failing.

title: `backdrop_source` is the only enum-shaped field in the file left as free-form `cv.string`, is absent from services.yaml, and a typo produces a custom layout that can never hold segments and cannot be repaired
impact: A hand-written create_custom_layout call with a near-miss value produces a layout that looks created, cannot be authored against, and cannot be fixed — only deleted. Not reachable from the card, which always sends the literal "live" (src/actions/map.js:510), and not reachable from the Developer Tools form, which does not offer the field.

title: 19 schemas (lines 115-301) are dead — defined once, referenced nowhere — and two of them are near-duplicate twins of LIVE schemas whose defaults would be rejected by the live validators
impact: No runtime impact today. The risk is maintenance: two of the dead schemas are indistinguishable at a glance from the live ones they shadow, and their defaults have already diverged from the live validators.

title: Authored custom segments grow ~1 working-pixel toward +X/+Y on every save, and the growth compounds without bound across save/reload cycles
brands: Both (custom layouts are brand-agnostic; Roborock declares segmenter_engine='noop_fallback' so the custom compose path is its ONLY segment source, making this its primary path)
impact: Every authored room polygon is stored 0.3% of the map larger than drawn from the very first save. `set_custom_segments` is REPLACE-ALL, so once the compose draft has been reloaded from storage (which happens on any map/layout switch or page reload - `maybeLoadComposeDraft`), a single Save re-inflates EVERY shape in the layout, not just the one the user touched. A user who edits their layout across a few sessions watches rooms drift down-right and start overlapping their neighbours, with no control that shrinks them back. This is the direct answer to 'does the edit survive a re-import' - it does not: it comes back bigger and offset each time. Common path, not an edge case.

title: `rasterize_primitives` returns the same `[]` for 'numpy/Pillow missing' as for 'degenerate shape', so set_custom_segments silently wipes the layout and reports saved:true
brands: Both (custom layouts are brand-agnostic; worst for Roborock, whose segmenter_engine is 'noop_fallback' so custom layouts are its only segment store)
impact: Destructive, silent, unrecoverable loss of an entire authored map layout on exactly the installs the CV-availability gate exists to protect. The card's comment 'Live/custom/manual paths don't need it' is a CLAIM and it is false - the no-CV authoring path hard-requires Pillow + numpy. Even with no prior data the user gets a silent dead-end (shapes drawn, saved:true, nothing appears), which is the precise failure mode the cv_available chip-hiding was added to prevent. Note scipy alone being absent does NOT trigger this (rasterize needs only PIL+numpy) even though it does hide the CV chip - so the card can be in 'CV hidden, custom path pushed' state while custom still works, which makes the broken combination harder to recognise.

title: `_apply_segment_adjustments` returns the PERSISTED segment dicts by reference, and its caller writes `room_id` into them - baking a cleared/moved room link permanently into .storage and breaking the documented 1:1 invariant
brands: Both (get_map_segments serves CV and custom scopes identically; on Roborock it bites in custom mode via the active layout's stores)
impact: src/state/map.js:1690-1698 `roomIdForSegment` reads `seg.room_id` from the backend payload and comments 'Backend payload is canonical when present' - so the stale value fully drives the card. After clearing a link the card still shows the segment linked; `segmentIdForRoom(3)` returns whichever stale segment comes first in list order rather than the actually-linked one; and the room-chip UI that 'disables rooms already taken by another shape' locks the room out. It survives an HA restart because it is written into .storage, and it cannot be undone through the UI - clearing the link is already a no-op. The documented 1:1 invariant is violated in the SERVED data while the underlying `segment_room_links` dict is still perfectly 1:1, so the bug is invisible from the storage the doc tells you to inspect. Secondary: every polygon is duplicated into storage as `polygon_pct` on every read.

title: `mask_to_polygon` keeps only the largest traced loop, so merging two non-touching shapes into one room silently discards every piece but the biggest
impact: A user merging a room with a detached alcove, a galley across a doorway, or a split L-shape whose two rects do not quite touch loses the smaller piece permanently. There is no error and no `skipped` signal. Because the card rebuilds its draft from the stored `polygon_pct` (src/state/map.js:1391-1402), the lost piece is not recoverable from the draft either - it is destroyed on the first save. Only the map overlay is affected (doc §4.3: polygons are never projected into vacuum space, so no wrong physical clean), which is why this is MEDIUM not HIGH.
