Common path (single shape, or an overlapping merge) is fine - only a non-touching merge bites, but when it does the loss is silent and permanent.

title: Stale `image_segment_adjustments` survive a CV re-analysis and are re-applied by segment_id to whatever polygon now carries that id - moving a room the user never edited
brands: Eufy only (adjust_map_segment writes against `image_segments`, populated only by the `eufy_cv_v1` engine; Roborock declares segmenter_engine='noop_fallback' at adapters/roborock/adapter.py:482 so it has no CV store to adjust)
impact: Silently wrong overlay geometry after a re-analysis, attributed to a manual edit the user never made on that room. Reversible only by calling `adjust_map_segment` with the exact inverse deltas (the values ARE surfaced in the adjust response, so a determined user can undo it) - which is why this is MEDIUM, not HIGH. The telling part: the project already KNOWS segment ids do not survive re-segmentation - docs/dev/03-data-model.md:156 says 'Re-running CV re-segments and forces a relink (accepted)' for segment_room_links - yet adjustments keyed by the same unstable id are silently retained. The comment at mapping_services.py:1181-1183 enumerates what survives re-analysis ('preserves the user's segment_room_links and companion_anchors - they're INDEPENDENT of the image-derived segments') and omits adjustments; that claim is false for adjustments, which reference vertex INDICES into the image-derived polygon.

title: `compactness` docstring claims 'Range 0-1; 1 = circle' - the attainable maximum is pi/4 and a circle scores LOWER than a square
brands: Neither at runtime (Eufy CV thresholds are empirically tuned); affects future adapter authors, which is exactly this module's advertised audience
impact: No runtime defect - segmentor.py's thresholds (e.g. `compactness < 0.08` for `fragmented_candidate`) were tuned empirically against the actual function. The harm is to the stated purpose of this module: its header calls it 'the recommended starting point when writing a new segmentor adapter' and points at docs/contributing/porting-guide.md. A new-brand adapter author who trusts 'Range 0-1; 1 = circle' will pick thresholds in the 0.8-1.0 band that are mathematically unreachable, and will reason backwards about round rooms scoring high.

title: `normalized_color_features`' luminance normalisation provably cancels out - the Rec.709 weights are dead arithmetic and tuning them changes nothing
brands: Neither at runtime (Eufy CV only, thresholds empirically tuned); affects future adapter authors
impact: No behavioural defect - the output is correct chromaticity and segmentor.py's hue clustering is tuned against it. The trap is for maintenance: the docstring says 'illumination-normalized chromaticity features' and the code visibly implements a weighted-luminance step, so anyone tuning those weights (a plausible move when porting to a brand whose app renders rooms in different hues - this module is the advertised porting starting point) will observe zero change and conclude the pipeline is broken elsewhere. It also costs an extra float32 division pass per pixel over the whole map image.

title: A malformed primitive is silently skipped mid-segment, so a partially-drawn room saves as a success with no signal in the response
impact: A card-side serialisation regression (a renamed field, a missing key on one shape type) degrades silently to a partial room rather than failing loudly, and the replace-all save makes the partial version canonical. `skipped` is designed to be the caller's failure signal but does not cover partial failure, so neither the card nor the service log can distinguish 'drew what you asked' from 'drew half of it'. Reachable only via a malformed payload, so LOW - but it is the mechanism that would make a future POLYGO-1/POLYGO-4-class regression invisible.

title: Re-analysis rebinds the user's room links and manual segment adjustments onto positionally-reassigned segment ids
brands: Both. Eufy (eufy_cv_v1) is where re-analysis actually reshuffles ids; Roborock inherits the same read-time enrichment for any image_segments it holds.
impact: The map overlay silently mislabels rooms after any re-analysis in which blob ordering shifts, and the mislabel is actuating, not cosmetic: tapping a segment polygon calls toggleRoomEnabled for the LINKED room (src/bindings/map.js:869-897 and 2135), so the user taps the polygon drawn over the kitchen and the integration enables the bedroom for the next clean — the vacuum then physically cleans a room the user did not point at. Manual geometry corrections are simultaneously re-applied to unrelated polygons. Nothing in the response marks a link or adjustment as stale, so there is no signal to relink and no way to tell which links are still valid.

title: A failed or unavailable segmenter run overwrites the good cached segmentation with an empty available:False envelope and persists it
brands: Both. Eufy via engine_exception / missing optional CV libs; Roborock and any adapter without a registered segmenter engine hits it on the very first analyze call via noop_fallback.
impact: All room polygons disappear from the map view (src/renderers/map.js:109 falls back to a placeholder when `!segmentsData.available`) and the cached segmentation is unrecoverable: the source PNG the segments were derived from was just overwritten at the same filename by the upload that triggered the analysis, so re-running analyze cannot reproduce the previous result. The user's `segment_room_links` and `image_segment_adjustments` survive as orphans and will be re-bound to whatever the next successful analysis produces (see IMAGE--1). The service returns the failure envelope, but the destruction has already been committed to .storage before the caller can react.

title: The analyze cache-hit gate tests truthiness, so a cached FAILURE envelope is served as a valid cache forever
impact: Analysis appears permanently broken with a stale, now-incorrect reason ('you're missing scipy') after the cause has been fixed. The card is immune today because both of its call sites hard-code force_reanalyze:true, so this bites service/automation callers and any future UI path that trusts the documented default.

title: Re-uploading a map image does not invalidate image_segments, so a default analyze returns the previous image's segments
impact: An automation or script that uploads a refreshed map export and analyzes it gets the previous map's room geometry back with a success-shaped response and no staleness signal. The card path is immune (it always passes force_reanalyze:true), so this is an edge case confined to service callers — but the invalidation belongs on the write side, and its absence is exactly why the card had to hard-code the flag.

title: Image filenames are built from an unsanitised free-form map_id, so one map's upload can silently overwrite another map's image
brands: Both; Roborock materially more exposed because get_active_map_id returns the user-authored map NAME verbatim.
impact: The user edits/uploads a backdrop for the map they named and it lands on a different map's file, with the storage records still claiming otherwise — a direct answer to 'does the edit land on the map it names?' being 'not guaranteed'. Requires an unfortunate but legal map name (a name ending in _dark/_light/_custom, or containing a path separator), so the common numeric-map_id Eufy path is unaffected; Roborock's name-as-map_id makes it reachable without any malicious intent.

title: delete_map_image calls itself the mirror of upload but has no layout_id/art_scope sibling and sweeps no back-references
impact: A layout survives its backdrop and becomes uneditable with a misleading reason ('no custom backdrop') while continuing to advertise one; get_map_segments silently substitutes the CV dark/default/light image metadata for the missing backdrop (1211-1217), so the layout's authored geometry is composed over a different picture than it was drawn on. Reachable only by a direct service call today (the card's variant list is dark/light/default only — src/renderers/map.js:76-80), which is why it rates MEDIUM rather than HIGH; the same asymmetry also means a per-layout backdrop or furnished-art PNG can never be removed through the card at all.

title: delete_map_image drops the storage record and reports deleted:True even when the file removal failed, and analyze's filesystem probe then re-uses the orphan
impact: The user is told a bad upload was removed, the UI agrees it is gone, and the segmenter keeps using it — the delete is neither honest nor effective. Also leaves an undeletable orphan: with no image_variants record, a second delete_map_image returns {"deleted": False, "reason": "not_found"} at 989 and never retries the unlink, so nothing in the integration can ever remove that file again. Requires the unlink to actually fail, which is uncommon on the usual Linux host, hence MEDIUM.

title: min_area_pixels silently overrides the adapter's configured tuning because absent is coerced to 1200 before the is-not-None check
brands: Both; any adapter that tunes min_area_pixels away from 1200.
impact: An adapter-level segmentation tuning knob that the adapter-config reference documents as configurable is silently inert for the omit-the-field case, so small rooms vanish from the segmentation with no diagnostic. Masked today because the only shipped adapter declares exactly 1200 — the bug is invisible until someone tunes it, which is precisely the forgotten-sibling shape (three knobs wired correctly, the fourth not, with a permissive default hiding it).

title: Upload persists width/height as None when Pillow is unavailable and still reports saved:True
brands: Both; depends on whether Pillow is importable on the host.
impact: On a Pillow-less install a successful upload is recorded in a state that makes custom-segment authoring report a missing backdrop, and the variant row displays null dimensions. Confined to installs without Pillow, and the recorded dims are the only casualty (the PNG itself is correct), hence LOW.

title: Layout existence is validated before the executor write and re-checked afterwards only by a silent isinstance guard, so a concurrent layout delete orphans the upload
impact: A leaked PNG plus a phantom image_variants entry, and an upload the user believes attached to their layout that attached to nothing. Requires two service calls to overlap across a single await, so it is rare in practice; the missing part is that the post-await re-check has no failure reason and the earlier validation is never re-honoured.

title: Four of the five services in this block have no services.yaml description, including the destructive delete_map_image
impact: No runtime behaviour change — this is documentation/UI surface only. The consequence is that the one destructive service in this area (delete_map_image, which removes a file from disk) is the least discoverable and least documented, and neither its two-tap card guard nor any field description reaches a user driving it from Developer Tools or an automation. Also a quality-scale gap (HA expects every registered service to have a description).

title: set_custom_segments is a REPLACE-ALL write that cannot name its target layout — it lands on whatever layout is active at call time, destroying another layout's authored geometry
brands: Both (Eufy + Roborock) — custom layouts are brand-independent map-bucket state.
impact: Silent, unrecoverable loss of hand-authored map geometry plus its room links. The layout the user was editing is left untouched and the one they were not looking at is destroyed; the service returns {'saved': True, 'segment_count': N} either way, so nothing surfaces. Requires either two clients or an in-flight layout switch — the single-client, single-tab path is fine.

title: In custom mode with no resolvable layout, _resolve_active_scope hands writers THROWAWAY dicts — set_companion_anchor / set_segment_room_link mutate a garbage-collected object and report saved: True
brands: Both (Eufy + Roborock). The card path additionally needs a live map source present (mss.present) for the dock-mascot fallback, which is the normal Eufy fork configuration.
impact: The mascot visibly stays where the user parked it for the rest of the session (the card never refetches after an anchor write) and silently snaps back on the next page load — repeatedly, with no error and no way for the user to tell the write failed. The same hole applies to set_segment_room_link for any script/automation caller. This is a result-returning API whose failure is not merely discarded but actively reported as success.

title: _backfill_saved_zone_area fails OPEN on an indeterminate active map and permanently persists area_m2 / room_number computed from the WRONG map's raster — the poisoned value never self-heals
brands: Eufy only — on Roborock async_get_map_data_dict returns None early (map_source_coordinator.py:683), so nothing is written.
impact: Permanently wrong zone size shown in the card, a zone filed under the wrong room in the browse list (grouped by room_number per docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md), and a wrong area feeding the learning/duration-estimate path — which this function's own docstring claims it exists to make reliable. Irreversible from the UI: nothing recomputes area_m2 once set, so the only repair is editing .storage by hand. The single-map household is unaffected (the loaded map IS the zone's map); it needs 2+ maps plus a blank active-map entity at read time.

title: _backfill_saved_zone_area overwrites a user's explicit 'Unassigned' filing — room_number=None means both 'never computed' and 'user chose Unassigned', and the read path cannot tell them apart
brands: Eufy only — zone_membership returns room_number=None on Roborock (no per-pixel raster), so the `membership.get('room_number') is not None` arm never fires there.
impact: A saved zone silently jumps out of the Unassigned section into a room section the user explicitly moved it out of. Filing only — docs are explicit that room_number never affects dispatch, so no wrong physical clean. Narrow: only bites zones that reached the user-editing stage while still unsized (i.e. authored off-active-map or with no map data). Once a zone has an area_m2 it is out of `pending` and immune.

title: _generate_saved_zone_id / _generate_custom_layout_id guarantee uniqueness only against LIVE ids, so an id is reused after a delete — and saved-zone ids are durably referenced by queue steps and run profiles
brands: Both — saved zones and queue zone steps exist for Eufy and Roborock alike.
impact: Wrong physical area cleaned by a saved queue step or run profile, with no warning — the failure class is the most serious in this subsystem, but the window is narrow (delete and create must land in the same wall-clock second). The far more common outcome of the same missing-reference-sweep is benign: the step silently cleans nothing. Layout ids reuse the same way but nothing durable outside the bucket keys off them (the migrated layout's backdrop variant is the literal 'custom', and per-layout variants are re-derived on upload), so the layout side is latent.

title: adjust_map_segment persists a map-level record keyed by a segment id that CV re-analysis recycles — a nudge authored for one room silently re-attaches to whichever segment inherits that id
brands: Eufy only in practice — image_segment_adjustments is written against the CV image_segments store, which only the Eufy CV segmentor populates.
impact: A displayed room outline is silently offset from its true position and falsely labelled as manually adjusted, and the correction the user made is lost from the room it belonged to. Display/linking only — segment polygons are not the dispatch geometry (room cleans go by room id, zone cleans by saved-zone geometry), so nothing physical goes wrong. Only bites installs that both use segment nudges and re-analyze after the map changed; a re-analyze that reproduces the same component order is harmless.

title: set_custom_segments' user-facing description is two features stale — it claims map-level scope and an uploaded-backdrop requirement that the layout + live-dims paths superseded
impact: Documentation precision only, but it is the load-bearing kind: the description is exactly what would have warned a caller about CUSTOM-1's implicit target, and it omits the two parameters that make the live-layout path usable. No runtime effect.

title: map_id is documented as optional + auto-resolving on 6 presentation services but is vol.Required; a literal blank map_id silently mints and writes a phantom map bucket
impact: The service reports success and the setting is permanently invisible — the classic silent-wrong-answer shape. It also leaves a ghost map in .storage that surfaces through get_vacuum_maps / diagnostics as an extra map with 0 rooms, and becomes a candidate for the `next(iter(vac_maps))` fallback in FURNIS-2. Blast radius is bounded: the card always sends a map_id (state/rooms.js activeMapId() falls back to "1" and can never return falsy), so only automation/script/Dev-Tools callers are affected. Branch (A) fails loudly and merely makes the published API wrong; branch (B) is the silent one. Fix is one line per handler (route through resolved_call_data, which already rejects the blank case correctly) — but see FURNIS-2 before copying its last-resort behaviour.

title: _handle_set_room_viewport is the only furnished writer with no clamp and a corner-valued default — zoom:0 and cx/cy:0.0 persist verbatim
impact: Latent today — say so plainly: docs/advanced/08-map-configuration.md line 270 records the per-room viewport as "service-only today, not yet a panel control", and the card reads no viewport (src/state/map.js: "Per-room art / sub-tabs / saved viewport are Wave 2 — NOT read or written here"), so nothing renders it yet. The cost is that unrenderable values are being accepted and persisted NOW, so a Wave-2 consumer inherits a store the two sibling writers were explicitly hardened against, and any automation-authored viewport is already silently mis-stored.

title: area_label_anchors are keyed by device room id and nothing prunes them on a room rebuild, so a re-import silently re-aims one room's dragged label onto a different room
impact: This is the direct answer to 'does the edit survive a re-import?': the bytes survive, their meaning does not, and nothing detects it. Cosmetic in consequence (a mis-placed m² chip, not a mis-cleaned room) but silently wrong and non-obvious — the user cannot tell that a chip is stale rather than mis-rendered. Reversible only by noticing and re-dragging (or calling the service with both pcts null). The same shape applies to the map-level `companion_anchors` and to each custom layout's furnished `rooms` map, which are keyed the same way and equally unpruned.

title: hidden_regions are stored as normalized rects with no record of the frame they were authored against, so a re-map re-aims the masks onto different physical areas — and masks hide content by default
brands: both — sharpest on Roborock, whose rendered image is trimmed to the occupied extent
impact: Map content silently disappears with no indication of why, on a map the user never edited — the mask looks like a rendering bug rather than stale state. Recovery exists but is undiscoverable unless the user remembers the Hide-area tool: toggling the hidden_regions overlay off reveals what is under, and edit mode exposes a per-rect delete. Not destructive (nothing else is overwritten) and not a dispatch risk (masks are display-only; cleaning is by room id).

title: Clearing a home-scope art placement setdefaults an empty home_art dict, flipping the 'no furnished data' sentinel from None to a confident empty payload
impact: No visible effect today: the card's clear button only renders when hasArt is true (src/renderers/map.js:1581), so the empty-home_art state is unreachable from the UI, and the current consumers key off art_url/render_mode rather than the payload's presence. It matters because `furnished_render is None` is the documented 'no furnished data' sentinel that a Wave-2 consumer is likely to branch on, and a no-op clear permanently falsifies it for that layout.

title: Saved-zone clean dispatches to the device when the active-map signal is blank — the "active map only" guard is permissive, not a refusal
brands: Both. Roborock is more exposed: map_id is the vendor map NAME read off a select entity that goes `unavailable` whenever the upstream integration reloads, and the wrong-map projection can land on a different FLOOR.
impact: The vacuum cleans a physically different area from the one the user named and tapped, with no error and no way to tell from the response (it returns {cleaned: true}). Requires the active-map entity to be blank (integration reload, cloud hiccup, HA restart window), so the common path is fine — but the failure is physical and silent, and an automation firing shortly after HA start sits exactly in that window.

title: delete_saved_zone performs no reference check; run-profile and queue `zone` steps keep the dead id and are silently dropped at run time while the UI still lists them
brands: Both — the zone step and its resolver are brand-agnostic.
impact: A saved run silently stops doing part of what the user built, and the UI keeps advertising the step that no longer runs. There is no warning at delete time and no reason code — the divergence is only discoverable by watching the robot. Non-edge: deleting a zone is a normal one-tap card action (docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §8 lists delete in the shipped Wave 3b UX).

title: The `map_version` re-map invalidation the design doc specifies as the zone's safety key does not exist anywhere in the codebase
impact: Every saved zone on a re-mapped floor silently points at the wrong physical spot, and the design's own stated defence against exactly this was never built. This is the direct failure of "survives a re-import": the edit does not survive, and nothing tells the user it stopped being valid. It is also irreversible from the UI — the only repair is delete + redraw every zone, and there is no signal telling the user which zones need it.

title: create_saved_zone files area_m2 + room_number from whatever raster is live when the active map is indeterminate, and that wrong value can never be corrected
brands: Eufy only — async_get_map_data_dict is the Eufy-only coordinator accessor (degrades to None elsewhere per docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md Wave 2), so on Roborock both fields simply stay None.
impact: A zone shows the wrong m² in the card list, is filed under a room from another map, and every ETA derived from it is wrong — permanently, with no UI path to fix the size. Needs the active-map signal blank at authoring time, so the common path is unaffected; the damage is that it is silent AND unrepairable rather than that it is likely.

title: create_custom_layout force-flips segmentation_mode to "custom" with no record of the prior mode; delete only restores "cv" when zero layouts remain, so create-then-delete strands the user on a layout they never chose
impact: Creating and then cancelling a layout silently changes what the map card renders — a different room-to-segment mapping, different mascot anchors, possibly a furnished art layer. Presentation-level only (room CLEAN dispatch keys off device room ids, not segmentation_mode — verified: the only non-mapping_services consumer of segmentation_mode is map_source.py:103), so it is not a wrong-clean, but it is a user-visible state change nobody asked for and it is not obviously reversible.

title: Every handler in the block mints a persisted map bucket for an unknown map_id — including on the pure not-found and read-only clean paths
brands: Both for the phantom-bucket mechanism. The rename trigger is Roborock-specific (map NAME as id); the Roborock select's state changing on an in-app rename is near-certain but is device behaviour I could not verify from source.
impact: All saved zones and custom layouts for a floor appear to vanish after a vendor-side map rename, with no error and no migration path — the data is intact in .storage under the old key but unreachable through any service. Separately, phantom maps accumulate in the map summary from typos or stale ids. Both are directly the "does the edit land on the map it names / survive a re-import" failure: the geometry is filed under a free-form, user-renameable key with no identity layer.

title: Both clean handlers ignore the zone's `kind`, so a zone saved with any non-"clean" kind is still dispatched as a clean
impact: Latent today: no UI produces a non-"clean" kind, so only a direct service call reaches this. It matters because the field is publicly accepted, publicly documented as extensible, and the failure mode when someone uses it is physical rather than an error. Either reject unknown kinds at the schema or gate dispatch on kind == "clean".

title: Zone size limits are not enforced at author time, contradicting the doc — an un-cleanable zone can be saved and only fails when the user taps clean
brands: Both (Eufy 0.5-10 m per side, Roborock 1 ft²-3.05 m²), per the caps quoted in the _handle_clean_saved_zones docstring at 2641-2642.
impact: A zone that can never be cleaned is savable and looks valid in the list. The failure is loud (an error toast) rather than silent, hence LOW — but it is discovered at the wrong moment, and in a batch it blocks the other zones too.

title: A raster containing ZERO rooms is published as present:True — decode's own room_ids signal is computed and discarded
impact: The card's `isVaRenderActive()` (src/state/map.js:1201) only tests `mapRenderData()?.present`, so the VA (▦) backdrop switches on over a completely blank canvas, replacing the live Roborock map image the user was looking at. Every pixel hit-test (`roomIdAtContentPct`, src/state/map.js:965) returns null because rid is 0 everywhere, so the auto-derived click targets vanish and rooms become unclickable; per-room colours and floor textures disappear with them. Nothing surfaces a reason — the card, and diagnostics' self_check 'map decoded' verdict, both read this as a successfully decoded map. Common path (a fully mapped device) is unaffected; this bites during a first/partial scan, after a map reset, or if the BFS locks onto a stale MapContent.

title: raster_room_bboxes runs an O(width*height) pure-Python per-pixel loop directly on the Home Assistant event loop
impact: Downloading diagnostics stalls the entire HA event loop — every integration, every automation trigger, the frontend websocket — for the duration of the scan. On x86 that is roughly 0.1-0.3 s for a mid-size map; on a Pi-class or NAS host with a large map it is comfortably into multiple seconds, long enough for HA's own loop-lag warnings and for a websocket-connected card to visibly freeze. It repeats once per configured Roborock vacuum in the same download. Not data loss, and only on a user-initiated diagnostics download — but it is the one path in this module with no cost bound at all.

title: `version` hashes the raster ONLY, while the payload also ships room_names — a room rename cannot invalidate a fetched render payload
brands: roborock (the identical raster-only version hash exists for eufy in map_source.eufy_version_of, out of scope here)
impact: Immediately after renaming a room, that room's custom fill colour and its floor-type material silently disappear from the rendered map and it reverts to the default palette fill — with no error and no way to tell why. It stays wrong until the user reloads the card or switches the active map. The card's own comment (src/bindings/map.js:326-330) states that the name bridge is the ONLY correct bridge ('Keying by room.id directly is WRONG — the raster rid and our stored room.id are DIFFERENT id spaces on real devices'), so there is no fallback path. This is squarely the 'does the edit survive?' question: the edit lands in storage but the map render keeps rendering against the pre-edit vocabulary. Note the Eufy sibling map_source.eufy_version_of:621-628 has the identical raster-only hash, so this is a shared contract, not a Roborock-only slip — but Roborock's is the one minted here.

title: ro_dx/ro_dy are hardcoded 0 and the decoded top/left are discarded — the payload cannot express any offset between the raw IMAGE-block frame and the parser's rendered frame
impact: IF the frames differ: the card draws the raster full-bleed at 0..1 while every overlay it composites on top — room bboxes, robot/dock anchors, no-go and no-mop quads, saved zones — comes from map_state_source in the parser frame, so overlays sit offset from the rooms they label; `roomIdAtContentPct` (src/state/map.js:931-966) names the wrong room for clicks near a boundary; and a zone drawn on the raster is converted to device mm through `correspondences_from_mapdata` (the PARSER frame) at dispatch/manager.py:154, so app_zoned_clean cleans a displaced rectangle — the robot physically cleans the wrong strip of floor. The round-trip refuse-gate cannot catch it: zone_dispatch.max_residual_mm validates the affine against parser-frame correspondences only, which are self-consistent, so the residual is ~0 and the dispatch proceeds. Discarding top/left removes the only data in the blob that could have detected or corrected the offset.

title: Two functions in this module read the same `flip_y` key with OPPOSITE defaults, so a decoded dict missing the key renders flipped but drift-checks unflipped
impact: Latent today: decode_roborock_v1_segments unconditionally sets flip_y True (line 126), so no shipped path produces a dict without the key. It bites the first time anything else builds a decoded dict — a b01/Qrevo decoder (the doc names b01 as the expected next format), a test fixture, or a future refactor that makes the flag conditional. The failure mode is maximally misleading: geometry_drift reports the exact 'inverted axis = a flip bug' signature that docs/dev/29 tells the maintainer to trust as evidence of a decode fault, when in fact the raster and the render agree and only the validator disagrees with itself.

title: geometry_drift reports max_center_delta: 0.0 when there are no common rooms — an optimistic accumulator that survives an empty loop
impact: Diagnostics-readability only. The drift block is the tool a maintainer reads to decide whether the Roborock decode is correct on a real device; 'max_center_delta: 0.0' next to 'aligned: false' invites reading the geometry as fine and the room-id sets as the sole problem. It compounds the already-reported A4-RB-5 (present: True regardless of verdict, map_source_runtime.py:427). No user-facing behaviour changes and nothing gates on the value.

title: The IMAGE-block dimension guard is `header_len >= 16`, but the four dims occupy the LAST 16 bytes of a header whose first 8 are the fixed type/len fields — anything under 24 reads dims out of the header's own metadata
impact: Not reachable on a well-formed v1 blob (roborock uses >= 24-byte IMAGE headers). It matters as the module's stated defence posture: the docstring at lines 14-16 says the byte walk is 'mirrored from vacuum-map-parser-roborock ... so a firmware format change is a one-file fix', and a firmware/format change is precisely the event that would present a short header. A `>= 24` guard would reject it as unparseable (returning None, which the caller degrades cleanly); `>= 16` accepts it and can emit a plausible-shaped raster built on coordinates read out of the header's own length fields. The other unchecked-offset risks in this walk are genuinely covered (see clean_areas) — this is the one gate that is looser than the format it guards.
